comments.text:
Second review of the uncommitted tree implementing .12, after the revisions to the first. No untracked files; all nine changes staged. The three prior findings on `unitName`, `staticArgs`, and the unfalsifiable `Groups` assertion are fixed and drop out.

## Intent

- `flake.nix:281` — `checks.units` is `pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest`, so building `nix flake check` needs `/dev/kvm`. AC 4 is "nix flake check remains hermetic and green"; .14 fixes its meaning ("stays no-node, no-VM, no-network") and the epic puts the VM test on hydraJobs. Unchanged from the first review, still your decision: `checks` or `hydraJobs`.
- `flake.nix:288`, `nix/unit-test.nix` — AC 3, "agent runs under it against a loopback endpoint". The VM boots `services.metsuke`; `contrib/metsuke.service` is only string-diffed against `contribUnit`. Its own `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/metsuke`, `[Install]`, and the signing-key-from-config path (no `LoadCredential`) are never executed. Fix: a fourth node installing the file verbatim with the binary at `/usr/local/bin/metsuke`, reusing `confined()` — or say in the close reason that shared `nix/unit.nix` plus the staleness gate is what meets it.
- Option-to-field correspondence is now complete: every `ServerConfig` field and nested limit is a declared option under its serde name, and the agent module covers every `Config` field bar the module-owned `signing_key`. The first review's main gap is closed.

## Correctness

- `nix/server-module.nix:104` — `environmentFile` defaults to null and `lib.optionalAttrs` drops `EnvironmentFile`, so an S3 archive with no environment file evaluates clean and dies at start on `Fatal::MissingCredentials` (`main.rs:261`). The description justifies the filesystem case only. Fix: `assertions = [{ assertion = !(cfg.settings.archive ? s3) || cfg.environmentFile != null; message = "..."; }]`, moving it to eval.
- `nix/unit.nix:40` — the shared table hands the agent `AF_UNIX`, which nothing in `crates/metsuke/src/` opens; the server needs it for the db-sync socket (ADR 0009). ADR 0007's decision is "No node socket, no journal access, no supplementary groups", and the missing groups are what currently keeps `node.socket` out of reach, not the family list. Fix: `addressFamilies` as a second argument of `hardening`, agent passing INET/INET6/NETLINK. Confirm in a VM run that dropping it does not break the agent — I did not test that.

## Reuse

- `flake.nix:185` — the `mkKeyValue`/`mkValueString` override is redundant: `generators.mkValueStringDefault` already renders bools as `true`/`false` and everything else via `toString`, and additionally aborts on a nested list where this silently `toString`s it. Verified: `custom hard == plain hard` evaluates `true` on `unit.hardening { stateDirectory = "metsuke"; }`. Fix: `directives = pkgs.lib.generators.toKeyValue { listsAsDuplicateKeys = true; };`, six lines to one.
- `nix/unit-test.nix:23` — `concatStringsSep "" (genList (_: "07") 32)` is `lib.strings.replicate 32 "07"`.

## Prose

- `nix/agent-module.nix:56-68` and `nix/server-module.nix:44-192` — ~35 lines of option `description` restate the Rust doc comments verbatim (`"Deadline for one S3 request."` = `S3Config::request_timeout_secs`; `"Cap on the compressed body."`, `"Ceiling the decompressor is allowed to inflate to."`, `"Uploads one pool may make per rate_limit_window_secs."`, `"Rows one listing may answer with."`, `"SNTP servers as host:port, tried in order."`, `"Clamp on the exponential backoff after 4xx rejections."`). Both `settings` descriptions already say the meaning is on the Rust field and then say it again anyway. Nothing diffs a Nix string against a Rust comment. Fix: descriptions become pointers to the field name; full prose stays only where the option is Nix's own (`package`, `signingKeyFile`, `environmentFile`, `restartSecs`, the `password_file` defaults).
- `nix/server-module.nix:25-26` and `:54-58` — the `put_retries`/ADR 0004 justification, twice here against `metsuke-server/src/config.rs:157-159` which owns it. Fix: cut both; `positive`'s absence at that one option is the signal.
- `nix/unit-test.nix:149` — "the twelve S3 fields it does not set" is eight (`bucket`, `region`, `endpoint`, `request_timeout_secs`, `signature_validity_secs`, `put_retries`, `put_retry_backoff_ms`, `list_max_pages`); nine with `kind`. Nothing checks the number. Fix: drop the count.
- `flake.nix:162`, `flake.nix:180`, `nix/agent-module.nix:11`, `nix/server-module.nix:13` — each opens with a sentence reading the code aloud before the sentence that carries the why. "The agent's own build, minus the native artifacts" is `removeAttrs agentArgs [ "cargoArtifacts" ]`; "Named once here and read twice below" is what a binding is. Fix: keep the second clause in each, cut the first.
- `contrib/config.example.toml:12-13` — the rewrite lost the instruction. "contrib/metsuke.service is where handing the key over as a systemd credential instead is written out" replaces text that told the operator what to do. Fix: "With systemd, leave this unset and pass the key as a credential — see contrib/metsuke.service."

## Gates run this session

- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{units,static-x86_64-linux,static-aarch64-linux,contrib-unit}` -> exit 0, all four outputs valid. The VM test, both linkage checks and the staleness diff are green on this KVM host.
- AC 1 checked independently of `linksNothing`: `file` reports the x86_64 output `static-pie linked` and the aarch64 output `statically linked`; `readelf --program-headers --dynamic | grep -Ec 'INTERP|NEEDED'` is 0 in both.
- `nix flake check` -> "all checks passed", but it printed `running 0 flake checks` because everything above was already in the store. That green proves nothing on its own, and on a machine without `/dev/kvm` it is what the first Intent finding predicts.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged and `br sync --status` reports in sync; this comment makes it dirty again, so `git add .beads/` before committing.
- .12 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment and no close reason.
- The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate.

## Filed

None. Every finding above is this diff's own work.

Not reported, checked and dropped: `types.path` on the three secret-file options (nixpkgs uses `types.path` for `passwordFile` throughout, so this is the convention, not a defect); `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS` overwriting an inherited value (the built drv env carries exactly `-C target-feature=+crt-static` and nothing else sets it) and the `pkgsStatic` alternative to it (cargo does not pass RUSTFLAGS to build scripts when `--target` is set, so the "leaks onto the host side" argument for switching does not hold); `linksNothing` passing on empty `readelf` output; giving the agent module its own `stateDirectory` binding (it would put `spool_path`'s digits in a second file, which the Rust default currently owns alone).

Verdict: not ready for /commit. Two decisions are yours — `checks.units` versus `hydraJobs`, and whether AC 3 wants the contrib file actually booted. The rest are small, and the prose block is the largest single edit.

comments.text:
Third review of the uncommitted tree implementing .12. No untracked files; all nine changes staged. Round 2's `checks.units` placement, the unexposed server limits, the `directives` override, `replicate`, the ADR 0004 double copy and the `contrib/config.example.toml` instruction are all fixed and drop out.

## Correctness

- `nix/agent-module.nix:76` vs `:109` — `spool_path` is a settable option while `StateDirectory` is fixed to `"metsuke"`, so any value outside `/var/lib/metsuke` renders a unit that cannot write it under `ProtectSystem=strict`: the option is offered, one value works, and the failure lands at start rather than eval. Same shape in `nix/server-module.nix` for `index_path` (`:125`) and `archive.filesystem.root`, where `hub` only ever sets a path under `${stateDirectory}`. Fix: one assertion per module, `spool_path == null || lib.hasPrefix "/var/lib/metsuke/" spool_path` and the server's two against its own state directory.

## Prose

- `nix/server-module.nix:120-123` — "No field there has a shipped default, so every one of them is set here or evaluation fails naming it" is false of three options in the submodule it introduces: `index_path` (`:127`), `calidus.password_file` (`:162`) and `developer.password_file` (`:179`) all carry Nix defaults, and `index_path` has no `#[serde(default)]` in `crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs:23`. Fix: "…bar the three systemd owns the paths of: `index_path` and the two `password_file`s."
- `nix/server-module.nix:43`, `:133`, `:142`, `:154`, `:173`, `:191` — six option `description`s restate the Rust doc comment the same option's `settings` pointer already routes to: `"Where accepted submissions go."` and `"The bucket production runs on (ADR 0005)."` against `config.rs:131`; `"As \`generate-allowlist\` emits them."` against `:178`; `"The db-sync registrations are read out of, and how long one resolution stands."` against `:87`; `"The one account that may pull the archive back out."` against `:116`; the `applications` paragraph against `:27-31` with "Absent" spelled "Null". Nothing diffs a Nix string against a Rust comment. Fix: delete all six; the `settings` pointer is the mechanism.
- `nix/server-module.nix:27-28` — "Every limit there is a NonZero bar put_retries, the one option that is not \`positive\`" reads its own types aloud; `config.rs:158-159` owns the why, and `put_retries`' `types.ints.unsigned` at `:150` is the signal. Fix: cut both lines.
- `nix/unit-test.nix:188` — "\`S3Archive::new\` reads the credentials" is wrong: `s3.rs:51` takes `credentials: Credentials` as a parameter, and `main.rs:261` is what reads the environment. Fix: name `main.rs`.
- `crates/metsuke/src/config.rs:37` — points at `nix/unit.nix` for the StateDirectory the default lives under, but `unit.nix` takes `stateDirectory` as a parameter and never names `metsuke`; `nix/agent-module.nix:109` does. Fix: name that file, or drop the pointer — `default_spool_path` (`:78`) owns the path.
- `flake.nix:199-206` — the generation why three times in eight lines: "So contrib/metsuke.service says exactly what a NixOS host runs under", "rather than written, because the confinement it demonstrates is the one nix/unit.nix already states", and the heredoc header that ships to the operator. The heredoc copy owns it; `checks.contrib-unit` diffs that one. Fix: cut the first sentence of each comment, keep `:200-202` — the `~`-inversion is the non-derivable half.
- `nix/unit-test.nix:265-268` — four lines for a `cp`, with a typo (`contrib/metsuke.service'`). Fix: "Copied into /run: /etc is read-only here, which is also why `[Install]` stays unexercised."

## Gates run this session

- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{static-x86_64-linux,static-aarch64-linux,contrib-unit} .#hydraJobs.units.x86_64-linux` -> exit 0, all four outputs valid. The 4-node VM test is green, `bare` included, so contrib/metsuke.service is executed and not only diffed.
- `nix flake check` -> "all checks passed", `running 0 flake checks` (everything cached). It no longer evaluates a `runNixOSTest`: `units` is on `hydraJobs`, so AC 4 holds on a host without `/dev/kvm`.
- AC 1 independently of `linksNothing`: `file` reports the x86_64 output `static-pie linked` and the aarch64 output `statically linked`; `readelf --program-headers --dynamic | grep -Ec 'INTERP|NEEDED'` is 0 in both.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged and `br sync --status` reports in sync; this comment makes it dirty again, so `git add .beads/` before committing.
- .12 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment and no close reason.
- The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate.

## Filed

None. Every finding above is this diff's own work.

Not reported, checked and dropped: `required` and the `restartSecs` option shape duplicated across the two modules (two callers, and `unit.nix` holding a `mkOption` shape buys nothing); the `hub`/`hubs3` nodes as scope creep past AC 3's agent-only wording (they are what shows the server module's rendered TOML loads, which is AC 2's other half, and the test header already says the travelling submission is .14's); `credentialPath` hand-writing `/run/credentials/<unit>.service/<name>` (no nixpkgs helper exists — every module in nixos/modules writes that string out); `linksNothing` and `taggedArchive` having no exported equivalent.

Verdict: ready for /commit once the two `settings`-description corrections land — `nix/server-module.nix:120-123` claims something the module contradicts three lines later, and `nix/unit-test.nix:188` names the wrong function. The rest are trims, and the `spool_path`/`StateDirectory` assertion is the one behavioural item, your call whether it belongs here or in .14.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Shipped: static musl outputs for both architectures (cross-built via crane, no interpreter or NEEDED in either), NixOS modules for agent and server with every config.rs field a declared option, contrib/metsuke.service generated from nix/unit.nix, and a 4-node VM test.

AC 3 is met by the bare node, which boots contrib/metsuke.service itself rather than the module's unit. Its [Install] section stays unexercised: systemctl enable writes under /etc, read-only on a NixOS node.

AC 4: the VM test is flake.hydraJobs.units, not a check, so nix flake check needs no /dev/kvm.

title: Three copies of poll-until-exit live in tests, none in support/mod.rs
description:
crates/metsuke/tests/binary.rs exited_within, crates/metsuke/tests/logsource.rs wait_until, and crates/metsuke-server/tests/binary.rs refuses_to_start each hand-roll the same deadline + try_wait/condition + sleep + kill-and-panic loop.
crates/metsuke/tests/support/mod.rs is the crate's stated home for shared helpers and already carries #![allow(dead_code)] for helpers only one target uses.
Fix: move exited_within into support/mod.rs and have logsource.rs's wait_until call it or be replaced by it. The server crate has its own tests/support, so leave that copy.
close_reason: Duplicate of metsuke-4zo.103, which already scopes moving copied agent test helpers into tests/support/mod.rs. Content moved there as a comment.

title: A binary test wanting a [log] section has to round-trip the config file
description:
write_config_for in crates/metsuke/tests/binary.rs already takes a signing_key_line for injecting an extra line, but no way to append a section, so binary_refuses_a_journalctl_that_cannot_read_the_journal writes the config, reads it back, string-appends [log], and rewrites it.
The section itself is written a third time: minimal_log_section in crates/metsuke/tests/config.rs, again at config.rs's journalctl_path test, and now in binary.rs.
Fix: give write_config_for an extra-sections parameter and lift minimal_log_section into tests/support/mod.rs, parameterised on the journalctl path.
close_reason: Duplicate of metsuke-4zo.103. Content moved there as a comment.

title: Two new journalctl-confirmation tests rest on timing that can flake
description:
From metsuke-4zo.116's confirm_following tests.

1. binary_refuses_a_journalctl_that_cannot_read_the_journal (tests/binary.rs) has the agent binary exec a stand-in written by sh_stand_in. That exec is outside spawning()'s ETXTBSY retry — support/mod.rs's own doc now says so. A sibling test forking in the write-fd window gives the agent StartError::Spawn, stderr then lacks '13', and the assertion fails as a product failure. Fix: retry the binary spawn on a stderr naming ExecutableFileBusy, or assert on NotFollowing's wording rather than the status digits.

2. a_journalctl_refused_the_journal_fails_the_start (tests/logsource.rs) needs sh -c 'exit 13' to fork, exec and exit inside TEST_START_GRACE (200ms). A loaded box that misses it makes confirm_following return Ok and the test panics as if the product were broken.

Both passed on every run so far; these are latent races, not current failures.

title: TLS terminator in front of the server, or no cross-host agent
description:
crates/metsuke/src/endpoint.rs refuses a plaintext upload_url unless it is loopback, and metsuke-server serves plain HTTP only. An agent on the node host therefore cannot reach a server on another host until something terminates TLS in front of it. nix/e2e-test.nix hides this by putting both on one host.

Playground deploy is blocked on this. Decide nginx+ACME on the server host vs the cluster ingress, then wire it.
acceptance_criteria: A playground agent uploads over https and the server records the submission in S3.
close_reason: cardano-playground terminates TLS for metsuke-leios with nginx and ACME on the server host (profile-metsuke-server.nix, commit 87988eb)

title: Tag client-v0.1.0 and server-v0.1.0
description:
No tags exist. ADR 0006 specifies client-vX.Y.Z and server-vX.Y.Z; docs/releasing.md adds fetch-vX.Y.Z and is the procedure. Tag the first of each, and write the CHANGELOG entries that replace the three Unreleased placeholders.

Acceptance Criteria:
Both tags exist and CHANGELOG.md has a dated entry under each.

The onboarding page reporting the tagged agent version is not an AC: build.rs reads the agent manifest at compile time and tests/version.rs pins CLIENT_VERSION to it, so a server built from the tagged commit cannot report another number. Whether the deploy happened belongs to metsuke-4zo.123.
acceptance_criteria: Both tags exist, CHANGELOG.md has a dated entry under each, the deployed server reports the tagged agent version on its onboarding page.

title: metsuke-server cannot use an EC2 instance role, only static keys
description:
cardano-playground has no aws_iam_user anywhere; AWS access on EC2 nodes is SSO and instance roles. main.rs:151 calls Credentials::from_env(), and rusty_s3 does no IMDS lookup, so an instance profile is unusable and the deploy needs a static key pair against repo convention.

Supersedes the framing in metsuke-4zo.50: the problem is not only that the secret is an env var, it is that env vars are the only source.

Reading credentials from IMDSv2 removes the static secret entirely.
acceptance_criteria: metsuke-server on an EC2 host with an instance profile and no AWS_* variables set reaches the bucket.

title: Verify metsuke's [log] source against cardano-parts' new tracing
description:
cardano-parts sets useLegacyTracing = mkDefault false (profile-cardano-node-group.nix:283), so the node forwards traces to cardano-tracer over a socket instead of writing them itself. ADR 0010 assumes the node journal carries the trace lines. profile-grafana-alloy.nix:350 tests for a PrometheusSimple backend rather than assuming one, which says the same about metrics.

Unknown whether the environments iohk-nix ships still keep a Stdout backend on the root entry. Until someone checks a real playground node, the trace feature is unpromised there.
acceptance_criteria: A journalctl read on a playground relay shows whether the node writes its own trace lines. Result recorded here, and docs/deploying.md says which log source works on a cardano-parts host.
close_reason: journald keeps the node's trace lines in machine format whether or not they are also forwarded to cardano-tracer, so ADR 0010's premise holds; playground runs the agent with log.journal_unit set against a real Leios node

title: The onboarding page is 908 lines of Rust for one HTML document
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/instructions.rs is 510 lines and its test is 398, for
one page. The markup lives inside a `format!` raw string, so every literal brace
is doubled and editing the most-read document in the project means editing a
Rust string.

Wanted: a dedicated web directory, HTML/CSS/JS, with a proper visual pass on the
page at the same time. devnet/cardano-signer already carries a bun2nix
toolchain if a build step is needed.

Two things must stay derived from code, and they are the reason the page is
served by the ingest binary rather than being a static site elsewhere:

- CLIENT_VERSION, which build.rs reads from the agent's manifest. Steps 6 and 10
  are the human form of the ADR-0006 nudge, and only the server that was built
  can say what it was built against.
- example_submission() and failure_reasons(), which build a real Envelope from
  the wire types and render Reason::ALL, so the page cannot show a shape the
  crate does not produce.

The rest is substitution: include_str! on the config example and the unit, a
port parsed back out of the config, the binary and config paths parsed back out
of the unit's ExecStart. All of it survives a move to a template.

The page renders once at startup (main.rs calls instructions::page() before
binding), so this is an authoring cost, not a runtime one. Whatever the page
gains, the ingest binary is the security-critical one and every byte it serves
is attack surface, so weigh JS against that.

title: metsuke-fetch reports no version anywhere
description:
The tool has no --version flag and prints no version line. A Developer hitting a bug cannot say which build they have, and nothing tells them their copy is behind.

Matters now that docs/releasing.md tags it fetch-vX.Y.Z: its compatibility surface is the cursor file --state names and the tree layout under --into, and a build that cannot read a cursor written by another needs to be able to name itself.

The agent and the server both log their version at startup; this one should too, and answer --version.
acceptance_criteria: metsuke-fetch --version prints the crate version, and a sync run names it in its output.
close_reason: metsuke-fetch answers --version and names its build on every run; --help and the usage text came along

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree.

## Intent conformance

- `crates/metsuke-fetch/src/main.rs:85` — the version line only reaches stderr on the success path. It sits after the `match command` block, so any `?` in `fetch()` (bad password file, `SyncError`) returns before it and the run names no build. The ticket's motivating case is "A Developer hitting a bug cannot say which build they have"; a run that hits a bug still doesn't say. `crates/metsuke/src/main.rs:88` and `crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs:178` both print theirs before doing any work, which is what "this one should too" points at. Fix: emit `metsuke-fetch {VERSION}` unconditionally at the top of `fetch()`, keep the summary line without the version, and cover it with a test that a failing run still names the build on stderr.

Silent failures, standards/smells, reuse, prose: no findings.

## Untracked files

None.

## In-scope fixes

The one above.

## Beads hygiene

- `br show metsuke-4zo.128`: no resolution comment, no close reason — still in_progress, the user's call.
- Map metsuke-4zo has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, nothing to graduate.
- `br sync --status`: in sync, 0 dirty.
- `git status --porcelain`: `.beads/issues.jsonl` staged alongside the code.

## Filed

Nothing.

## Gates run this session

`just test` — 418 passed, 0 ignored, 46 binaries in 5.81s. clippy/treefmt/audit/deny (`just check`) and the VM tests were not run.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — one in-scope fix (version on the failure path).

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
metsuke-fetch --version prints the crate version on stdout, exit 0. Every run names the build on stderr before anything that can fail, so a failed run names it too.

Past the ticket, at the user's call on release day: --help/-h answer the same way, both are read anywhere in the arguments, USAGE became a real help body (what each flag is for, a full example), and refusals print one line plus 'try metsuke-fetch --help' instead of the whole usage.

title: metsuke and metsuke-server answer neither --version nor --help
description:
metsuke-fetch/src/cli.rs has VERSION, USAGE, HELP_HINT and an Invocation enum; crates/metsuke/src/cli.rs and crates/metsuke-server/src/cli.rs have none of it. Neither binary answers --version, --help or -h, and their only usage text is a one-line parenthetical inside ArgsError::Unknown.

Both also name their build too late: metsuke's startup line sits after the spool opens and the key resolves, metsuke-server's sits inside serve() after config, credentials and the developer password. A start that fails reports no version at all, which is the run that most needs one.

Fix: give both the fetch shape, and move the build line ahead of anything that can fail.

Acceptance:
- metsuke --version and metsuke-server --version print the crate version on stdout, exit 0.
- --help and -h print a usage covering every flag on stdout, exit 0.
- A refusal points at --help instead of restating usage.
- A start that fails still names the build on stderr.
- Binary tests compare against env!(CARGO_PKG_VERSION) and the USAGE const, not copied strings.
close_reason: both binaries answer --version and --help, and name their build before anything that can fail

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
metsuke and metsuke-server now answer --version, --help and -h on stdout with exit 0, needing no config and no key. USAGE covers every flag, the verify-archive subcommand and the default config path. Refusals end in the help hint instead of an inline usage. Both binaries name their build on stderr before anything that can fail, so a failed start reports a version; the version left the later detail lines, which keeps the substrings unit-test.nix and e2e-test.nix grep for.

Help and version are scanned out of argv in main rather than modelled as an enum. metsuke-fetch still has its Invocation enum, so the three binaries do not parse alike.

title: Server SQLite backup timer
description:
## What to build

Recovery for the index between rebuilds: a systemd timer in the server NixOS module running roughly hourly — sqlite3 .backup, zstd, aws s3 cp into a backups/ prefix in the same bucket, using the server's existing scoped credentials. Complements (does not replace) the rebuild-from-listing path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Timer and service rendered by the server module; cadence is an option.
- [ ] Backup is a consistent snapshot (sqlite3 .backup, not a file copy), compressed, uploaded under backups/.
- [ ] Failure surfaces in the journal; it never blocks ingest.

## Blocked by

Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.
close_reason: Obsolete: server SQLite deleted by metsuke-jfb.5

title: a_connection_past_the_concurrency_cap_waits_for_a_slot flakes in a full-suite run
description:
crates/metsuke-server/tests/binary.rs. Failed once during a full --test binary run: 'the waiting connection was accepted rather than left in the backlog', left 2 right 1. Passed in isolation on the same tree and on every rerun of the full suite since, so it is timing under load, not a regression.

Same class as metsuke-4zo.118 but a different test and a different assertion.

title: NixOS VM end-to-end test
description:
## What to build

The one non-hermetic sanity gate (hydraJobs only, never in nix flake check): a NixOS VM test wiring a real idle Leios node (pinned via the ouroboros-leios prototype tag input, not capkgs), the real agent via its module, the real server via its module, and Garage as S3. Asserts the full path — scrape → spool → signed upload → verify → S3 object → ACK — once; moving values stay covered by tier-2 fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] VM test passes: an object appears in Garage and the agent logs the ACK.
- [ ] Runs from hydraJobs; excluded from nix flake check (which stays no-node, no-VM, no-network).
- [ ] Leios pin is a flake input, bumpable with the fixture re-record flow.

## Blocked by

S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index; Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.
close_reason: NixOS VM end-to-end test: hydraJobs.e2e in the devnet flake, plus hydraJobs.pool-id and checks.leios-pin guarding the pin

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .14 (NixOS VM end-to-end test). No untracked files; all six changed paths are staged except `.beads/issues.jsonl`.

## Correctness

- `nix/e2e-test.nix` (last subtest) — the comment "An empty archive verifies vacuously, so the count is the assertion" is false. `report_audit` (`crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs:255`) returns `Fatal::ArchiveEmpty` on `(0, 0, 0)`, so `e2e.succeed` already fails on an empty bucket. Fix: drop the comment and the `re.search`, or keep the count and say what it actually adds.

## Prose

- `nix/e2e-test.nix` `nodeConfig` — "Converted to JSON (cardano-node's YAML parser reads JSON) so plain jq can address the empty-string TraceOptions key" is verbatim from `scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh` (its own `yq -o=json` block), and `devnet/flake.nix`'s `devnet-setup` states the same why a third time. Same for "No peers": three phrasings of one fact. Fix: a pointer, once the shared derivation lands (metsuke-4zo.60).
- `nix/e2e-test.nix` header and comments say "upload" and "batch" where `CONTEXT.md` §Submission reads "_Avoid_: upload, batch, post, payload". `upload_url` / `rate_limit_uploads` / the `'batch acked'` grep are schema and log strings and stay. The prose is new writing with nothing forcing the old spelling.

## Design call, your decision

`nix/e2e-test.nix` `poolId` — the constant is correct (checked: blake2b-224 of `poolKeys/cold.vkey`, bech32). Its comment argues a stale constant fails the ACK subtest rather than passing quietly, which holds. Against: `cardano-cli` is already in `leiosPkgs`, so a `runCommand` deriving it from `cold.vkey` would be self-correcting on a leios bump instead of failing CI. My recommendation is derive it — the failure mode the comment defends is a red CI run someone then has to diagnose.

## Verified, not findings

- `flake.nix` `leios-pin` reading `inputs.cardano-node-leios.rev` does not make `nix flake check` fetch anything it did not already fetch: `lazy-trees` is not in this Nix's `experimental-features`, so all locked inputs are realized during lock resolution regardless of use. The asymmetry with the devnet side's `importJSON` is style only.
- `devnet/flake.nix`'s `metsuke.url = "path:.."` evaluates with the devnet's gitignored `.devnet/node.socket` present (`nix eval --no-eval-cache .#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux.drvPath` succeeds).
- Both `wait_until_succeeds` greps are on specific log strings with `-q` on the final stage; neither passes vacuously.

## Gates run this session

- `nix flake check` — all checks passed (`running 0 flake checks`: every output already in the store).
- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.leios-pin` — built; both locks read `3534e7065419c906b35d3be7c976aeace8cf2085`.
- `nix eval .#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux.drvPath` (from `devnet/`) — evaluates.
- **The VM test itself was not run.** Acceptance criterion 1 ("an object appears in Garage and the agent logs the ACK") is unverified by this review; it needs `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` on a `/dev/kvm` host.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is unstaged (` M`) and now carries this round's filings; `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code.
- .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason — pre-commit, your call.
- The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate. No `## Out of scope` line needed: nothing here crossed one.

Filed metsuke-4zo.86; commented on metsuke-4zo.60.

metsuke-4zo.87 (`needs-decision`) — `hydraJobs.e2e` is defined only in `devnet/flake.nix` and the repo carries no jobset config, so "runs from hydraJobs" holds only if CI is pointed at `devnet/` as a second flake. Jobset entry, or root re-export?

Verdict: not ready for /commit — one wrong comment-plus-assertion to fix, the prose trims, and the unrun VM test, which is the ticket's first acceptance criterion.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. All three round-1 fixes landed and are correct in substance; the prose axis is now clean (pointer to `scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh` resolves and does state the why for all three things it is cited for). Three findings, one design call, one proposed fix refuted.

## In-scope

- `crates/metsuke/tests/fixtures/README.md:6-10` — the re-record flow still reads "Re-record on every bump of the `cardano-node-leios` input in flake.nix". After this diff a bump also has to move `devnet/flake.lock` (or the new `leios-pin` check goes red) and re-check `poolId` (or the new first subtest goes red). This is acceptance criterion 3 — "Leios pin is a flake input, bumpable with the fixture re-record flow" — and the flow is now understated by two steps. Fix: name both in that bullet.
- `nix/e2e-test.nix`, first subtest — `assert derived == "${poolId}", derived` prints only what `cardano-cli` produced, never what it was compared against. The subtest exists to name a mismatch immediately, and its own failure message withholds half of it. Fix: `f"cardano-cli derived {derived}, expected ${poolId}"`.
- `nix/e2e-test.nix`, ACK subtest — `mc alias set` has no `--region` flag, so `mc` signs with `us-east-1` while Garage serves `garage`. From the run log: `Response: error 400 Bad Request, Authorization header malformed, unexpected scope: 20260825/us-east-1/s3/aws4_request`. The listing only comes back because `mc` re-signs after that error. The `region` binding's own comment says "the server signs against it, so the two have to be the same word" — `mc` is a third party that also has to and does not, and nothing here would notice if that retry went away. Fix: write the region into the alias config after `mc alias set`, or drop `mc` and assert the key prefix from something already region-correct.

## Design call, your decision

Two axes independently proposed moving the pool-id check from a guest subtest to a build-time `pkgs.runCommand`, shaped like `leios-pin`. Your IFD objection does not reach this shape: the derivation would compare `cardano-cli`'s output against the recorded constant and exit non-zero, never feeding a derived value back into evaluation, so nothing is imported from a derivation and `allow-import-from-derivation` stays irrelevant. Your second argument — that a recorded constant makes a changed `pool1` show up as a diff — is untouched either way, because the constant stays recorded under both. What changes is that the check runs without `/dev/kvm`, on any host, before a 4 GB VM boots, and stops the `cardano-cli` closure being installed in the guest for one string comparison. My recommendation is to move it. Keeping it is defensible: it is one subtest, it costs 9s, and it sits where a reader of the test finds it.

## Refuted, not a finding

Restoring an object-count assertion to the last subtest. The regex round 1 removed was `int(...) > 0`, not an exact count, so it never distinguished one stored object from several and adds nothing `succeed` does not already give. An exact count would be worse than nothing: in the run I inspected, `upload_interval_secs = 5` produced two PUTs and three `batch acked` lines before the units stopped, so the number of objects at verify time is a race.

## Gates run this session, on the working tree

- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → `/nix/store/q32lhl57hqjlyvm1fg7awg2301lkcsvy-vm-test-run-metsuke-e2e`. Read the log rather than trusting the exit code: all six subtests green, `metsuke[910]: batch acked` at t=19.6s, `v1/<poolId>/…json.zst` listed, `verify-archive` GETting the stored object. **Acceptance criterion 1 is met and is no longer unverified in this review.**
- `nix flake check` → all checks passed.
- Verified, not taken on report: `cardano-cli latest stake-pool id --output-bech32` exists in the pinned cli (11.1.0.0, `--output-bech32` is the default spelling), `cardano-cli` is on the guest PATH via `environment.systemPackages`, and its output matches the recorded constant exactly.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is still unstaged (` M`) and carries round 1's filings and both review comments — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason, which is yours to set. metsuke-4zo.86 and metsuke-4zo.87 stay as filed; .87 is still unanswered and your read (a second jobset entry for `devnet/`, not a root re-export) is not yet recorded on it.

Round-2 filings: none. All three findings above are this diff's own work.

Verdict: ready for /commit once the three in-scope items land. None changes behaviour, the VM test passes, and every gate is green.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 3. All three round-2 fixes landed and are correct; the `awscli2` swap is real (this round's log has zero `Authorization header malformed` lines and one clean `list-objects-v2`, against one 400-and-re-sign before). One blocking regression, one prose trim, two proposed findings refuted.

## Blocking

- `devnet/flake.nix` `flake.hydraJobs` — `nix flake check` in `devnet/` goes from exit 0 to exit 1. Nix evaluates every flake output with IFD enabled except `hydraJobs`, and reaching `cardano-node` through haskell.nix needs it: `error: cannot build '…-cardano-node-plan-to-nix-pkgs.drv^out' during evaluation because the option 'allow-import-from-derivation' is disabled`. Measured both sides in this session: a detached worktree at HEAD (`90cff82`, no `hydraJobs` in `devnet/flake.nix`) gives `all checks passed`, exit 0; the working tree fails while checking `hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux`. The root flake is unaffected — `hydraJobs.units` reaches only nixpkgs. This is acceptance criterion 2, "excluded from `nix flake check` (which stays no-node, no-VM, no-network)": true of the root flake, and this diff makes it false of the devnet one. Options: expose the pair under `flake.legacyPackages.<system>`, which `nix flake check` does not force, and point the jobset there; or keep `hydraJobs` and state in `devnet/flake.nix` that its own flake check is expected red. The first keeps a green gate and is my recommendation; the second is cheaper but leaves a red gate in the repo, which is the thing that trains people to stop reading gates. It interacts with metsuke-4zo.87 — whatever CI is pointed at has to find the jobs — but it is a separate problem: .87 is jobset wiring, this is a gate that now fails.

## In-scope

- `nix/e2e-test.nix`, listing subtest — the comment about `mc` ("asks the bucket for its location, takes the 400 …, and re-signs — so it would list this bucket whether or not the region matched") narrates a tool that is no longer in this file, which is journey rather than why. It is also wrong about the contrast it draws: botocore performs the same redirect, retrying on `AuthorizationHeaderMalformed` when the error body carries a `Region` element, and Garage emits one — so `aws` would also list this bucket with a mismatched region. The comment claims coverage the assertion does not have. Fix: cut it. `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=${region}` next to the `region` binding needs no defence.

Optional, three words: the README's `` `checks.leios-pin` `` sits unqualified beside `` `hydraJobs.pool-id`, in the devnet flake ``. The parenthetical is correctly scoped to `pool-id` and `leios-pin` is in the root flake, so nothing is false — but the asymmetry invites the misread. "(`checks.leios-pin`, in the root flake)" closes it.

## Refuted, not findings

- `keyPrefix = "v1/"` as an unguarded Nix-side copy of `KEY_PREFIX` (`crates/metsuke-server/src/archive.rs:55`). Drift is caught, loudly: the listing is filtered by `--prefix ${keyPrefix}` and asserted to contain `${keyPrefix}${poolId}/`, so a `KEY_PREFIX` that moved in Rust alone puts the objects somewhere the filter does not reach and the assert fires. The comment is a pointer to the owner, not a second unchecked home, and needs no `runCommand`.
- Divergent Change in one file yielding two derivations with disjoint parameters. Splitting `poolIdRecorded` out would duplicate `devnetSrc`/`poolKeys`/`poolId` or make a second file import this one for three bindings. The header states the reason. Leave it.

## Verified, not taken on report

- `nix eval devnet#hydraJobs --apply attrNames` gives both `e2e` and `pool-id`, each with `x86_64-linux`: the `genAttrs`/`mapAttrs` shape is right and one jobset entry reaches both.
- `aws s3api … --query 'Contents[].Key' --output text` on a zero-match prefix prints `None` and exits 0, so `succeed` passes — but the assert still fires, with `None` as its message. Not a vacuous pass.
- `derived=$(cardano-cli …)` in `poolIdRecorded` is an assignment, not an argument-list substitution, so stdenv's `set -e` does see a `cardano-cli` failure. This is the shape metsuke-4zo.55 was about, on the right side of it.
- Both README red-on-drift claims hold: `checks.leios-pin` compares the two locks' `leios` revs, `hydraJobs.pool-id` compares the recorded `poolId` against the pinned tag's keys.

## Gates run this session

- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.pool-id.x86_64-linux devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → both built. Read the e2e log rather than the exit code: five subtests green, `batch acked` at t=20.0s, the `list-objects-v2` call clean, `verify-archive` GETting the stored object.
- `nix flake check` in the repo root → all checks passed.
- `nix flake check` in `devnet/` → **exit 1**, per the blocking finding above.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is still unstaged (` M`) — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. Your read is recorded on metsuke-4zo.87 and it is correctly left open. metsuke-4zo.86 stays filed. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason, which is yours to set.

Round-3 filings: none. Both findings are this diff's own work.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — the devnet flake check regression is a gate this diff turns red, and the ticket's own second criterion is about exactly that.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 4. The `mc` comment is gone and both README qualifiers now resolve correctly. The flake-check regression is **not** fixed: your stated residual is right, and it is not a footnote — it is the finding.

## Blocking, carried from round 3

- `devnet/flake.nix:7` — `nixConfig.allow-import-from-derivation = true` is a no-op for anyone whose Nix does not already trust that setting, so `nix flake check` in `devnet/` still exits 1 off your machine. Measured this session with both `HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` pointed at a fresh directory, non-interactive:

  ```
  warning: ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting 'allow-import-from-derivation'.
  error: cannot build '…-cardano-node-plan-to-nix-pkgs.drv^out' during evaluation
         because the option 'allow-import-from-derivation' is disabled
  ```

  The rule, from `ConfigFile::apply` in libflake: a `nixConfig` key is applied if it is on a six-item whitelist (`bash-prompt*`, `flake-registry`, `commit-lock-file-summary`) — `allow-import-from-derivation` is not — else if `accept-flake-config = true`, else if `~/.local/share/nix/trusted-settings.json` holds that name and value, else it prompts, and a non-TTY prompt answers no. **`trusted-users` is never consulted on this path**, so being a trusted user does not help; on your machine it is the persisted `trusted-settings.json` entry doing the work, which is why the setting reads as unconditional from inside it.

  Your green measurement with and without `--accept-flake-config` is consistent with this and does not distinguish it: both runs read the same saved entry.

## What that leaves

The choice is now genuinely blocked on metsuke-4zo.87, because two of the three answers are CI-side. I have recorded this coupling there as a comment.

- **O1** — the pair under `flake.legacyPackages.<system>`, which `nix flake check` does not force, with a jobset that names the attribute. Green everywhere, no trust dependency. Costs the `hydraJobs` discovery convention, which is the objection you already raised and it stands.
- **O2** — keep `hydraJobs`, delete the `nixConfig`, and record in `devnet/flake.nix` that its own flake check is expected red. No trust dependency, honest, leaves a red gate.
- **O3** — keep both, and set `accept-flake-config = true` in the Hydra evaluator's own `nix.conf`. Keeps `hydraJobs` and every gate green, at the cost of a deployment-side fact this repo cannot assert.

My recommendation is **O3 if .87 resolves to a jobset you control**, since it is one line in the deployment and preserves the name the convention exists for; **O2 if it does not**, because a gate that is red for a stated reason is better than one that is green only where it was written. O1 remains available but pays the convention for a problem the other two solve.

Whichever you take, the `nixConfig` line as it stands is the one thing that should not survive unchanged: it currently makes the flake's evaluability depend on the reader's machine without saying so.

## Prose

- `devnet/flake.nix:4-6` — the comment presents the fix as unconditional. It states what `nix flake check` does and why IFD is needed, and never states the precondition that decides whether the line does anything. Fix falls out of the option chosen: under O3, say the evaluator must set `accept-flake-config`; under O2, the comment goes with the line.
- `devnet/flake.nix:5` — "`nix flake check` disables it by default" is Nix-internal behaviour with no version pin, sitting where nothing will report it stale. CLAUDE.md: a version pin claims the behaviour churns, so make it only when it does. Either pin it or state only the requirement and the error string.

Also, minor and falling out of the same decision: `nixConfig` is not scoped to `nix flake check`, so `nix build` and `nix develop` on `devnet/` prompt a first-time user too.

## Verified, not taken on report

- Root `nix flake check` → all checks passed; the root flake is genuinely untouched by the devnet `nixConfig`.
- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.pool-id.x86_64-linux devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → both built; the e2e log on the current derivation shows five subtests green and `batch acked` at t=19.2s. The `mc` comment is gone from the file.
- README: "(`checks.leios-pin`, in this flake)" resolves — the README sits in the root flake's tree and `leios-pin` is at `flake.nix:305` — and the sibling "(… in the devnet flake)" is correct for `pool-id`. The asymmetry is now the accurate one.
- `nixConfig`'s first sentence and the `inputs` comment below it state different facts (this flake needs IFD; haskell.nix is kept out of the root flake). Not a second copy.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` still unstaged — `git add .beads/` with the code. Comment added to metsuke-4zo.87 recording the trust coupling; it stays open and unanswered, and it now gates the choice above. metsuke-4zo.86 stays filed. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment.

Round-4 filings: none.

Verdict: not ready for /commit. One decision to make, and it is on .87.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 5. O3 is landed and works: both directions reproduce on a genuinely fresh trust store, and the "expected red" block is correctly gone. One clause of the new comment is false, measured.

## In-scope

- `devnet/flake.nix:6-7` — "an evaluator that already allows IFD never reads it" is wrong. Such an evaluator does read the line; acceptance and the evaluator's own IFD setting are independent gates. Measured on a fresh `HOME`/`XDG_DATA_HOME`, non-interactive, with `--option allow-import-from-derivation true` and no acceptance:

  ```
  warning: ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting 'allow-import-from-derivation'.
  all checks passed!
  ```

  The outcome half of the claim is right — the check passes, so the line is inert in effect — but the mechanism is not, and the observable consequence is that warning on every such evaluation, including Hydra's if its `nix.conf` allows IFD without setting `accept-flake-config`. Someone reading that warning in an evaluation log will go looking for a problem the comment told them could not exist.

  The clause is also the one O3 rests on, which is why it is worth correcting rather than cutting: what makes the setting inert on Hydra is that Hydra's own config already permits IFD, not that Hydra skips the line.

  Suggested wording, same length:

  ```
  # haskell.nix resolves cardano-node's plan by importing from a derivation, so
  # `nix flake check` — which refuses IFD — cannot evaluate the hydraJobs below
  # without this. Nix honours it only for a reader who has accepted this flake's
  # config; anyone else gets "ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting",
  # and then needs IFD allowed in their own nix.conf or the check fails.
  ```

## Verified this session

- Fresh `HOME`/`XDG_DATA_HOME`, non-interactive, no flag → `warning: ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting 'allow-import-from-derivation'` then `error: cannot build '…-cardano-node-plan-to-nix-pkgs.drv^out' … because the option 'allow-import-from-derivation' is disabled`.
- Same, with `--accept-flake-config` → both Hydra jobs checked, `all checks passed`.
- Same, with `--option allow-import-from-derivation true` and no acceptance → warning, then `all checks passed`. This is the third case the comment speaks to and the one it gets wrong.
- Both round-4 asks are met: the precondition is now stated rather than implied, and "which refuses IFD" is a statement about what `nix flake check` is for rather than an unpinned claim about a current default. It will not go stale the way "disables it by default" would have.
- The `nixConfig`, `inputs`, and `hydraJobs` comments state three different whys. Still not second copies.
- The deleted "expected red" block described a state that no longer exists; removing it was right.

## Gates run this session

- `nix flake check` in the repo root → all checks passed.
- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.pool-id.x86_64-linux devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → both built; the e2e log on the current derivation shows five subtests green and `batch acked` at t=19.2s.
- Devnet `nix flake check` in all three trust configurations above.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is still unstaged (` M`) and now carries five rounds of review comments and two filings — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code, or the record and the work part company. metsuke-4zo.87 holds the O3 answer and stays open on the jobset half, correctly scoped out of this ticket. metsuke-4zo.86 stays filed. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason.

Round-5 filings: none.

Verdict: ready for /commit once the one clause is corrected. Nothing about it changes behaviour, and every gate is green.

comments.text: Shipped: nix/e2e-test.nix, a single-machine NixOS VM test asserting scrape -> spool -> signed submission -> ACK -> object under v1/<poolId>/ -> verify-archive, on a real idle Leios node from the pinned proto-devnet config, the agent and server through their own modules, and Garage as S3.
