title: TLS-handshake test helper is copied verbatim into both crates' tests
description:
opening_bytes and TLS_HANDSHAKE_PREFIX exist twice, byte-identical except pub and the Duration path: crates/metsuke/tests/uploader.rs:117-140 (written by commit c316d03) and crates/metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs:198-226 (copied by metsuke-4zo.41). Both prove the same thing, that the peer sees 0x16 0x03 on an https endpoint.

Also in both copies: `.expect("peer connected but sent nothing")` names a cause for what is any Read error (reset, read timeout). A true empty read returns Ok(0) and never reaches that branch, so the message is wrong exactly when it fires.

Decision needed on where a cross-crate test-only helper lives. O1: a module in metsuke-wire, the metsuke-4zo.23 precedent, but wire is linked into both shipped binaries and this is dead code there. O2: a new publish=false crates/metsuke-testsupport, dev-dependency only, no shipped surface. O3: leave both copies; 25 lines, two crates, no third caller in sight. Recommendation: O2.
close_reason: two copies kept deliberately; the misleading expect message fixed in both

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Decided O3: both copies stay. A new workspace crate costs a manifest, a member entry, flake.nix crateSrc entries and another gate derivation to deduplicate 25 lines of test scaffolding with no third caller; the copies can also diverge, since the server's budget comes from its TIMEOUT const. Fixed the finding that mattered: .expect("peer connected but sent nothing") fired only on a reset or read timeout, never on an empty read, so it now reads "reading the peer's opening bytes" and lets the io error supply the cause.

title: Calidus registrations read from raw db-sync metadata are unwitnessed
description:
No `Directory` implementation ships, so `main` wires `ColdKey` and the Calidus
path is unreachable in production. Before writing one, decide where a
registration's authority comes from.

ADR 0003 says "resolved by SQL against the Leios db-sync (label 867)". Raw
`tx_metadata` is unvalidated: anyone who pays for a transaction can post a
label-867 payload whose scope names a victim pool and whose nonce is huge.
CIP-151 anchors a registration with a pool-cold-key witness over
blake2b-256(hex-CBOR(payload)); without checking it, resolving from
`tx_metadata` grants upload rights for any allowlisted pool to any bidder.

- O1: verify the witness in-server. Needs CBOR + blake2b-256 + Ed25519, and a
  COSE_Sign1 unwrap for hardware-wallet registrations, against ADR 0001's "no
  COSE, no CBOR in the runtime data path".
- O2 (recommended): resolve from a source that has already validated the
  witness — a pre-validated indexer view over the existing ureq, or a
  witness-validating view on the Leios db-sync. Keeps CBOR out and matches
  ADR 0001's "the server only reads its on-chain result". Amends ADR 0003.

Whichever lands also brings the `[calidus]` config section (source address plus
the refresh budget `CalidusKeys::new` takes as parameters today) and a recorded
fixture from the real source for the double in `tests/support`.
close_reason: Calidus registrations verified in-process against raw db-sync metadata

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Two more things for whichever option lands, both surfaced reviewing .8:

- `Registration { nonce, key }` has public fields and `Directory::registrations` promises nothing about a witness, so the unwitnessed-row hazard is representable. Make `Registration` constructible only from a witness-verified row (private fields, constructor taking the pool id and the witness) so no `Directory` impl can hand up an unchecked one.
- `calidus::current` collapses four chain states into `None`: nothing registered, contested highest nonce, all-zero revoke, and 32 bytes that are not a curve point. Contested and not-a-key are operator-actionable (an SPO must re-post), and indistinguishable from never-registered in logs. Return an enum or `Result` naming which, once there is a production `Directory` whose refusals reach a log.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Also gated on this ticket's answer: a cached resolution never re-resolves, so a CIP-151 revoke or a rotation away from a key someone else holds reaches a running server only through a restart (ADR 0003 Consequences records it). Whatever source is chosen brings the [calidus] section, and the section needs a re-resolve age charged against the same refresh budget alongside the source address and the refresh limit.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Decided (grilling session, 2026-08-24). ADR 8 records it; ADR 3 rewritten, ADR 1 clarified.

Neither O1 nor O2 as written. O2's "already validated" doesn't hold: nothing establishes
that a pre-validated view binds the witness key to the pool id in the payload scope, and O1's
cost was overstated: the workspace already
has bech32/blake2/ed25519-dalek, so a CBOR codec is the only new crate.

- Source: raw label-867 metadata from the Leios db-sync, read-only role, server colocated on
  leios1-dbsync-a-1 so the connection is loopback.
- Verification in-process, including blake2b-224(witness key) == scope pool id.
- `Directory` returns raw blobs; `Registration` is constructible only by the verifier, so no
  test double can fabricate authority.
- Resolution returns an enum naming never-registered / revoked / contested / not-a-key. Rows
  failing the witness check are dropped before that and never logged per pool.
- A registration counts only k blocks deep; k is read from the Shelley genesis (path is config),
  not hardcoded — devnet and testnet disagree on it.
- Plain TTL, chosen against k. `RateLimiter` for refreshes, `Resolution`, `Refreshed` and
  `Undecided::RefreshThrottled` all go.
- `[calidus]`: connection, dbname, role, password_file, query timeout, genesis path, TTL. No
  secrets in the environment (metsuke-4zo.50).
- Fixtures from a local devnet (`nix run github:input-output-hk/ouroboros-leios#dev-demo-proto-devnet`):
  the blobs for verification tests, one SQL round-trip for the query.
- Audit stays on ColdKey, reporting Calidus objects unverifiable, not failed (metsuke-4zo.49).

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree. Everything staged, nothing untracked.

## Intent

- `src/verify.rs:162` — "the refresh budget an audit spends against db-sync is one window's worth" names the budget this ticket deleted. Fix: say the resolution TTL, or drop the sentence.
- `docs/adr/0002-replay-protection-in-signed-payload.md:37` — "a ceiling per pool of one resolution plus that pool's refresh budget per window" describes a mechanism this diff removed. ADR 2 was not in the rewrite list, but this diff invalidated the line. Fix: amend to the TTL, pointing at ADR 8.
- `src/intake.rs:27` — `Rejection::UnauthorizedKey`'s Display embeds `{refusal}`, and `http.rs:227` puts the reason text in the 403 body, so any client claiming an allowlisted pool learns never-registered vs revoked vs contested vs not-a-key. The decision bullet said refusals reach a log; nothing asked for them to reach the client. Impact is small — those states are chain-public — but it is unasked. Fix: keep `refusal` in the `eprintln!` and return the bare text. Same family as metsuke-4zo.48, which holds the 5xx half.
- Audit half of the last decision bullet is not done: commented on metsuke-4zo.49 rather than restated here.

## Silent failures

- `src/dbsync.rs:96-99` — the justification for dropping a non-hex line is wrong. The column is `encode(tm.bytes, 'hex')`, produced server-side, so it is hex whatever a stranger put on chain; a non-hex line can only mean the CSV was mis-parsed or `psql` misbehaved. That is a tooling fault silently reported as "this pool has one fewer registration". Fix: `DirectoryError::Unavailable` for a line that is not hex, and cut the comment's chain-data reasoning.
- `src/dbsync.rs:151-154` — `securityParam` absent, present as the wrong JSON type, and present above `u32::MAX` all report as "has no securityParam". Fix: a second variant for present-but-not-coercible, naming the value.

## Duplication

- `src/dbsync.rs:46-84` and `src/applications.rs:140-168` — the psql invocation is typed twice: `env_clear`, `PGOPTIONS` `statement_timeout`, `--csv --no-psqlrc --quiet`, `--host <socket_dir>`, `--dbname`, `--username`, `--command`, and the same cannot-run / non-zero-exit / not-UTF-8 triple. The "Nothing is inherited: PGPASSWORD, PGSERVICE and PGDATABASE" comment is near-verbatim in both. Fix: one runner taking the socket/dbname/role/timeout, the extra env, the extra `--set` args and the query text.
- `src/dbsync.rs:106` and `tests/support/mod.rs:361` — variable-length hex decode written twice, with the same justifying sentence about `metsuke_wire::hex`, differing only in Option vs panic. Fix: one decoder in `metsuke_wire::hex`; the test helper `.expect()`s it.

## Prose

- The TTL-chosen-against-k why is in three places: `docs/adr/0008:41` owns it, `src/calidus.rs:96-97` and `src/config.rs:112` restate it. Fix: both code sites become a pointer.
- `src/registrations.sql:5-6` cites ADR 0008 and then retells its immutability-flag reasoning. Fix: keep only `Genesis rows have no block number and can never be that deep`.
- `1.35.0` appears in `docs/research/cip-0088-calidus.md:48` and `devnet/flake.nix:91`. CLAUDE.md: digits live in exactly one file. Fix: drop the version from the doc.
- `src/cip151.rs:19` — `/// Registration keys: version, payload, witnesses.` re-lists the three constants under it. Delete; the "numeric order CIP-151 fixes for hashing" comment below earns its place.

## Gates run this session

`nix flake check` — all checks passed. `cargo test --workspace` — 261 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` — silent. `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean.

## Verified, not taken on report

Dropping rows whose CIP-151 witness fails, unlogged, is specified and correctly implemented. `cip151::Registration` is constructible only through `verify`. `k` comes from `securityParam`, not a constant. `RateLimiter`, the old `Resolution`, `Refreshed` and `Undecided::RefreshThrottled` are gone from code and from prose. The resolution cache cannot grow unbounded: `intake.rs:101` refuses an unknown pool before the key check, so keys are allowlist-bounded. `ciborium` is the only new crate; `bech32`, `blake2`, `ed25519-dalek` and `PoolId`/`Signature`/`VerifyingKey` are reused. ADR 0001's CBOR ban is carved out by ADR 0008, not breached. `crafted/scope-mismatch.hex` is not a recording, but it is disclosed as such in its own directory with the README naming which real signature went where.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged with the code; it goes stale again from this comment, so `git add .beads/` before committing. This ticket is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason — pre-commit, your call. The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section. Fixtures are files in the repo, not pasted into issue bodies. `devnet/cardano-signer/bun.nix` in this tree is the bun2nix regeneration churn metsuke-4zo.66 already tracks, not a finding.

Filed metsuke-4zo.67; commented on metsuke-4zo.49.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — eleven in-scope fixes, of which `dbsync.rs:96-99` and `intake.rs:27` are the only behaviour changes.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review round 1 applied. Restating the audit half of the decision here, per the report:

Audit stays on ColdKey. `verify::audit` takes an `Authority`, and `main` hands it `ColdKey`: a Calidus-signed object is a `Undecided` that stops the audit rather than a finding, because a directory that cannot answer says nothing about the corpus. Making the audit resolve Calidus keys is metsuke-4zo.49.

Fixed: the two behaviour changes (a non-hex db-sync row is `Unavailable`, not a dropped row; a securityParam present but not a block count is its own variant), the 403 body no longer names which chain state refused the key (`IngestError::withheld` carries it to the log alone), the psql invocation is one `psql::Query` both chain reads run, variable-length hex decode is `metsuke_wire::hex::decode_bytes`, and the six prose duplications.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. All eleven round-1 fixes landed and are correct in substance; the three
behaviour ones verified at the code, not taken on report. Prose axis: no findings.

But the shipped Calidus path cannot run. One blocking finding, verified against a
real psql.

## Blocking

- `src/psql.rs:83` — `Query::run` sends the query with `--command`, which does not
  interpolate psql variables, so `registrations.sql`'s `:'scope'` and `:k` reach
  the server literally. psql exits nonzero, `PsqlError::Failed` becomes
  `DirectoryError::Unavailable`, and every Calidus upload 503s. Verified on psql
  17.10:
      $ psql --csv --no-psqlrc --quiet --tuples-only --set foo=bar --set k=42 \
          --command "select :'foo' as x, :k as y"
      ERROR:  syntax error at or near ":"
      $ echo "select :'foo' as x, :k as y" | psql <same flags> --file -
      bar,42
  Fix: send `self.text` on stdin with `--file -`. That also makes `variables`
  work for both callers, which is the second finding's fix too.
- `scripts/record-calidus-fixtures.sh:145` — the recorder runs the same query text
  with `-f "$query"`, which does interpolate. So the recording is honest about the
  SQL and silent about the invocation, and `support::fake_psql` prints its canned
  CSV whatever argv it is handed. That is why 264 tests are green over a path that
  cannot execute. The decision bullet asked for "one SQL round-trip for the query";
  half of it is recorded. Fix: assert the recorded argv is the argv `Query::run`
  builds, or drive the fixture through `Query::run`.

## Correctness

- `src/dbsync.rs:112` — `securityParam: 0` passes `as_u64().and_then(u32::try_from)`
  and becomes k=0, so `b.block_no + 0 <= MAX(block_no)` counts the tip and the
  depth wait ADR 0008 rests on is gone. CLAUDE.md: make bad values unrepresentable.
  Fix: parse to `NonZeroU32`, fold zero into `NotABlockCount`.
- `flake.nix:53-58` — `extraSources` matches `.hex` and `.csv` by suffix anywhere
  under `./.`, and `cleanSourceWith`'s filter is not gitignore-aware. A devnet run
  leaving either suffix under `devnet/.devnet` enters `src` and re-hashes every
  derivation, which is the hermeticity the map's success criteria names. Fix: union
  the fixtures directory as a fileset rather than a repo-wide suffix.

## Duplication

- `src/psql.rs:26-28` — `variables` is documented as "bound as psql variables rather
  than spliced into `text`, so every query stays fixed at compile time", but
  `applications.rs:138-141` splices with `.replace("{key}", ..)` and passes
  `variables: &[]`. Harmless today (both are compile-time constants), but the
  seam's stated invariant holds for neither caller: one splices, the other's
  variables never arrive. Fix, once `--file -` lands: bind `key`/`label` as
  `variables` and delete `Psql::query`.
- `scripts/record-calidus-fixtures.sh:109` — `reader()` hand-rolls
  `psql -h $socket -U metsuke_ro -d cexplorer`, which `scripts/devnet.sh:104-106`
  already exposes as `devnet.sh psql [args...]` over the same socket path. Fix:
  `reader() { "$repo/scripts/devnet.sh" psql -A -t "$@"; }`.

## Gates run this session

`nix flake check` — all checks passed. `cargo test --workspace` — 264 passed, 0
failed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` — silent.
`cargo fmt --all --check` — clean. All four green, and green over the broken path
above: the gates are not what is wrong here.

## Verified, not taken on report

Fix 1: `read_registrations` collects into `Result`, a non-hex row is
`Unavailable`, and no stranger can trigger it — `encode(tm.bytes,'hex')` is
server-side, so the column is hex whatever went on chain. Fix 2:
`NotABlockCount { found }` covers string, negative and above-u32, and `found`
renders the offending value. Fix 3: `Rejection::UnauthorizedKey`'s Display no
longer embeds `refusal`; `withheld()` returns `Some` only there and reaches only
`eprintln!`; `AuthError`/`VerifyError` still embed it but never reach a client.
Fix 4: `Command::new` appears exactly once in `crates/`, and `ChainError` kept its
CSV concern while `PsqlError` took the subprocess one — no context lost from any
message. Fix 5: `hex::decode_bytes` is the only variable-length decoder and
`hex::encode` the only encoder; `decode<N>`'s parity and exact-length checks both
survive, so the `try_into().expect` is sound. All six prose fixes landed with live
pointer targets and no new copy.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged with the code and goes stale again from this
comment — `git add .beads/` before committing. This ticket is still
`in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason: pre-commit, your call.
Fixtures are files in the repo, not pasted into issue bodies.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review round 2 applied.

- psql.rs: the query goes to psql on stdin with --file -, the only form that binds --set variables. Recorded the contract under tests/fixtures/psql (psql 17.10).
- The fixture gap that hid it: tests/support/fake-psql.sh is now one script in the repo that refuses --command as psql does and records the script it was piped, so the old invocation fails the suite. It also ends the write-then-exec ETXTBSY race that made the nix test check flake (a file this process wrote a moment ago races another test thread's fork). Per-test behaviour comes from answer.csv / failure beside the socket dir the config names.
- The recorder runs the query the same way (--file - on stdin) and reads through 'devnet.sh psql' rather than its own connection.
- security_parameter returns NonZeroU32; a securityParam of 0 is NotABlockCount, since k=0 counts the tip block and leaves no depth to wait.
- applications.rs binds the metadata key and label as psql variables; Psql::query and its .replace() splicing are gone.
- flake.nix matches the fixture suffixes under crates/ only, so a devnet run leaving .hex or .csv in the tree cannot re-hash every derivation.

Gates: nix flake check passed, cargo test --workspace 265/0, clippy --deny warnings silent, fmt clean.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 3. Both round-2 blockers are fixed: `--file -` interpolates, and the double
now refuses the old invocation. Every other round-2 item landed and is correct.

But the guard around the fix is one spelling deep. Six findings, all on the test
surface that was supposed to make round 2 impossible, and one on an error message.

## The guard is narrower than the regression it guards

- `tests/support/fake-psql.sh:28` — `[ "$argument" = --command ] || continue` is an
  exact-string match, and real psql accepts two other spellings. On psql 17.10:
      $ psql --csv --no-psqlrc --quiet --tuples-only -c "select 1"      -> 1
      $ psql --csv --no-psqlrc --quiet --tuples-only --command="select 2" -> 2
  Neither equals `--command`, so a regression to `-c` or `--command=` replays
  `answer.csv`, passes the suite, and 503s in production exactly as round 2 did.
  Fix: refuse any argument matching `-c*` or `--command*`.
- `tests/dbsync.rs:92` — `argv.lines().any(|line| line == "--file")` asserts the
  flag and never its value. `--file /path` is a valid psql invocation that
  interpolates (verified: `--file /tmp/q.sql` printed the bound variable), so a
  regression to a path passes the assertion while the server pipes to a psql that
  reads a file instead. Fix: assert the value is `-`, and have the double exit
  nonzero on a `--file` it cannot read.
- No test asserts `--tuples-only` anywhere (grepped `crates/metsuke-server/tests`;
  the only hits are inside the transcript). Dropping it makes real psql prepend a
  header row — verified: `select 7 as reg` without `--tuples-only` prints `reg`
  then `7` — which `read_registrations` would refuse as not hex, so every
  resolution would 503. The double replays `answer.csv` regardless. Fix: assert
  the flag per query, or have the double print a header when it is absent.
- `tests/applications.rs:350` asserts `key=musashinet_incentives_application_code`
  and nothing asserts `label=674`. Drop or misspell the `("label", ..)` binding at
  `src/applications.rs:129` and the suite stays green while real psql leaves
  `:label` literal in `WHERE tm.key = :label`. Fix: assert the label line too,
  as `tests/dbsync.rs:68` does for `k`.

## The recorded provenance is not checked by anything

- `tests/fixtures/psql/interpolation.txt` is read by no test and no script —
  `grep -rn interpolation` over the tree returns only the pointer comments. It is
  the sole committed evidence for why `--file -` is required, and it cannot
  drift-detect: a psql that changed either behaviour leaves every gate green. The
  enforced home is really `fake-psql.sh`'s refusal plus the two argv assertions.
  Fix: assert `fake-psql.sh`'s stderr against the transcript's `ERROR:` line, or
  reword the pointers to name the refusal as the home and the transcript as a
  dated note. Also: the note says five code sites point at it; there are four
  (`src/psql.rs:29`, `tests/applications.rs`, `tests/dbsync.rs`,
  `tests/support/fake-psql.sh:11`).
- `scripts/record-calidus-fixtures.sh:144-145` says "Run the way psql::Query runs
  it, down to --file -: an invocation that differs would record an answer the
  server cannot ask for." The invocation does differ: `reader()` at `:108` bakes
  in `-A -t`, so the recorder's argv is `-A -t --csv --no-psqlrc --quiet --set ...
  --file -` against the server's `--csv --no-psqlrc --quiet --tuples-only --set ...
  --file -`. Harmless today (`-t` is `--tuples-only`, `--csv` overrides `-A`), but
  the two flag lists are typed independently with nothing comparing them, and the
  comment asserts an equality no artifact holds. Fix: drop `-A -t` from `reader`
  and pass the server's flags at the one call site, or have the recorder ask the
  binary for the argv.

## Error message

- `src/psql.rs:117-122` — when the stdin write fails but psql exits zero, the
  return is `PsqlError::CannotRun`, whose text is "cannot run {psql}". psql ran and
  succeeded; the operator gets a spawn-failure message for a truncated query, and
  the stdout psql did produce is discarded. Fix: its own variant saying psql exited
  zero without reading the whole query. The ordering itself is right — psql's own
  stderr ahead of the broken pipe is the reachable case and it is handled
  correctly.

## Gates run this session

`nix flake check` — all checks passed. `cargo test --workspace` — 265 passed, 0
failed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` — silent.
`cargo fmt --all --check` — clean.

## Verified, not taken on report

The 264->265 move drops no coverage: the four removed tests are all
`RateLimiter` refresh-budget cases whose subject the decision deleted, and every
`current()` state (never-registered, revoked, contested, not-a-key) survives in
`tests/calidus.rs`. `security_parameter` returns `NonZeroU32` and reaches the SQL
only as a `--set` string, so zero cannot re-enter. `flake.nix`'s filter is scoped
to `crates/` with `.sh` added, and `fake-psql.sh` is committed 100755 — I ran
`nix flake check` and it passes, so the sandbox does get the double. The ETXTBSY
cause is genuinely gone: `make_executable` and `set_permissions` no longer appear
anywhere in `crates/`. A missing `answer.csv` is loud, not empty — the redirect
fails under `set -eu` and surfaces as `PsqlError::Failed`. No stdin deadlock:
`ChildStdin` drops at the end of the write statement, and both queries are small
fixed SQL, so the pipe cannot fill. `Psql::query` and all `.replace()` SQL
splicing are gone, `Command::new` still appears once in `crates/`, and the
recorder's only psql path is `devnet.sh psql`.

Bounded acknowledgment, not a finding to act on: `fake-psql.sh` is hand-authored
for everything except the `--command` refusal, so "test doubles are recordings"

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged with the code and goes stale again from this

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Shipped: the server resolves Calidus registrations itself.

- cip151::verify checks the CIP-151 witness in-process, including blake2b-224(witness key) == the scope pool id, and is the only constructor of Registration. Rows failing it are dropped, unlogged.
- dbsync::DbSync is the Directory: the shipped registrations.sql run through psql over a loopback socket, k blocks deep with k from the Shelley genesis (NonZeroU32).
- calidus::Resolution names never-registered / revoked / contested / not-a-key; the answer stands for a plain TTL chosen against k. RateLimiter, Refreshed and Undecided::RefreshThrottled are gone.
- [calidus] config: connection, dbname, role, password_file (PGPASSFILE, no secret in the environment), query timeout, genesis path, TTL.
- Fixtures recorded off a local Leios devnet by scripts/record-calidus-fixtures.sh; the psql invocation contract is recorded under tests/fixtures/psql.
- Audit stays on ColdKey (metsuke-4zo.49). ADR 0003 rewritten, ADR 0001 clarified, ADR 0008 added.

title: ADR 0003's refresh trigger and nonce tie-break do not match the code
description:
`docs/adr/0003-key-agnostic-verification.md` Decision says "On a signature-verify failure the server does one fresh lookup and retries before rejecting". `ColdKeyOrCalidus::speaks_for` (`crates/metsuke-server/src/authority.rs`) refreshes on an *authorization* mismatch, before any signature check. The code is right — ADR 0001 signs over the presented vkey, so a signature-verify failure says nothing about the registered key and a refresh could not help.

Same ADR says only "highest nonce wins"; `calidus::current` also refuses when two different keys share the highest nonce, a tie-break neither the ADR nor CIP-151 records.

Fix: amend ADR 0003's Decision to name the real trigger (a vkey the cached registration cannot explain) and the tie-break.
delete_reason: misfiled: findings about code metsuke-4zo.8 itself wrote, and the ADR text it outdated. Folded into .8 as in-scope fixes.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
ADR 0002 needs the same amendment, surfaced reviewing .8 round 2.

Its second invariant is "Cheap checks run before expensive ones", and its Consequences say "A signature check is the most an unknown sender can cost the server past the allowlist". `authenticate` runs the key check first, which for a Calidus pool is a db-sync query — so an unknown sender past the allowlist now costs a SQL round trip before any Ed25519 work. Bounded per window by the refresh budget, but no longer bounded by a signature check.

Amend ADR 0002's Consequences to name the Calidus lookup as the new ceiling, alongside this ticket's ADR 0003 edits.

title: verify.rs's catch-all AuthError arm mislabels oversized payloads and absorbs new variants
description:
`crates/metsuke-server/src/verify.rs`, the `authenticate` error mapping: after `UnauthorizedKey`, `BadSignature` and `Directory`, `other => VerifyError::MalformedPayload` catches `AuthError::OversizedPayload`, so an object that inflates past the ceiling is reported as "not a schema v1 envelope". An auditor chasing a decompression bomb or a mis-set ceiling reads it as corruption, and any variant added to `AuthError` later lands here instead of failing to compile.

Fix: match every `AuthError` variant explicitly and give `VerifyError` an `OversizedPayload { key, max }`.
delete_reason: misfiled: findings about code metsuke-4zo.8 itself wrote, and the ADR text it outdated. Folded into .8 as in-scope fixes.

title: A revoked Calidus key keeps verifying until the server restarts
description:
`ColdKeyOrCalidus::speaks_for` (crates/metsuke-server/src/authority.rs) returns true on a cache hit and never refreshes, and `CalidusKeys.resolved` has no expiry. So a CIP-151 all-zero revoke, or a rotation away from a stolen hot key, never reaches a running server: the compromised key uploads for the pool until the process restarts. `calidus::current` handles the revoke correctly; nothing carries that answer to a pool already cached.

ADR 0003's Consequences names rotation healing via refresh-on-fail. Revocation is the reverse direction and has no path at all.

- O1 (recommended): re-resolve a cache hit when its entry is older than a configured age, charged against the same refresh budget. Keeps zero-per-upload load, bounds a stolen key's life to that age.
- O2: document restart-only convergence as an accepted ADR 0003 consequence, and give the operator a command that drops the cache.
- O3: accept it silently. Unacceptable for a rewards program: a stolen key falsifies telemetry indefinitely.
delete_reason: misfiled: findings about code metsuke-4zo.8 itself wrote, and the ADR text it outdated. Folded into .8 as in-scope fixes.

title: 5xx bodies hand internal error text to any client that guesses an allowlisted pool id
description:
`http::refuse` (crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs) puts `error.to_string()` in the response body for every status, 5xx included. Behind `IngestError::Undecided` that is the directory's own reason string; behind `Archive` it is the S3 endpoint and bucket; behind `CounterState` the SQLite error. Pool ids are public, and the allowlist check is the only gate before those paths, so anyone can spoof one and read where the internal db-sync, bucket or database lives.

The reason text must keep reaching the log (that is what `refuse` exists for). Fix: send a fixed string for 5xx and log the detail.
close_reason: 5xx bodies now send a fixed string; status_for takes a Rejection

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
The .44 diff builds the mechanism this ticket asks for and applies it to one status only.

`http::refuse_withholding` now takes a `withheld` string appended to the log line
and never sent, and `IngestError::withheld()` feeds it — but only for
`Rejection::UnauthorizedKey`, a 403. The `_ => None` arm leaves `Undecided`,
`Archive` and `CounterState` sending `error.to_string()` as the body, which is
exactly what this ticket named.

The diff also widens what flows through it. `DirectoryError::Unavailable`'s
`reason` is now `PsqlError`'s text, so a 503 body can carry raw psql stderr:
Postgres `FATAL` lines, the role name, the socket path.

Fix is unchanged and now cheap: return `Some(reason)` from `withheld()` for the
5xx variants and give each a fixed public string.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree.

## Reuse

The same four lines, including the message string "the store's own error is the operator's to see, not the client's", already sit at :283 and :297. Fix: one helper beside `body()` (line 109) — `fn withholds(answer: &Answer, secret: &str)` asserting both the 503 and the absent substring — called from all three.

## Prose

- src/http.rs:290 and tests/http.rs:193 — "a pool id is public, so being on the allowlist is no reason to be told" is written twice. `unavailable`'s doc owns it: it is the function whose `signer` param exists for the log and not the body. Fix: the test comment points at it instead of restating.

No findings on intent conformance, silent failures, or standards. Every 5xx site in crates/metsuke-server/src (http.rs `listing`/`object`/`submit`, serve.rs's panic fallback) now sends a fixed body; the detail reaches the log through `refuse_withholding`.

Gate run this session: `just test` — 414 passed, 0 failed, 46 binaries. clippy/fmt/flake check not run.

Beads: .beads staged, `br sync --status` in sync, no drift. Map has no `## Decisions so far` section to graduate into. Ticket has no resolution comment or close reason yet.

Verdict: two in-scope fixes, both prose/test hygiene, no behaviour change.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. Both round-1 fixes landed: `withholds` at tests/http.rs:117 replaces the three verbatim assertion copies, and the submit test's comment points at `unavailable` instead of restating it. `cargo test -p metsuke-server --test http` — 23 passed, run this session.

Two new findings, both in the helper the round introduced.

## Unowned fact — the secret is untied from the fixture

tests/http.rs:55 is the only place "s3.example" is produced (`FailingArchive.reason`), but the three `withholds` calls (:210, :290, :299) each retype the literal as an argument. Rename the fixture's endpoint and all three still pass, asserting the absence of a string that was never in the body — a false green, which is the one failure mode this assertion exists to prevent.

Fix: one const both ends read, and drop the parameter.

    const UNREACHABLE_REASON: &str = "the bucket at s3.example is unreachable";

`unreachable_archive` sets `reason: UNREACHABLE_REASON`; `withholds(answer)` asserts the body does not contain it. The three call sites lose an argument and the assertion can no longer drift off its fixture.

It was left behind by shrinking the sibling comments. Fix: delete it. The download test's comment beside it earns its place — `ArchiveError::EndpointUnusable` is what distinguishes that route.

comments.text:
`status_for` now takes `&Rejection`, so it cannot be reached with a
server-fault error and a 4xx body can only carry a rejection's own text.
`submit` matches `IngestError` exhaustively: `Archive` goes to

The bucket, endpoint and key reach the log only.

title: Audit cannot verify Calidus-signed objects without timestamp-relative resolution
description:
`verify-archive` passes `ColdKey` at the audit site (main.rs), so once Calidus
resolution lands, objects a pool signed with its Calidus key are reported as
unverifiable rather than failed. Making them verifiable means resolving
registrations as of each object's timestamp, not as of now — otherwise a pool
that rotated fails an audit for objects that were valid when stored. Until
then ADR 0005's "independently verifiable forever" holds only for cold-key
objects.
close_reason: Obsolete: Calidus removed by metsuke-jfb.5

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Code as of the .44 diff does the opposite of this body's premise: Calidus-signed
objects are reported as *failed*, not unverifiable.

`ColdKey::speaks_for` returns `Speaks::Not(Refusal::NotTheColdKey)`, `verify.rs`
maps that to `VerifyError::UnauthorizedKey`, and `AuditFailure` has only
`Unreadable` and `Failed` — so every archived Calidus object lands in
`failed()` and `verify-archive` exits nonzero as if the corpus were corrupt.
`AuditFailure`'s own doc draws the distinction it then does not offer a bucket
for.

Fix: a third `AuditFailure::Unverifiable` fed by `Refusal::NotTheColdKey`,
counted apart from `failed()`, before the timestamp-relative resolution this
ticket is really about.

title: Client binary end-to-end
description:
## What to build

The complete agent an SPO runs: TOML config (pool_id, metrics_url, upload_url, optional signing_key; interval/SNTP defaults commented), key resolution --signing-key flag > config path > loud failure (systemd LoadCredential support), a 5-minute sample loop and a decoupled 1-hour upload loop (both configurable) that compresses, signs, and POSTs batches with pool_id/vkey/signature headers. 5xx or network failure keeps spooling and retries next interval with jitter; 4xx keeps the spool, logs the server's reason to journald, and backs off exponentially with a clamp; an ACK carrying a newer latest_version logs a journal warning. Demoable end-to-end against a wiremock server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recorded scrape bodies in → signed, compressed batch with correct headers out (external-behaviour test).
- [ ] Missing key at both flag and config → startup fails loudly.
- [ ] 5xx: spool intact, retry scheduled with jitter. 4xx: spool intact, reason logged, backoff clamped.
- [ ] ACK deletes the delivered rows; newer latest_version in the ACK logs a warning.
- [ ] Sample and upload cadences are independent configuration.

## Blocked by

Prometheus scrape into a sample; SNTP clock-offset probe; SQLite spool.
close_reason: client binary end-to-end; 32 tests incl. binary-level; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: config.rs (TOML, required fields loud, all limits defaulted knobs, example config pinned by test), keys.rs (TextEnvelope 5820 seed, flag>config>loud failure), cli.rs (hand-parsed --config/--signing-key), uploader.rs (ADR-0001 headers, Acked/Retryable/Rejected + ADR-0006 nudge), schedule.rs (pure: jitter on retryable, clamped exponential backoff on 4xx), agent.rs ticks, main.rs loop with journald severity prefixes. Delivery now takes pool_id from config (Calidus, ADR 0003). Review round 1: split AckAfterAccept error, binary-level tests incl. mutation-checked flag>config precedence, tests/support module, prose fixes. Filed metsuke-oqh.

title: S3 credentials come from environment variables
description:
`main.rs` reads S3 credentials with `Credentials::from_env()` and
`Fatal::MissingCredentials` names AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY;
`S3Config`'s doc comment states this as deliberate. Secrets belong in a file
passed by path (sops + agenix, delivered via systemd LoadCredential), which is
what `[calidus]` does for its Postgres role. Bites when the NixOS module is
written.

title: Confirm metsuke rejects a scope-mismatched CIP-151 registration
description:
CIP-151 anchors a registration by requiring blake2b-224(witness key) to equal
the pool id in the payload scope. Confirm metsuke's own verifier enforces that
binding: craft a blob against the local devnet where the witness key does not
match the scope and check it is refused. Source reading plus one crafted blob;
not expected to find a metsuke bug, this closes the loop on ADR 8's claim.
close_reason: Confirmed: metsuke's verifier rejects a crafted scope-mismatched CIP-151 registration (pgrx-equivalent unit test, calidus.rs suite green). Forwarded finding to security for coordinated disclosure to the relevant upstream projects.

title: Allowlist chain query has never been answered by a db-sync
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/applications.rs QUERY is written from the db-sync schema, not recorded: no Postgres has run it. Unverified: the join through pool_update.registered_tx_id to tx_metadata, the current-registration restriction (= MAX(registered_tx_id)), the SELECT DISTINCT that collapses one pool_update row per certificate, and the pool_retire exclusion — which ignores retiring_epoch, so an announced-but-pending retirement drops a pool that is still active. A wrong join silently drops pools from the gate.

tests/support fake_psql replays a hand-written CSV for the same reason (CLAUDE.md: test doubles are recordings).

Fix: run it against the Leios devnet (metsuke-4zo.53 stands one up), post a label-674 pool update, commit the psql CSV as the cassette.
close_reason: Obsolete: in-server db-sync removed by metsuke-jfb.5; gate moves offline (metsuke-jfb.7)

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Second query semantic to check on the devnet, alongside the join: the pool_retire exclusion drops a pool whose retirement is announced but not yet effective. The NOT EXISTS compares pr.announced_tx_id against MAX(registered_tx_id), never pr.retiring_epoch against the current epoch, so a pool that announced retirement for a future epoch and is still minting is excluded from the gate. Decide whether announced-but-pending counts as active, then record the cassette for that case too.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Description is stale after the round-1 rename: it names crates/metsuke-server/src/participants.rs (now applications.rs), "the GROUP BY that makes a contested code two rows" (the GROUP BY is gone) and Excluded::ContestedCode (deleted). The query it describes is not the query in the tree. Rewrite against applications.rs const QUERY before anyone picks this up — tests/support/mod.rs fake_psql points readers here.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Partial evidence, from a real Postgres 17.10 rather than a devnet. I built the four tables the QUERY touches with db-sync's column types (pool_hash.view varchar, pool_update.hash_id/cert_index/registered_tx_id, tx_metadata.key numeric(20,0) + json jsonb, pool_retire.hash_id/announced_tx_id/retiring_epoch), seeded seven pools, and ran the shipped QUERY verbatim.

What it answers:

- Two registration certs sharing one tx: DISTINCT collapses them to one row. Without DISTINCT the same pool comes back twice, which is what the fix was for.
- A superseded code is dropped for the current one: a pool registering TYPO at tx 300 then MUSA-0003 at tx 301 returns only MUSA-0003.
- A pool retired after its last update is excluded.
- Hostile label-674 shapes do NOT error the query. json '["musashinet_incentives_application_code"]', a bare string equal to the key, and {"...":null} each satisfy `jsonb ? key` and yield NULL from `->>`, so they arrive as an empty application_code and land in Registered.ignored. jsonb returns NULL where the json type would have raised; db-sync's column is jsonb, so the SQL-level denial of service is not reachable.

What it does not answer: that these are db-sync's real column types and that the join through pool_update.registered_tx_id to tx_metadata is how db-sync actually files pool-registration metadata. The schema here is hand-built from the documented shape, not dumped from a running db-sync — that is still this ticket's work, and the CSV cassette still has to come from one.

Also demonstrated, for the retiring_epoch gap already on this ticket: a pool whose retirement is announced at tx 601 for epoch 999 is excluded today, though it is active until epoch 999.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Reachability of Excluded::ContradictoryCodes belongs here. With SELECT DISTINCT plus = MAX(registered_tx_id), and tx_metadata holding one row per (tx_id, key), the query returns at most one row per pool — so the variant is unreachable from this query as verified against the Postgres run recorded above. read_registered keeps the guard because the query has not run against a real db-sync; confirm here when the cassette lands, and drop the variant if it holds.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Correction to the Postgres transcript comment above: it says the NULL-code rows 'land in Registered.ignored'. That field was split in metsuke-4zo.9 — they land in Registered.unreadable, because an empty application_code fails ApplicationCode::parse. Registered.contradicted is the other half and is not what these hit.

title: Local Leios devnet with db-sync and a metadata submitter
description:
Three tickets need to observe raw chain metadata through db-sync and none stands the setup up: metsuke-4zo.44 (label-867 registration blobs), metsuke-4zo.51 (craft a scope-mismatched CIP-151 blob), metsuke-4zo.52 (record the label-674 allowlist query). Whichever runs first pays for it and the others inherit an undocumented dependency.

nix run github:input-output-hk/ouroboros-leios#dev-demo-proto-devnet gives a chain only. What is missing: db-sync against it, a read-only role, and a way to submit arbitrary transaction metadata (labels 674 and 867).

Deliver a script under scripts/ that brings all three up and tears them down, plus the k value its Shelley genesis carries (metsuke-4zo.44 reads k from genesis, and devnet disagrees with testnet).
close_reason: devnet stack, submitter and cardano-signer package land with the k values recorded

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Verified end to end: submit-metadata 674 -> block -> db-sync -> tx_metadata row read by metsuke_ro.

Four findings the blocked tickets need, all in docs/research/leios-devnet.md: the demo config's GenesisMode stalls a lone forger at exactly k blocks (LoE fragment is empty without peers, then NoLedgerView at tip+3k/f forever), so setup sets PraosMode; Byron's genesis hash is over canonical encoding, not the file; db-sync refuses a node config without ByronGenesisHash while the node tolerates it; the devnet's k is 6 and is not the network's 108.

Not answered here: rollback and depth. One forger, no reorgs.

title: counters_path is not validated as absolute
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs counters_path is a bare PathBuf, so a relative value opens the counter database under whatever directory the process started in — / under a systemd unit with no WorkingDirectory. The replay index then silently lives somewhere nobody looks, and a rebuild seeds the wrong file.

The [applications] section's three paths gained AbsolutePath in metsuke-4zo.9; counters_path and archive.root are the same class and were out of that ticket's scope.

Fix: AbsolutePath for counters_path and ArchiveConfig::Filesystem::root.

title: devnet setup and submitters lose exit status through command substitution
description:
devnet/flake.nix, three sites where `$(...)` sits in an argument list, so errexit
never fires and a failure becomes an empty or `null` value:

- `set_hash ByronGenesisHash "$(cardano-cli byron genesis print-genesis-hash ...)"`
  and the `for era in Shelley Alonzo Conway Dijkstra` loop: a failing cardano-cli
  writes `"ByronGenesisHash": ""`, setup reports success, the node dies later
  with GenesisHashMismatch.
- `--tx-in "$(utxos | jq -r 'to_entries | max_by(.value.value.lovelace) | .key')"`
  in both `devnet-submit-metadata` and `devnet-register-pool`: `max_by` on `{}`
  prints the literal `null`.
- `await()`'s `if utxos | jq -e ...` suspends errexit, so a dead node or socket
  burns 600s and reports "not on chain within 600s".

Fix: assign to a variable first (assignment does trip errexit), use `jq -er`, and
in `await` run `utxos` outside the `if` condition.
close_reason: fixed in the devnet commit

title: devnet-submit-metadata ignores its label argument
description:
devnet/flake.nix, `submitMetadata`: `label` is only used to assert the key is
present (`jq -e --arg l "$label" 'has($l)'`), then the whole file goes to
`--metadata-json-file "$blob"`. A file holding both 674 and 867 submits both
whichever label is named, so `submit-metadata 674 blob.json` does not do what its
usage string says.

Fix: `jq '{($l): .[$l]}' "$blob" >"$tmp/meta.json"` and submit that, or drop the
argument and rename the command.
close_reason: fixed in the devnet commit

title: devnet.sh down races the running stack and wipes state regardless
description:
scripts/devnet.sh, `down`: `pkill -f 'process-compose.*devnet' 2>/dev/null || true`
then unconditional `rm -rf "$work"` and an unconditional "devnet: stopped".
`|| true` swallows pkill's 2 and 3 (usage, fatal) alongside 1 (no match), nothing
waits for shutdown, so the delete races a live Postgres, and a missed pattern
leaves the stack running with its state gone. `up` also wipes `$work` without
checking whether a stack is already on it.

`up` is `exec nix run` in the foreground and records no pid, so `down` has nothing
authoritative to kill.

Fix: record a pidfile outside the wiped tree, have `down` use it, poll until the
process is gone, then delete; branch on pkill's status instead of `|| true`.
close_reason: down is a process-compose client call now, and keeps state

title: grant-reader races db-sync's schema migration
description:
devnet/flake.nix, `grant-reader` gates on `depends_on.db-sync.condition =
"process_started"`. `GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES` covers tables that exist when it
runs and `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` covers tables created after it, so any table
db-sync migrates in the window between process start and the psql call gets
neither, and metsuke_ro cannot read it.

Fix: gate on db-sync reaching a migrated state (a readiness probe selecting from
`schema_version`), or re-run both GRANTs idempotently after migration.
close_reason: Obsolete: grant-reader/db-sync removed by metsuke-jfb.5

title: devnet node readiness probe tests socket existence, not liveness
description:
devnet/flake.nix, the `node` process: `readiness_probe.exec.command = "test -S
${workdir}/node.socket"`. The socket file outlives a crashed node, so
`node.condition = "process_healthy"` on db-sync can be satisfied by a dead node
and db-sync then fails against a stale socket.

Fix: probe `cardano-cli latest query tip` against the socket instead.

title: Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path
description:
## What to build

The ingest server accepting its first authenticated submission end-to-end. Checks run cheap→expensive: allowlist → per-pool rate limit → Ed25519 verify over the compressed bytes → bounded streaming decompression (fixed arena) → replay-counter check — verification precedes decompression so only authenticated bytes reach the decompressor (ADR 0002). Cold-key identity is pure computation: blake2b-224(vkey) == pool_id (ADR 0003). Accepted submissions go to storage behind a trait with a filesystem implementation (the cargo-test seam); the ACK carries latest_version embedded from the client crate at build. Every limit is configuration, never a constant. Rejections carry a reason the client can log.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid signed batch in → stored object (raw bytes as received) + ACK with latest_version out.
- [ ] Each check rejects independently with a distinct reason: oversized body, unknown pool, rate limit, unauthorized key, bad signature, oversized decompression, unsupported schema version, envelope pool id not the submitted one, timestamp outside the window, stale/replayed counter.
- [ ] Property test: replay-counter acceptance logic (monotonic per pool, state in SQLite).
- [ ] Decompression never allocates beyond its configured ceiling.
- [ ] No check reads decompressed bytes before signature verification passes.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core.
close_reason: Intake library green; HTTP wiring split to .16

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Review of .4 (O3): build ingest as one intake module — single entry point taking raw bytes + signature, returning accepted-envelope-or-rejection with one exhaustive error type; key store, counter store, archive as adapters behind it. Keeps the four-ADR ordering out of main.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review of the working tree (report-only)

Gates run this session: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean; `cargo test --workspace` 100 passed 0 failed; `nix flake check` all checks passed. No untracked files — every new file is staged, so the flake gate saw them.

### Intent

- crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs:1 — no HTTP layer, no config loader, main is still a stub, so 'the ingest server accepting its first authenticated submission end-to-end' holds only at library level. Filed metsuke-4zo.16; decide whether .6 closes on the library or absorbs .16.
- crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs:189 — 'Decompression never allocates beyond its configured ceiling' is not met: read_to_end doubles a growing Vec, so peak capacity reaches ~2x the ceiling. Fix: Vec::with_capacity(max+1) before read_to_end.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:443-461 — counter advances before archive.store, ADR-0002 says counter state 'is updated only after the full chain passes'. The code comment argues for the current order; that argument belongs in the ADR. Either reorder or amend ADR-0002.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:418-430 — UnsupportedSchema and PoolIdMismatch are not in the ticket's check chain or ADR-0002. PoolIdMismatch closes a real gap (allowlist and rate limit run on the header, not the signed body). Keep, add both to the ticket's reason list and to ADR-0002's chain.

### Standards

- crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs:187-194 — migrate() is byte-identical to crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs:57-63. Extract one `migrate(conn, migrations)` into the metsuke crate; each caller keeps its own `#[from] rusqlite::Error`.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs:189 — `.skip(applied as usize)` returns Ok when user_version > MIGRATIONS.len(), so an old binary opens a newer schema silently. Error naming both numbers. Same hole pre-exists in spool.rs: metsuke-4zo.17.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:286 — Submission.body vs wire_bytes everywhere else (envelope::open, SealedBatch.wire_bytes, StoredSubmission.wire_bytes); intake.rs:460 copies one into the other. Rename the field to wire_bytes.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/archive.rs:36-37 — 'so the stored object re-verifies on its own' is false for FilesystemArchive, which writes only wire_bytes; vkey, signature and schema_version on StoredSubmission are read by no code. ADR-0005's metadata headers and index row belong to metsuke-4zo.7. Cite .7 where the fields are declared, or drop the claim.

### Prose

- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:1-5 — restates ADR-0002's check ordering verbatim. ADR-0002 owns it; keep the pointer only.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/archive.rs:1-2 — restates ADR-0005's 'zstd bytes exactly as received'. Same.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs:177-178 — restates spool.rs:45's migration-convention sentence. Point at metsuke::spool.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/lib.rs:5-8 — the parenthetical module map repeats what the five `pub mod` lines below say. Drop it.

### Discarded

Rate limit charged before the cold-key check is the order ADR-0002 documents. RateLimiter's HashMap is bounded by the allowlist, since the allowlist check precedes it. u64-as-i64 casts and the duplicated all-sevens test seed do not clear the bar.

### Filed

metsuke-4zo.16, metsuke-4zo.17.

### Beads hygiene

.beads/issues.jsonl is modified and unstaged — stage it with the code. Ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason yet; the map's Success Criteria section carries no per-ticket decision line.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review of the working tree (report-only, second pass)

Gates run this session: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean.
`cargo test --workspace` — one run failed `metsuke --test scrape`, the rerun
passed 84/0. `nix flake check` — one run failed the same test, the rerun said
"all checks passed". That is metsuke-4zo.18, 2 of 4 runs red on this tree; the
evidence is on .18 now. No untracked files, so the flake gate sees every new
file.

The four findings from the first pass that were fixed are gone from this report:
the shared `migrate()`, its future-schema guard, the decompression arena, and
`Submission.wire_bytes`.

### Intent

- crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs:190-192 — the arena fix overshot: every `open`
  now commits `max_decompressed_bytes` up front, so the configured ceiling
  became a per-request floor. A 200-byte payload reserves the full ceiling, and
  once metsuke-4zo.16 serves this concurrently it is N × ceiling of RSS. Read
  `decoder.take(max+1)` into a fixed chunk buffer and `reserve_exact` per chunk
  — capacity then tracks real data and still never passes the ceiling.
- crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs:191,194 — `saturating_add(1)` for the arena but
  plain `max_decompressed_bytes + 1` for `take`, and the `usize::try_from` is an
  `.expect()`. An operator config value should not panic the request path.
  One saturating value for both, and an `OpenError` variant instead of the
  expect.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:474-495 — `archive.store` precedes
  `counters.accept`, so a submission that loses the counter race is stored and
  then rejected. Two racing bodies at one counter share an object key, so the
  archive can end up holding the loser's bytes while the ACK went to the
  winner. Either put the store and the counter write in one transaction, or
  state in ADR-0002 that a stored-but-rejected object is the accepted cost.
- crates/metsuke/src/sqlite.rs:21-26 — this is metsuke-4zo.17's fix, done
  inside .6. Commented on .17; close it with this work or the work is
  untracked.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs:1 — still `println!`, so "the ingest server
  accepting its first authenticated submission end-to-end" holds at library
  level only. metsuke-4zo.16 owns the HTTP layer; decide whether .6 closes on
  the library or absorbs .16.

### Standards

- crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs:16 — "Cap on the compressed body, checked
  before anything reads it" is false: intake.rs:95 measures
  `submission.wire_bytes.len()`, a slice already fully buffered. Say that .16
  owns the streaming cap, or the comment claims protection the code has not
  got.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/ratelimit.rs:31-32 — "a rejected attempt is not
  charged, so a throttled pool cannot extend its own lockout by retrying": the
  window resets on elapsed time and `started_at` never moves on a charge, so
  charging could not extend anything. Drop the clause; the behaviour is right,
  the reason given for it is not.

### Prose

- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:113-115 — restates ADR-0003:18-19 ("the
  pool id *is* that hash. Pure computation, no infrastructure"). Keep the
  pointer and the Calidus note, drop the mechanism.
- crates/metsuke/src/lib.rs:4-5 — the ACK-embedding mechanics are already on
  the field at envelope.rs:23-24, which owns them. Shorten to "This agent
  build's version (ADR 0006)."
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:189-190 — first sentence restates
  ADR-0002's amended decision text verbatim in substance. Cut it; the
  read-spares-the-PUT / write-settles-the-race sentence is local reasoning and
  stays.

### Discarded

`or_insert_with` in ratelimit, `create_dir_all` per store, the two `test_now()`
helpers (separate test binaries, and counters.rs:11-12 states why its instant
differs), `pool()` vs `pool_of`, unpadded counter in the object key,
`Intake::accept` naming, the twice-built `ReplayedCounter`, and the rustfmt
churn in binary.rs and uploader.rs.

### Filed

Commented on metsuke-4zo.17, metsuke-4zo.18. No new tickets.

### Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged, and staged again after this comment — restage
before committing. The ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason.
The map metsuke-4zo has no `## Decisions so far` section to gain a line; its
Success Criteria block is untouched. Acceptance criterion 2 was rewritten by
this diff to add the five reasons the code implements, so that criterion now
matches the code by construction — worth a word in the resolution comment.

### Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`. Blocking: `nix flake check` is red on 2 of 4 runs via
metsuke-4zo.18, and the envelope.rs allocation regression should not ship as
the answer to the first pass.

title: devnet setup duplicates the genesis stamp and node launch in record-scrape-fixtures.sh
description:
`devnet-setup` and `devnet-node` in devnet/flake.nix re-derive what
scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh already does: the same
`cp .../config/genesis/*.json` + `date +%s` / `date -u -d @` pair, the same two
jq genesis rewrites, the same `yq -o=json config.yaml | jq '.TraceOptionNodeName
= ... | .TraceOptions."".backends'` patch, and a byte-identical `cardano-node run`
argument list down to `--port 3001`. Two independently editable copies.

The recorder also resolves its binaries by `nix flake prefetch` plus a `nix build`
of a rev read out of flake.lock, which the devnet flake now pins properly.

Fix: one shared shell function parameterised by k, epochLength, metricsPort,
consensus mode and node name, called by both — or point the recorder at
`devnet#cardano-node` and `devnet#devnet-setup`.

comments.author: claude

Found reviewing metsuke-jfb.20 / .21.

title: leios-devnet.md restates the devnet flake's comments and digits
description:
docs/research/leios-devnet.md carries second copies of prose the code already
owns, against CLAUDE.md "Digits live in exactly one file" and "Name the fact's
home before writing it":

- k=6 / epochLength=1200 are owned by `securityParam` / `epochLength` in
  devnet/flake.nix; md repeats them in the table, in the bolded fixture note, and
  in the PraosMode section.
- The devnet-k-is-not-the-network's-k fact has copies in md, the flake comment,
  the devnet.sh usage footer and the ticket comment. Home is ADR 0008 ("k is read
  from the network's Shelley genesis").
- md's Postgres, GRANT-ordering, NodeConfigFile-is-relative, mempool-wait and
  PC_DISABLE_TUI paragraphs each restate a comment sitting at the code. The
  NodeConfigFile note is also duplicated inside flake.nix itself (the `setup`

- Counts nothing checks or that are already wrong: "89 Haskell derivations",

  iohk-monitoring log config" (the file has 14 top-level keys), and flake.nix's

- Network genesis digits (108/21600, 2160/432000) belong to the cardano-playground
  leios genesis and the proto-devnet genesis pinned by devnet/flake.lock; name the

Keep: the PraosMode measurement (slot 294, first NoLedgerView at 655 = 294 + 360)
and the "what it cannot answer" list. Those are the file's own.
close_reason: fixed in the devnet commit

title: devnet identity constants are re-typed instead of named once
description:
devnet/flake.nix already names `database`, `owner`, `reader`, `securityParam`,
`epochLength`, `metricsPort` in its `let`, but:

- network magic `164` is written literally in `submitterEnv`, the pool
  registration certificate, `access-instructions` and scripts/devnet.sh, and is
  never asserted against the stamped genesis' `networkMagic` — unlike
  `epochLength`, which is checked with `jq -e`.
- `await`'s timeout is `seq 120` and `sleep 5` with a hand-derived "within 600s"
  in the error message; change either number and the message lies. CLAUDE.md:
  limits and intervals are configuration.
- scripts/devnet.sh's `psql` case hardcodes `metsuke_ro` and `cexplorer`,
  duplicating `reader` and `database`.

Fix: `networkMagic` and `awaitAttempts`/`awaitIntervalSeconds` in the `let`, with
the message interpolating the product and a `jq -e` magic assertion; expose a
`devnet-psql` package so the wrapper stops re-typing the role names.

title: cardano-signer is packaged but nothing can reach it
description:
devnet/flake.nix packages `cardano-signer` (plus the `cardano-signer-src` and
`bun2nix` inputs and the committed bun.lock / bun.nix), and its comment states why
the reference CIP-151 implementation is needed rather than our own encoder. But no
scripts/devnet.sh subcommand invokes it and docs/research/leios-devnet.md never
mentions it, so a consumer has to know to run `nix run ./devnet#cardano-signer`.

Question: wire it in now — a `devnet.sh sign` subcommand plus a line in the
research doc — or leave the package unreferenced until metsuke-4zo.44 / .51 use it?
close_reason: packaged and reachable as nix run ./devnet#cardano-signer; wiring deferred to .44/.51 so the interface follows a real caller

title: db-sync self-deadlocks on every devnet start
description:
devnet/flake.nix: on every `scripts/devnet.sh up`, and on every db-sync restart, db-sync's
NearTip index migration blocks forever. pg_locks: the chain-sync connection holds AccessExclusive
on epoch_stake and reward inside an open transaction (`ALTER TABLE reward ADD CONSTRAINT
unique_reward`, idle in transaction, ClientRead) while the migration connection waits for a
ShareLock on epoch_stake (`CREATE INDEX idx_epoch_stake_pool_id`). Nothing else is connected, so
db-sync is deadlocking against itself; block_no stays at 0 and tx_metadata is never populated.

Cleared by `process restart db-sync` -- sometimes after several tries. Recording the CIP-151
fixtures (metsuke-4zo.44) cost three restarts, and metsuke-4zo.52 will hit the same wall.

Fix: hold db-sync back until the migrations it runs at NearTip are done, or drop the
migration-4-* index files the schema dir ships (db-sync's own warning says they are for clients,
not for it).
close_reason: devnet hands db-sync a schema dir without stage-4 client indexes

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree (devnet/flake.nix dbSyncSchema). No untracked files.

## Verified

- 9 of 83 files in the pinned schema match `migration-4-*` (rev 6d7f6134707b73610464def9601a0561460a4d85), all `.sql`; the glob and the `ls` guard both hold at this pin.
- `idx_epoch_stake_pool_id` -- the index the ticket's pg_locks trace names -- is defined in `migration-4-0003-20210116.sql`, so the removal targets the exact deadlock.
- `dbSyncSchema` is the only reference to the schema path (flake.nix:241, :504); nothing else went stale.
- Upstream's log line and `addConstraintsIfNotExist` both resolve at the pin (`cardano-db-sync/src/Cardano/DbSync.hs`, `.../Util/Constraint.hs`).
- `nix fmt -- --ci devnet/flake.nix`: 0 changed. `nix flake check` not run.

## Prose

- flake.nix:52-60 -- the 9-line comment is the ticket's incident trace re-typed almost sentence-for-sentence (lock modes, both table names, the ALTER/CREATE INDEX pair). CLAUDE.md: "Why the project needed the work belongs to the ticket and the research doc." Fix: keep the why and the upstream citation, point at the ticket for the trace:

    # db-sync self-deadlocks: chain-sync holds AccessExclusive on epoch_stake
    # while its own stage-4 migration waits to index it -- metsuke-4zo.64.
    # Upstream's log (DbSync.hs) calls these client indexes db-sync does not
    # use and names deleting migration-4-* as the fix. Nothing here needs them.

## Considered and dropped

- `lib.cleanSourceWith` instead of cp/chmod/rm: works, but trades a build-time assertion for eval-time and diverges from `signerSrc`'s runCommand idiom in the same file. Not worth the churn.
- Error message at :67 lacking a "why": the comment is three lines above it.

Nothing filed -- no finding fell outside this ticket.

Verdict: one prose fix, then commit. Stage .beads/ with the code.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Strip migration-4-* from the schema dir handed to db-sync. Root cause at db-sync 6d7f613: Default.hs commitOrIndexes commits before addConstraintsIfNotExist, then 'unless commited' skips the second commit, so that ALTER's AccessExclusive on reward/epoch_stake is still held when the NearTip connection issues CREATE INDEX idx_epoch_stake_pool_id. validateMigrations is test-only, so a short schema dir is safe. Verified on one up, zero restarts: block_no 0 to 10, 'Migration 0/0' at NearTip, tx_metadata populated by a label-674 submit, and advance 9 to 10 after a db-sync restart.

title: CIP-151 registrations witnessed without COSE resolve as unregistered
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/cip151.rs `cose_witness` reads only the CIP-8 witness shape
({1: COSE_Key, 2: COSE_Sign1}). CIP-151 also defines the simple witness
[witnessType, pubKey, sig]; a registration carrying one is dropped, so its pool resolves as
never-registered and its uploads are refused.

Deliberate: cardano-signer 1.35.0 emits COSE only, so every fixture under
tests/fixtures/calidus is COSE and what a simple witness signs is unverified. Implementing it
against the CIP text alone would be a guess -- the same text that says the payload hash is over
hex, which cardano-signer does not do.

Fix: find or make a simple-witness registration to record, then read it. Until one exists the
gap is real for any operator using a tool that emits one.
close_reason: Obsolete: CIP-151 witness check removed by metsuke-jfb.5

title: bun2nix output loses its formatting on regeneration
description:
devnet/cardano-signer/bun.nix is generated by bun2nix and checked in. treefmt's deadnix strips
three unused function arguments from it and nixfmt adds the trailing newline, so the committed
file and the generated one differ: checks.treefmt was red at 9599f69 and every regeneration will
make it red again.

Fix: run `nix fmt` as part of regenerating it, or exclude the file from treefmt so what is
committed is what bun2nix wrote.

title: Calidus registrations query filters scope by JSON extraction with no index
description:
`crates/metsuke-server/src/registrations.sql`: the pool filter is
`tm.json -> '1' -> '1' ->> 1 = :'scope'`. `tm.key = 867` narrows to every
Calidus registration on the chain, then the JSON extraction is evaluated per
row, so cost scales with chain-wide label-867 volume rather than this pool's
rows. The query has never been run against a db-sync holding real registration
volume.

Fix needs a decision the read-only role cannot make alone: a functional index
on the scope expression filtered to `key = 867` is a db-sync schema change,
so either the Leios db-sync deployment carries it or the query is restructured
(e.g. join through a scope-extracting materialized view). Measure first.
close_reason: Obsolete: Calidus registrations query removed by metsuke-jfb.5

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
metsuke-4zo.68 added `LIMIT $3` to registrations.sql. It does not close this
one: a LIMIT stops the scan only once N rows have matched, so the honest case —
a pool with one registration, under a cap of 10 — still examines every label-867
row to prove there is no 11th. The cap bounds the in-process CBOR/Ed25519 work,
not the query. The index this ticket asks for is what makes the limit able to
stop early.

title: Calidus registrations query has no row cap, so a spammer sets a pool's verification cost
description:
`crates/metsuke-server/src/registrations.sql` selects every label-867 row
scoping a pool with no `LIMIT`. The scope is attacker-chosen — anyone who pays
for a transaction can post rows naming a victim pool — and `calidus::witnessed`
CBOR-decodes and Ed25519-verifies each one per TTL expiry. Enough rows and the
query trips `statement_timeout`, which is `DirectoryError::Unavailable` and a
503 for that pool's uploads.

Distinct from metsuke-4zo.67: that one is the scope predicate's index cost, a
deployment call. This is the row count the server agrees to verify.

The decision: capping in SQL means choosing which rows survive the cap before
the witness check has run, and the highest nonce may be the unwitnessed one, so
a naive `ORDER BY nonce DESC LIMIT n` lets a spammer push the real
registration out of the window. Options are a cap large enough that the loss is
theoretical, a cap plus a refusal when it is hit, or verifying in nonce order
until one passes.
close_reason: Row cap in SQL, refusal rather than truncation, 403 naming the bound

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
# Review of the working tree (report only, nothing edited)

Gate run: `cargo test -p metsuke-server` — 212 passed, 0 failed. `nix flake check`
not run. No untracked files; 17 tracked files modified.

## Intent — the decision the `needs-decision` label was holding

1. **The default cap makes the attack cheaper than the one it replaces.** Before,
   a spammer needed enough rows to burn `query_timeout_secs = 30`, and the result
   was a 503 the pool could retry. Now 11 transactions against
   `max_registrations = 10` (contrib/server.example.toml) produce a 403 that
   recurs every TTL and is liftable only by an operator editing config. ADR 0008
   concedes "the rows are free to post on the chain we read" and argues refusal
   over truncation, but never weighs the chosen cap against option 1 ("a cap
   large enough that the loss is theoretical"). The mechanism is right; the
   default is what decides whether the attack costs 11 tx fees or thousands.
2. **docs/adr/0008:39-47 answers one of the ticket's three options.** It argues
   against truncation, which kills option 3's ordered-LIMIT variant, and says
   nothing about why option 1 or nonce-order-until-one-passes was rejected.

Correct as implemented: `LIMIT max+1` with `len > max` distinguishes at-bound
from over-bound exactly; `TooMany` is cached through the same
`resolved.insert` as a key, so a crowded pool costs one query per TTL; the
cold-key path never reaches the directory.

## Silent failures — scripts/record-calidus-fixtures.sh

3. **:190 `|| true` masks a psql failure as a row-count mismatch.**
   `answered=$(prepared "$pool_b" "$crowded_cap" | grep -c . || true)` — with
   `set -o pipefail`, a SQL error, a dead devnet, and a genuinely empty answer
   all land on "the query answered 0 rows under a limit of 2". Redirect
   `prepared` to a file as its own statement so `set -e` catches it, then count
   the file.
4. **:83-85 `jq -r .poolIdHex` prints `null` instead of failing.** A
   cardano-signer output change silently yields the scope `0xnull`; every count
   reads 0, `fill` resubmits on every run, and the failure surfaces ten minutes
   later as a depth error. `jq -er`, as :161 already does for `securityParam`.
5. **:190 races the depth wait.** `pool_b`'s rows are submitted after
   `pool_a`'s (:143), but the only wait loop (:178-181) polls `pool_a`. On a
   fresh recording the assertion can read fewer than `crowded_cap` and hard-exit
   on a chain that is fine. Wrap :190 in the same `seq 120`/`sleep 5` loop,
   breaking when `answered -eq crowded_cap`.

## Reuse

6. **:119-120 re-implements the shipped query's scope filter in shell.**
   `scoped="json -> '1' -> '1' ->> 1"` duplicates registrations.sql's
   `tm.json -> '1' -> '1' ->> 1`, which is the one thing this recorder exists to
   avoid. It fails silently: if the path or db-sync's rendering changes,
   `rows_for` returns 0 and the recorder reports "reusing" while proving nothing.
   Count through `prepared` with k=0 instead and delete `scoped`.

## Prose

7. **"Refuse rather than truncate, because truncation decides before the witness
   runs" is argued in four places.** ADR 0008:39-47 owns it. Retold at
   calidus.rs:23-26 (which both retells it *and* points at the ADR),
   registrations.sql:10-11, tests/calidus.rs:188-190. Keep the pointers, drop the
   retellings; the test name already says what its comment says.
8. **"The refusal is sent, not withheld" is argued in four places.** ADR
   0008:44-45, intake.rs:30-32, tests/intake.rs:499-502,
   contrib/server.example.toml:49. The assert message at tests/intake.rs:531
   ("the bound is not a secret") already states it inline.
9. **contrib/server.example.toml:49-50 restates config.rs.** The file header
   routes field prose to config.rs, which carries both sentences at :114-116.
   Keep `max_registrations = 10`, drop the comment.
10. **`TEST_MAX_REGISTRATIONS = 10` claims a distinction it does not hold.**
    support/mod.rs:315-316 says "Not the shipped default", and the value is 10 —
    exactly contrib/server.example.toml's and nix/unit-test.nix's. Change the
    constant so it differs, or drop the claim.
11. **"one past the cap" is explained twice**, dbsync.rs:46-47 and
    registrations.sql:9-10. The SQL owns the parameter contract.
12. **support/mod.rs:525-527 and :549-550 both say a crowded directory hands up
    no rows**, which `return Ok(Registrations::TooMany …)` already says. Keep the
    one on `crowd`.

## Standards

13. **calidus.rs:39 "The three refusals are separate"** — `Resolution` now has
    five non-`Key` variants, one of them added by this diff. Drop the count.
    (The same staleness in authority.rs is commented on metsuke-4zo.77.)
14. **tests/intake.rs:366 and :384 seed a row the double never reads.**
    `CannedDirectory::holding(pool, vec![registration("nonce-1-key-a")])` then
    `crowd(...)` — `registrations` returns `TooMany` before it looks at the map.
    The setup reads as "a real registration among stranger rows" and proves only
    the crowded branch. Drop the `holding` row.
15. **contrib/server.example.toml:49 says "upload".** CONTEXT.md's **Submission**
    entry: `_Avoid_: upload, batch, post, payload`. The CONTEXT.md exemption at
    :111-112 covers naming in code, not new operator-facing prose.

## Beads hygiene

- metsuke-4zo.68 is still labelled `needs-decision` with no resolution comment
  and no close reason. Expected pre-commit, but the label must become
  `to-issues:build` or the ticket must close once finding 1 is settled.
- `.beads/issues.jsonl` changes by one line (the `--claim` timestamp) and is
  unstaged; stage `.beads/` in the same commit as the code.
- The map has no `## Decisions so far`; ADR 0008 is the right home and gained
  its paragraph.

## Filed

Filed metsuke-4zo.84, metsuke-4zo.85; commented on metsuke-4zo.67 and
metsuke-4zo.77.

## Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`. Finding 1 is a decision for the operator to make before
this ships: pick the default cap against what crowding a scope costs an
attacker, and record that in ADR 0008 alongside why options 1 and 3 lost.
Findings 3-5 are correctness bugs in the recorder. The rest is prose weight.
