title: Allowlist generation admin command
description:
## What to build

The admin command producing the participant gate: registration CSV ∩ active on-chain pool registrations carrying the matching CIP-20 label-674 key musashinet_incentives_application_code, queried from db-sync, emitted as (pool_id, code) pairs into Nix-managed server config. Codes are public and never treated as secrets; runtime stays db-sync-free on the cold-key path. The command is how operators onboard pools, so its output format is the server's allowlist input format by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CSV row with matching on-chain code → pair emitted; CSV-only or chain-only pools are excluded.
- [ ] Output loads directly as the ingest server's allowlist configuration.
- [ ] Emitted with a summary the operator can review (counts of matched/excluded).

## Blocked by

Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path (defines the allowlist it feeds).
close_reason: generate-allowlist emits the gate; ingest.allowlist is now pool-to-code

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .9. No untracked files; everything staged.

Gates run this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 247 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

All three acceptance criteria have executing evidence: intersection and both one-sided exclusions (tests/participants.rs `a_pool_on_only_one_side_is_excluded`), output loads as the server's allowlist (`the_emitted_pairs_load_as_the_servers_allowlist`, which splices into the shipped example and re-parses), summary counts on stderr (tests/binary.rs `generate_allowlist_writes_the_pairs_to_stdout_and_its_summary_to_stderr`).

## Intent

- `src/participants.rs:114-126` — the QUERY joins every `pool_update` row for a live pool, so a code from a superseded registration still counts. An operator who registers MUSA-0001, spots the typo, and corrects to MUSA-0002 in the next update produces two rows and is permanently `Excluded::ContestedCode`, with no on-chain remedy. Fix: restrict the join to the current registration, `pu.registered_tx_id = (SELECT MAX(registered_tx_id) FROM pool_update WHERE hash_id = ph.id)` — which is also what \"active on-chain pool registrations\" says. That makes `ContestedCode` unreachable, so decide whether it survives.
- `src/participants.rs:272` — \"Anyone can pay for a transaction naming a code\" is the label-867 threat model, not this one. A `pool_update` row exists only in a tx carrying the pool's registration certificate, which only the cold key can sign — the diff's own CONTEXT.md says exactly that (\"only that key can sign a pool registration\"). Both codes in a contested pair came from the operator. Fix: state the real reason (the operator registered two, and picking one is guessing which they meant), or drop the variant with the query fix above.

## Standards

- `src/participants.rs`, `src/config.rs:33-47`, `contrib/server.example.toml:52-60` — CONTEXT.md:60 under **Allowlist** reads `_Avoid_: whitelist, roster, participants`, verbatim. The diff makes both banned words operator-facing: a `[participants]` config section, `pub mod participants`, `ParticipantsConfig`, `roster_csv`, `RosterError`, `read_roster`. This is the mechanism that builds the Allowlist, which is the exact confusion the glossary reserves those words against — and the diff edits CONTEXT.md eleven lines below without reconciling. Fix: rename to the vocabulary the diff itself added — `applications` / `[applications]` / `applications_csv` — or amend CONTEXT.md's Avoid list in this diff and say why.
- `src/participants.rs:187` — `RosterError` is also the error type of the psql CSV path (`ChainError::Unreadable { source: RosterError }`), because both halves go through `read_applications`. The name promises one half and carries both. Fix: `ApplicationsCsvError`, or a distinct variant per producer.
- `src/participants.rs:104` — `Applications` has one implementer, and `main.rs:358` calls `Psql::new(participants).on_chain()?` concretely; no caller takes `impl Applications`, and `fake_psql` fakes the subprocess rather than the trait. Its cost today is an import in `main.rs` and `tests/participants.rs` for method resolution alone. CLAUDE.md: every line earns its place. Fix: inherent method until a second source exists, or take `impl Applications` in `generate_allowlist` so the seam is real.

## Prose

- The Nix-renders-the-config *why*, 3x: `src/participants.rs:288-289` (`to_toml`, which produces the bytes, and owns it), `src/main.rs:169`, `tests/participants.rs:239`. Fix: drop the Nix clause from the latter two. Note none of the three is backed — no `.nix` in the repo consumes the output yet; metsuke-4zo.12 owns the module.
- `src/participants.rs:129` — \"A Postgres client would bring an async runtime into a server that has none\" restates ADR 0008's Consequences line word for word. Fix: `(ADR 0008)`.
- `src/config.rs:36` — \"(ADR 0008 colocates the server with db-sync)\" attributes to the ADR the opposite of what it says: \"Colocation is a deployment constraint, not a protocol one: a separate host reaching db-sync over some authenticated transport would serve equally.\" The peer-authenticated-socket why is already at `participants.rs:153` beside `env_clear()`, which owns it. Fix: drop the citation and the second copy.
- `tests/participants.rs:94` — second copy of `Excluded::ContestedCode`'s why (`participants.rs:272`). Fix: the test doc states the assertion only.
- `tests/support/mod.rs:225` — \"ticket metsuke-4zo.9's own follow-up\" names this ticket, not the follow-up. It is metsuke-4zo.52. Fix: name it.
- Restating the line below, delete: `src/config.rs:46` \"Directory holding the Postgres unix socket.\" over `socket_dir: PathBuf`; `src/config.rs:41` \"with a `pool_id` and an `application_code` column\", which `POOL_ID_COLUMN`/`CODE_COLUMN` own; `src/participants.rs:298` \"Intersect the two halves on pool and code.\" over `fn gate`.

## Scope beyond the ticket, recorded not filed

`Fatal::NobodyMatched` makes an empty intersection a nonzero exit. The ticket asks for pairs plus a summary; a zero-match run is arguably a valid answer. The test at tests/binary.rs `generate_allowlist_refuses_when_the_two_halves_share_nobody` argues for it and I agree with the choice — recording it because nothing asked for it.

`ApplicationCode`'s identifier alphabet is likewise unasked, and justified at the site (`to_toml` interpolates unescaped) and tested. Not a finding.

## Discarded

No findings on silent failures or reuse: every fallible step in `participants.rs` maps to a named variant carrying the path, row, or command, and nothing in the diff duplicates an existing helper. `record.get(at).unwrap_or_default()` at :643 is unreachable — `csv::Reader` is non-flexible by default, so a record's length matches the header's.

## Filed

Commented on metsuke-4zo.52 (the pool_retire exclusion ignores `retiring_epoch`, so an announced-but-pending retirement drops an active pool — same devnet run that ticket already needs). No new tickets: metsuke-4zo.52, filed by this diff, already owns the unverified query.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is in sync after the flush but `MM` from this comment — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. The ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason; pre-commit, your call. The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate.

## Verdict

Not ready for /commit. Two items decide first: the QUERY's superseded-registration semantics, and the CONTEXT.md terminology breach, which is cheapest to fix before `[participants]` reaches an operator's config. The rest are cleanups and none changes behaviour.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. All round-1 items landed: the QUERY takes the current registration only, `ContestedCode` is gone, the rename to `applications` is complete (no `roster`/`participant` survives in crates/, contrib/ or CONTEXT.md outside the `_Avoid_` line), the `Applications` trait is inlined, and the three ADR/Nix prose items are fixed. Two of the three round-1 restatements did not land — see Prose F1/F2.

Gates run this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` no failures; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

## Correctness

- `src/applications.rs:287` and `:207` — `read_codes` is shared by both halves, but the halves have different trust models and only one of them is ours. The applications CSV is the program's own record, so strict is right there. The QUERY returns **every live pool on the chain carrying label 674 with the key**, not just applicants — so any pool operator anywhere can register `674: {musashinet_incentives_application_code: \"hello world\"}` and `ApplicationCodeError::NotAnIdentifier` aborts `generate-allowlist` for the whole program, permanently, from a transaction nobody involved in the program signed. Nothing in the gate can recover: onboarding stops until the query is changed. Fix: parse the chain half leniently — a row that is not a well-formed pool id and code cannot match any application anyway (applications are validated strictly), so drop it and count it in the summary. Keep `read_codes` strict for the CSV.
- `src/applications.rs:110-113` — the query can return two rows for one pool, and after the change above that is now fatal rather than merely wrong. One transaction may carry several pool registration certificates for the same pool; db-sync writes one `pool_update` row per certificate, distinguished by `cert_index`, all sharing `registered_tx_id`. Both then satisfy `pu.registered_tx_id = MAX(...)` and both join the same `tx_metadata` row, so `read_codes` sees the pool twice and returns `PoolTwice`. Round 1's `GROUP BY` was collapsing this; removing it removed the dedup with it. The two rows are byte-identical (one metadata row, one tx), so `SELECT DISTINCT` is the whole fix. `DISTINCT ON (ph.id) ... ORDER BY pu.registered_tx_id DESC, pu.cert_index DESC` says the same thing more precisely if you prefer it. Not verified against a live db-sync; this rests on db-sync's `pool_update(hash_id, cert_index, registered_tx_id)` shape and the Shelley tx body's `certs` list, and metsuke-4zo.52 is where it gets confirmed.
- `src/config.rs:35-36` — \"Absolute, not a PATH lookup: which binary reads the database is not the operator's shell's to decide.\" Nothing enforces it, and `env_clear()` does not: I compiled and ran `Command::new(\"echo\").env_clear().arg(\"REACHED\").output()`, which returned `Ok(\"REACHED\\n\")` — Rust resolves the program against the parent's environment, not the child's. So `psql_path = \"psql\"` PATH-searches, which is exactly what the comment says must not happen. Fix: validate at load (reject a path with no separator) so the config fails loudly, not at exec.

comments.text:
Round 3. All three round-2 blockers landed and are correct: the strict/lenient split, `SELECT DISTINCT`, and `psql_path: AbsolutePath`.

Gates run this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 251 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

I verified the QUERY against a real PostgreSQL 17.10, on four hand-built tables with db-sync's column types. DISTINCT collapses two registration certificates sharing one tx (without it the pool comes back twice, so round 2's finding was real). A superseded code is dropped for the current one. A retired pool is excluded. Hostile label-674 shapes — a JSON array containing the key, a bare string equal to it, and an explicit null — all satisfy `jsonb ? key` and return NULL from `->>` with no SQL error, so they arrive as an empty code and land in `ignored`; `jsonb` returns NULL where the `json` type would have raised, and db-sync's column is `jsonb`. Full transcript is on metsuke-4zo.52, along with what it still does not prove.

## Correctness

- `src/config.rs:74` — `socket_dir` is a plain `PathBuf`, and `psql --host` only means a unix socket directory when the value starts with `/`. Anything else is a hostname: I ran `psql --host relativedir --dbname cexplorer --username x --command "select 1"` and got `could not translate host name "relativedir" to address: Name or service not known`, a DNS lookup and a TCP attempt. So a relative `socket_dir` silently turns the connection into a network one, and `Psql`'s own comment at `applications.rs:136-139` — "the connection is a peer-authenticated unix socket" — becomes false without anything saying so. This is the same defect `AbsolutePath` was just added for, with a worse failure. Fix: `socket_dir: AbsolutePath`. `applications_csv` and `counters_path` carry the milder CWD-relative version of it; your call whether they follow, but `socket_dir` should not wait.
- `src/applications.rs:270` and `src/main.rs:194` — `ignored: ignored + contradicted.len()` adds a pool count to a row count, and the line prints "ignored {ignored} registered rows that are not a pool and a code". Neither half of the label is true of the contradicted case: it counts pools, not rows, and a contradicted row *was* a pool and a code. `tests/applications.rs:193` pins it — two contradicting rows give `ignored: 1`. The field doc at `:232-234` states the same wrong thing. Fix: two fields and two lines — `unreadable` rows, and pools whose registrations gave two different codes.
- `src/applications.rs:244-272` with `gate` — a pool dropped by `read_registered`, whether unreadable or contradicted, is absent from `codes`, so an applicant hits `Excluded::NotRegistered` and the operator is told "applied, but registered no application code". That is false and points at the wrong fix: they did register, and the registration is the problem. Fix: carry the dropped pools out of `Registered` and give `gate` a distinct variant for them.
- `src/main.rs:196-204` — every `DidNotApply` pool gets its own stderr line, and `read_registered` admits *every* live label-674 pool on the chain, not just applicants. Anyone can register the label, so the per-pool listing is unbounded text written by strangers. `main.rs:191-192` makes exactly this argument for not listing ignored rows one each; it applies here too. `applications.rs:322`'s "Every one is operator-actionable" is false for the same reason. Fix: list `NotRegistered` and `CodeMismatch` per pool, count `DidNotApply`.

## Prose

- `tests/binary.rs:235` — "which `neither_store_is_opened` reads" names a test that does not exist; it is `generate_allowlist_opens_neither_store` at `:340`.
- `src/config.rs:143-144` and `tests/config.rs:143-144` — the PATH-search why is in both, but only the test doc carries the half that is not obvious: that `env_clear()` does not prevent it. Fix: move that clause to `config.rs`, which owns the field, and leave the test asserting.
- `tests/support/mod.rs:220-222` — "Every utility it could call is absent from its environment (`Psql` clears it), so it is written in shell builtins alone" gives the wrong mechanism. `env_clear()` is not what makes utilities unreachable: I ran `/bin/sh -c 'echo PATH=$PATH; ls /'` under `env_clear()` and got `PATH=/no-such-path` and a failed `ls` — the shell's compiled-in default PATH is doing the work, and a sh defaulting to `/bin:/usr/bin` would not. Fix: say the double uses builtins only, without claiming why it must.
- Second copies, round-2 survivors: the `[applications]`-is-optional why (`config.rs:26-30` owns it; copies at `tests/config.rs:30-31` and `tests/binary.rs:352-353`), and `ApplicationCode`'s TOML-bare-string and form-whitespace whys (`applications.rs:19-21` owns them; copies at `tests/applications.rs:225-226` and `:218-219`), plus `applications.rs:211`'s "dropping it would read as a pool that never applied" copied at `tests/applications.rs:129`.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 4. All four round-3 correctness items landed and are correct: `AbsolutePath` on all three `[applications]` paths, `unreadable`/`contradicted` counted apart, `Excluded::ContradictoryCodes` checked ahead of the `codes` lookup, `did_not_apply` reduced to a count. metsuke-4zo.54 is well-formed and resolves against the tree.

Gates run this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 252 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

Nothing in this round is a behaviour bug. Three items, then prose.

## Correctness

- `src/main.rs:170-185` and `src/applications.rs:340-350` — `Gate` is not the verdict. `generate_allowlist` copies `registered.unreadable` out before `gate` consumes the whole `Registered`, then threads it to `report_gate` as a second parameter, while `Gate` already carries the sibling whole-chain count `did_not_apply`. CLAUDE.md: every parameter earns its place. Fix: `Gate.unreadable`, set inside `gate`, and `report_gate(&Gate)`.
- `src/applications.rs:391` with `:270` — the same fix closes a gap: a pool that is contradicted and did **not** apply is counted nowhere. `gate` walks `applied` only, and `did_not_apply` counts `registered.codes.keys()`, from which contradicted pools were removed. So `allowed ∪ excluded ∪ did_not_apply` misses exactly `contradicted \ applied`, while the line says "N pools have a registered code and never applied". Everything else balances: each applicant lands in `allowed` or `excluded` exactly once, and `unreadable` is rows labelled as rows. Low impact — these are strangers — but it is a silent under-report. Fix: count `did_not_apply` over `registered.codes.keys()` chained with `contradicted`, deduped against `applied`.
- `CONTEXT.md:81-82` — "A **Pool** reaches the **Allowlist** only when its **Application Code** appears in both an **Application** and one of its pool registrations" is now false. Round 1 changed the query to the current registration only (`= MAX(registered_tx_id)`), so a superseded code does not qualify; the glossary line was written before that and never followed. Fix: "its current pool registration".

## Prose

- `src/applications.rs:335-337` — `ContradictoryCodes` says "the chain names more than one code for the pool". Through this query the chain cannot: on the PostgreSQL 17.10 run recorded on metsuke-4zo.52, `DISTINCT` plus `= MAX(registered_tx_id)` leaves one transaction per pool, and `tx_metadata` holds one row per (tx_id, key), so one code. Only the direct `read_registered` tests reach the variant. Keep it — the query is unverified against a real db-sync, so a guard is right — but state it as `read_registered`'s guard against a duplicated answer, and put the reachability question on .52 with the rest.
- Second copies named in round 3 and still here, third time: the `[applications]`-is-optional why (`config.rs:25-29` owns it; `tests/config.rs:31`, `tests/binary.rs:352`), `ApplicationCode`'s form-whitespace and bare-TOML-string whys (`applications.rs:19-22` owns them; `tests/applications.rs:241`, `:248`), `cli.rs:26-29`'s no-archive-credentials why (`tests/binary.rs:337`), and `config.rs:144`'s "nothing at ingest reads it" (`tests/support/mod.rs:105`).
- New second copies: `tests/config.rs:143-145` restates all three `AbsolutePath` field whys that `config.rs:32-33`, `:70-73` and `:75-77` own — "Each of these is `AbsolutePath`." is the whole test doc; the spreadsheet-quoting why, owned by `Cargo.toml:15-17`, copied at `tests/applications.rs:139-140`; and the count-not-a-line-each why, owned by `applications.rs:348-349`, copied at `main.rs:203-204`.
- `tests/support/mod.rs:225-227` — "the shell falls back to a default `PATH` that resolves nothing" is my measurement of this host's `/bin/sh` (`PATH=/no-such-path`), and no artifact records it. A sh defaulting to `/bin:/usr/bin` resolves plenty. Fix: drop "that resolves nothing" and leave the builtins-only statement.
- `tests/applications.rs:325-326` — "the only way it can" is false (a `SET` in `--command` would also work) and "in an environment `Psql` cleared" is unasserted: the double records `PGOPTIONS` and argv, nothing else.

## Recorded, not a finding

`to_toml` emitting bare pairs with no `[ingest.allowlist]` header has now been raised in three rounds, which says the intent is not evident from the code. The reading I take as correct: the emitted bytes are the *value* of `ingest.allowlist`, a whole TOML document that Nix reads with `fromTOML` and assigns — which `the_emitted_pairs_are_a_toml_document_of_their_own` pins. Worth one sentence on `to_toml` so a fourth reader does not ask.

`ingest.allowlist` changing from `HashSet<PoolId>` to a map is a breaking config change carrying a value nothing at ingest reads, but the ticket asks for exactly that: "its output format is the server's allowlist input format by construction". Not scope creep.

Nothing new. metsuke-4zo.52 gains the `ContradictoryCodes` reachability question when that doc is fixed; metsuke-4zo.54 already holds `counters_path` and `archive.root`.

The prose is one pass over the same two test files round 3 asked for; four of those copies are on their third naming, which is the part worth actually finishing rather than carrying to round 5.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 5. Every round-4 item landed. No correctness findings.

Gates run this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 252 passed / 0 failed across 36 targets; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

Verified rather than taken on report: `Gate`'s "every pool either half named is in exactly one of the three" holds. `excluded` holds only applicants; `did_not_apply` filters `!applied.contains_key`, so the two cannot overlap; `read_registered` removes contradicted pools from `codes`, so `codes.keys()` and `contradicted` are disjoint and the `.chain()` cannot double-count; an unreadable row parsed no `PoolId`, so it names no pool and belongs outside the three. `report_gate(&Gate)` takes one argument and `generate_allowlist` copies nothing out.

Six prose items. One is a false claim; the rest are duplication.

- `tests/binary.rs:313-315` — "the two ways of getting one — a mistyped export path and a program nobody joined — look the same in the output" is false. A mistyped path exits through `Fatal::OpenApplications` ("cannot open the applications {path}"), never reaching `NobodyMatched`; the test's own `allowlist_config` writes the file, so that path cannot occur here. Fix: drop the first clause and keep the rest — an allowlist nobody is on stops every upload, so it exits nonzero.
- `tests/binary.rs:351-352` and `tests/config.rs:30-31` — the `[applications]`-is-optional why, owned by `config.rs:25-28`, in both test docs. Fourth naming: rounds 2, 3 and 4 each listed these two, and round 4's pass trimmed the example config instead. Fix: `tests/binary.rs` says "`generate-allowlist` names the missing section"; `tests/config.rs` says the filesystem archive and an absent `[applications]` both load.
- `tests/config.rs:143-145` — enumerates all three per-field whys that `config.rs:32-33`, `:70-73` and `:75-77` own. Third naming. Fix: "Each of these is `AbsolutePath`."
- `tests/applications.rs:138-139` — the spreadsheet-quoting why, owned by `Cargo.toml:15-17`. Second naming.
- `src/applications.rs:398` — "a contradicted pool is absent from `codes`" is now in three places: `:238` owns it on the field, `:373` repeats it, `:398` repeats it again. Fix: `:398` keeps only the part neither of the others gives — `codes` keys and `contradicted` are disjoint, so `.chain()` cannot double-count.
- `tests/applications.rs:318-319` — "the timeout reaches psql the only way it can" overstates twice: `SET statement_timeout` inside `--command` is another route, and "in an environment `Psql` cleared" is unasserted, since the double records `PGOPTIONS` and argv and nothing about what is absent. Fix: "the timeout reaches psql through `PGOPTIONS`".

`tests/support/mod.rs:224-226` now reads "`Psql` clears the environment, so nothing on a `PATH` is there to call". Strictly the shell then invents its own `PATH` — `/no-such-path` on this host, which is why nothing resolves — so the mechanism is still one step off. It is a test helper and the previous wording was worse; not worth a sixth round unless you are editing the line anyway.

## Filed

Nothing new. I corrected my own comment on metsuke-4zo.52, which named `Registered.ignored` — that field became `unreadable` in round 4, and the NULL-code rows land there.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` in sync after the flush, dirty from this round's comments — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. The ticket still has no resolution comment and no close reason; both are yours to write before closing.

## Verdict

Ready for /commit. Nothing above changes behaviour, every gate is green, and all three acceptance criteria have executing evidence. `tests/binary.rs:313-315` is the only item that is wrong rather than merely duplicated, and it is one clause.

comments.text:
Owner agrees the mainnet premise goes, and that the security goal does not. ADR 0010 must argue least privilege on its own terms, not treat the dead premise as licence.

Three ways to reach trace lines, narrowest first:
A. Node StandardOutput=append:<file>, metsuke ReadOnlyPaths that one path, DynamicUser survives. Narrowest, but replaces journal output so operators lose journalctl -u cardano-node, and node 11 has no file backend to tee with.
B. Pipe mode, metsuke as transparent tee. Zero privileges, journald keeps everything, but metsuke then runs inside the node unit alongside the KES and VRF keys.
C. SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal. Own unit, own hardening, no reach to node keys, dies without touching the node. Costs read of every unit's journal (journald has no per-unit ACL). No change to the node unit.

Recommendation: C, with the residual stated in Consequences and A named as the escape hatch.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: docs/adr/0010-log-based-trace-collection.md is drafted in the tree at status proposed, arguing the systemd-journal grant on least-privilege grounds with A/B/C compared. Remaining work is the owner's: accept it, flip ADR 0007's status, update CLAUDE.md's invariant line. .91 and .99 are blocked on that.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Mainnet premise dropped. 0007 superseded by 0010, CLAUDE.md invariant now states the conditional grant. Three status/invariant lines, no new prose.

title: Pipe line source: cardano-node run | metsuke, for hosts without journald
description:
Not every SPO runs systemd/journald; docs/research/openblockperf.md:223 flags the same coupling. metsuke-4zo.91 covers the journald source only.
Same line-source abstraction, stdin as the second implementation. Requires no privileges and no ADR 0010 grant.
Transparent tee: every line read is written through to stdout unchanged, so the operator keeps whatever consumed the node output before.
Must ignore SIGPIPE and survive stdout write failure while still draining stdin. Dying on a closed downstream sends SIGPIPE to cardano-node and takes the block producer with it.
Must never block the node: drop when the spool is full rather than apply backpressure. EOF on stdin means the node exited, so flush and exit.
From the wire-rework spec (metsuke-jfb): the tee thread writes every line through to stdout FIRST, then enqueues on a bounded channel for a parse-and-spool worker. No JSON work ever sits on the node's write path. Drop on a full channel, matching the drop-when-full rule above. Blocked by metsuke-jfb.2 (parse-based selection) and metsuke-jfb.3 (per-line provenance).
close_reason: pipe line source: tee-first, bounded queue, drop-not-block, config-selected

title: Trace batch budget wedges permanently against the server decompress limit
description:
spool outstanding_rows budgets raw line bytes; server max_decompressed_bytes bounds serialized JSON. Lines pay string escaping samples never did: measured 1.1095x on the committed recording.
Both ship at 4194304. rows=12306 raw=4193975 -> json 4653395 -> rejected at decompress. 413 clamps backoff at upload_backoff_max_secs, the batch is deterministic, so the same batch retries daily forever and lines evict oldest-first after one warning.
Triggers at ~6h outage, or ~8min if namespaces is widened. contrib/config.example.toml tells the operator to set exactly the wedging value.
Fix: budget against serialized size, or ship upload_batch_max_bytes well under max_decompressed_bytes.
e2e never catches it: upload_interval_secs=5 never accumulates a full batch.
close_reason: Agent budgets against the bytes the server decompresses

comments.author: claude
comments.text: No second measure to disagree with: the row bytes column holds what the row costs in a sealed body, so the agent budgets against the bytes the server decompresses.

title: Instructions set the trace backend but never pin the node root severity
description:
Every Leios namespace is severity Info, below cardano-node default root threshold. The instructions page step sets only TraceOptions backends.
An SPO whose root severity sits above Notice emits no notice/warning traces either, metsuke selects nothing, and nothing reports it. "All error/warn/notice traces" silently returns a subset.
Fix: the page pins the root severity, not just the two Leios keys.
close_reason: Instructions page pins the node root severity

comments.author: claude
comments.text: The instructions page pins the node's root severity from the agent's own configured floor, checked by the_node_root_severity_comes_from_the_agents_own_floor.

title: Trace loss is invisible in the archive and removes contiguous time windows
description:
Four loss paths, none recorded in any archived object: spool eviction (logtail::drain reports the running total only when the drain ends, which under --follow is never), journald rate limiting, agent restart (--lines=0, no persisted cursor), and a wrong journal_unit that waits forever in silence.
All four remove a contiguous window, oldest-first, which skews a distribution rather than thinning it. The developers compute CDFs off these bytes and cannot tell a complete record from a truncated one.
Counter gaps reveal missing batches; nothing reveals missing lines.
close_reason: won't fix — measurement says four paths never fire and the fifth has no count; ADR 0010 amended, cursor work is 4zo.114

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Two more loss paths from reviewing the uncommitted tree, both invisible for the same reason:

- logsource::JournalSource::drop discards the child's exit status (let _ = kill/wait), so logtail's 'the trace line stream from <unit> ended' cannot distinguish journalctl refused the journal from a unit that does not resolve. Keep the wait status and put it in that warning.
- logselect::severity returns None for a spelling this build does not know, so a node that adds or renames a severity drops those lines from the floor rule with nothing counting them - the highest severities are exactly what the floor exists for. Either ship an unclassifiable line or count it in the drain report.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Third silent path in logtail::run, from the same tree: a JournalSource::spawn failure — journalctl_path wrong, binary absent, group grant missing — is eprintln'd and retried every respawn_backoff_secs forever. It is a startup config error the operator can fix, but start_trace_collection already returns Result<(), StartupError> and main already treats an unopenable spool as fatal, so this is the one such error that never reaches them. Fix: spawn once inside start_trace_collection, propagate as a StartupError, and keep the retry loop only for re-spawns of a stream that once worked.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Won't fix. Built the loss record as a payload line, then measured against it and took it out.

Four of the five loss paths do not occur: log_max_bytes holds weeks of selected lines (retention figure on metsuke-uxw's comments), journald rate limiting is invisible to --output=cat and is prevented in the node's unit, the queue drop is pipe-only, and a node writing the reserved key does not happen. The fifth is a restart, which is a window with no count in it — a record would state a guess. A per-line sequence number was weighed and refused: it costs every line to detect what does not happen.
Against that, a synthetic line puts a rare shape in the stream every consumer reads, which is what a columnar reader handles worst (metsuke-4zo.112). No collector does this: Prometheus, Fluent Bit, Vector and Filebeat keep loss out of band, and Filebeat answers restart loss with a persisted cursor.
So: operator learns loss from the agent's counters (metsuke-4zo.109), the program from absence in the bucket (metsuke-4zo.110), and the restart gap gets closed rather than described (metsuke-4zo.114). Large gaps stay visible as holes in the lines' own timestamps; small ones are not worth a shape.
Kept from the attempt: journalctl's exit status in the stream-ended warning, and a stream that cannot be opened is now a StartupError instead of a retry forever. ADR 0010's consequences record the decision.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree (report only, nothing edited).

## Correctness and intent

- crates/metsuke/src/main.rs:186, logtail.rs:26-30, logsource.rs:64-67, docs/adr/0010:148-151 — all four say a journal this agent may not read is now a startup failure. It is not: `JournalSource::spawn` fails only when `Command::spawn` fails (exec/ENOENT), so a journalctl that execs and is then refused the journal exits non-zero afterwards and lands in the respawn loop exactly as before. Fix: narrow the claim at all four sites to a journalctl that cannot exec. The detection half is filed (metsuke-4zo.116).
- crates/metsuke/src/logsource.rs:139-149 — `end` calls `try_wait` after the reader saw EOF, but a child closes stdout before it becomes reapable, so `try_wait` can answer `None`, the code then kills it, and the warning reports `signal: 9` in place of the status the ticket asked to keep. Fix: blocking `wait()` on the EOF path, `try_wait`+kill only for a stream still following.
- crates/metsuke/tests/logsource.rs:63-79 — `a_stream_still_running_is_ended_and_says_so` races and can only fail. Its stand-in is `exec cat` over leios-node-traces-startup.log, 46063 bytes, under Linux's 64 KiB pipe buffer: the `cat` can write everything and exit 0 before `end()` runs, giving "journalctl exited without an error" and no "signal". Fix: a stand-in that cannot exit (`while :; do sleep 1; done`).
- crates/metsuke/src/logsource.rs:79-80 — the comment states the inverse of its branch. A killed child reports a signal, so `success()` is unreachable from the kill path; it is reachable only from a journalctl that exited 0 itself. Fix: delete it.
- crates/metsuke/src/logsource.rs:133-138 — `end(&mut self)` makes a second call representable and answers it with a fabricated `io::Error` under a variant documented as "waiting for the child failed". Fix: `pub fn end(mut self) -> ChildEnd`; logtail.rs:64 drops the source right after, and the branch and its invented error go.

## Standards and reuse

- crates/metsuke/tests/logsource.rs:84-95 — `refusing_journalctl` repeats support/mod.rs:53-67 byte for byte (shebang write, `0o755` chmod). Fix: one `sh_stand_in(dir, name, body)` in support/mod.rs, both callers through it.
- crates/metsuke/src/logsource.rs:66 vs tests/logsource.rs:47 — the doc says a refused journal is "exit 1", the test picks 13, and no fixture records either. Fix: drop the digit, or record journalctl's refusal.
- scripts/report.nu:349-350 — "Only what git knows about is read. A change this test has to see is a change that is at least staged." Wrong for tracked files: nix reads a dirty tree's tracked files from disk, so unstaged edits are seen. Only new files are invisible. Fix: say a *new* file must be tracked.

## Prose

- docs/adr/0010:118-145 and the 2026-08-27 close comment on this ticket are the same argument sentence for sentence — five paths, the refused sequence number, the columnar shape, the Prometheus/Fluent Bit/Vector/Filebeat survey, counters/absence/cursor. The ADR owns an accepted decision. Fix: cut the comment to the two kept behaviours plus a pointer, and trim the ADR entry, which is 28 lines for one consequence.
- The startup-failure why is written four times: main.rs:45-47 (the variant doc, which owns it), main.rs:185-188, logtail.rs:26-30, docs/adr/0010:148-151. Fix: keep the variant doc, delete main.rs:185-188, trim logtail.rs to the sentence the ADR lacks.
- Restatement: logsource.rs:57-58 restates `Option<Child>` + `take()`, :71-72 restates the variant name, :128 restates the signature; tests/logsource.rs:42-44 and :63-64 restate their own test names and the assert messages below them. Fix: delete; keep the `try_wait`-order why at :130-132.

## Scope

- scripts/report.nu:339-353 (`path:devnet` to `.?dir=devnet`) is unrelated to this ticket. Split it out or name the ticket that owns it.

## Gates run

`nu scripts/report.nu cargo` — ok, 362 passed, 0 ignored, 39 binaries, 4.15s. Both new tests pass today; two of them pass by scheduling, per the findings above. `just check`, `just vm`, `just e2e` not run in this session.

## Beads hygiene

No untracked files. Resolution comment and close reason both present on this ticket. `.beads/issues.jsonl` staged and unstaged both dirty — the flush is clean (`br sync --flush-only`: nothing to export), stage it with the code. The map is a build epic with no `## Decisions so far` section, so nothing owed there.

## Filed

Filed metsuke-4zo.115, metsuke-4zo.116.

## Verdict

Not ready for /commit: the four-site startup-failure claim is false, two new tests pass only by scheduling, and logsource.rs:79-80 documents the opposite of its branch.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Re-review of the fixed tree. Every finding from the previous report is closed; one dead reference is left, and the new retry checks out.

## Closed

- The four-site startup-failure claim: `main.rs:45-49` now owns it and states only the exec case, naming 4zo.116 for the other. `logtail.rs:26-30` and `docs/adr/0010:134-138` point at the owner. Correct against the code.
- `reap(self)`/`stop(self)`: the EOF path blocks on `wait()` with no kill, so it reports the status the child chose; `stop` kills first. `logtail::run` picks on `DrainEnd`, and the spool-failure path leaves the child to `Drop`. Consuming `self` deletes the double call and the fabricated `io::Error`; the `taken()` expect is unreachable from outside the file.
- `exec sleep 3600` cannot exit, so the race is gone. `exec` also means the killed pid is the sleep, not an orphaning shell.
- The inverted comment and the `success()` arm are both gone; `ExitStatus`'s Display carries "exit status: 13" and "signal: 9 (SIGKILL)", which is what the two tests assert.
- `sh_stand_in` is the one writer. The "exit 1" digit is dropped and the test says 13 is arbitrary.
- `report.nu:348-349` is now accurate: tracked edits are read from disk staged or not, only a never-seen file is invisible.
- ADR consequence is 13 lines, no digit, pointers only.

## Left

- crates/metsuke/src/logsource.rs:178 — the `Drop` doc says "A source `end` already reaped holds no child to wind up." `end` no longer exists; it is `reap` and `stop`. Fix: name both, or cut the sentence — `Option<Child>` and the field doc at :57 already carry it.

## The new retry

`support/mod.rs:74-96` retries `ExecutableFileBusy` up to 50 times at 20 ms and panics on exhaustion, so it cannot exhaust silently, and the justification is at the site. The diagnosis is right: between `fork` and `exec` the child holds the write fd of a file a sibling thread just wrote, and `O_CLOEXEC` only closes it at the exec — so the window is real and is the harness racing itself, not the source. Confined to tests, one place, no finding.

## Gates, re-run in this session

- `just test` — ok, 362 passed, 0 ignored, 39 binaries, 4.33s
- `just check` — ok, 16 derivations, 23.65s
- `just vm` — ok, 7 subtests, 17.83s
- `just e2e` — ok, 11 subtests, 46.48s

All four match what the implementer reported.

## Beads hygiene

No untracked files; the whole change is staged, which is what `just e2e` reads. metsuke-4zo.115 and .116 are open, parented to metsuke-4zo, labelled `to-issues:build`. The 2026-08-27 close comment on this ticket still duplicates the argument the ADR now owns; `br comments` has no edit, so it stands as history — accepted, the ADR is the short authoritative copy.

## Verdict

Green for `/commit` once logsource.rs:178 is corrected — a one-line doc fix, no re-run needed. `scripts/report.nu` belongs to 4zo.113, so two commits.

title: Server pushes additional trace namespaces on ACK, bounded by local roots
description:
Node updates change namespaces; pushing config to every SPO to follow is coordination we do not want. Ack already carries latest_version (ADR 0006), so it is the established server-to-client channel.
Security bound is not optional: under ADR 0010 the agent holds systemd-journal and can read every unit journal on the host. The ns filter is the only thing scoping that. An unbounded server-pushed pattern turns a compromised ingest server into remote read of every SPO system journal.
Fix: local config sets namespace_roots; a pushed ns is accepted only if it is under one, otherwise refused and logged. severity_floor stays local.
Prefix match only. A regex arriving over the wire is a DoS primitive across the whole fleet.
Rules persist in the spool so a restart does not drop to bare config; local config is the floor when the server is unreachable. Needs an ADR: this changes who decides what an agent collects.

title: Extract wire contract into metsuke-wire crate
description: crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs is the wire contract; metsuke-server depends on the whole agent crate for it. Every future agent dep (HTTP, rusqlite, SNTP) becomes a server dep transitively, against least-privilege, and ADR 0006 independent versioning forces server manifest churn per client tag. Fix: move envelope.rs into a metsuke-wire crate both binaries depend on. Deliberately deferred from metsuke-4zo.1 review: do it when the first heavy agent dependency lands (metsuke-4zo.2/.4).
close_reason: wire contract extracted to metsuke-wire; server off the agent crate

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Trigger fired: metsuke-4zo.2 added ureq (+ its tree) to the metsuke lib, so metsuke-server now pulls it transitively. Extraction is due.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Trigger fired: rusqlite (bundled sqlite) landed in metsuke via metsuke-4zo.4, so metsuke-server now links it transitively. Review of .4 endorses the wire-crate option over a feature gate.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
More cross-crate duplication for the extraction to absorb, found reviewing metsuke-4zo.16:

- journald severity prefixes: crates/metsuke/src/main.rs ERR/WARNING/INFO (private) vs crates/metsuke-server/src/lib.rs ERR/WARNING/INFO — byte-identical.
- lowercase hex encode: metsuke/src/uploader.rs `fn hex` (private) vs metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs `fn hex` — byte-identical.
- hex decode, three shapes: metsuke/src/keys.rs `decode_seed`, metsuke/tests/support/mod.rs `decode_hex`, metsuke-server/src/http.rs `decode_hex<const N>` (the best-shaped of the three).
- `Args::parse` loop: metsuke/src/cli.rs vs metsuke-server/src/cli.rs — same shape; the client's `value()` helper already generalises the flag-value case.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree. No untracked files; everything is staged. Gate: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{test,clippy,treefmt,deny,audit}` all built green.

## Intent

Extraction itself is complete and correct. metsuke-server no longer depends on metsuke; envelope.rs and sqlite.rs moved byte-identical; journal prefixes and hex are unified. build.rs matches ADR 0006 ("the client crate's version read from the workspace at server compile time") and tests/version.rs guards it.

- crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs:282-299 — hex()/unhex() were not folded into metsuke_wire::hex, so the tree ships two hex decoders with different strictness: unhex() has no is_ascii_hexdigit pre-check, so u8::from_str_radix accepts a '+' pair ("+f" -> 15) that hex::decode rejects. Also s3.rs:285 'Mirrors the header decoder in `http`' is now false — http.rs delegates. Fix: hex::encode at s3.rs:164-165, hex::decode::<N> at s3.rs:258-260 mapping HexError into the local String refusal, delete both fns. Tracked in metsuke-4zo.23, commented there.
- cli.rs value() dedup, named in comment 3 of this ticket, is untouched. Already metsuke-4zo.23's, commented.

## Standards

- CLAUDE.md:24 — "`crates/metsuke-wire` is what the two agree on, and the only crate either depends on" is false. metsuke-server declares 10 other direct deps (rusqlite, rusty-s3, serde, serde_json, thiserror, time, tiny_http, toml, ureq, url) plus a toml build-dep; metsuke declares 7. Fix: drop the second clause.
- metsuke-wire holds journal.rs and sqlite.rs, neither of which is anything the two sides agree on over the wire, and pulls rusqlite bundled. No leak (the server links rusqlite directly anyway), but the crate's name and its lib.rs header both claim narrower than its contents. Fix: reword, or split. Reword is the recommendation.

## Silent failures

- crates/metsuke/src/keys.rs:75 — `hex::decode::<32>(digits).ok()` throws away HexError::WrongLength{found, expected}, which hex.rs was written to carry, so a truncated key file reports NotAnEd25519Seed with no byte count. Fix: `#[source] HexError` on the variant and map_err instead of .ok().

## Prose

- crates/metsuke-server/build.rs:1-2 — first sentence narrates what main() does. Drop it, keep the ADR-0006 clause.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs:79-80 — the new doc says only what the four-line match does, replacing a doc that carried a real why (the uppercase-accepted rationale, which correctly moved to hex.rs). Fix: state why the wrapper exists (HexError doesn't know which header) or delete.
- The dependency-leak why appears three times: metsuke-wire/src/lib.rs:1-4 (owner), CLAUDE.md:24, build.rs:3-4. Cut the other two to pointers.
- crates/metsuke-wire/src/hex.rs:1 'Hex for the upload headers' — keys.rs now decodes a cardano-cli seed through it, which is not a header.

## Discarded

build.rs and tests/version.rs both parsing ../metsuke/Cargo.toml is the point of the test, not duplication. flake.nix version="0" is crane derivation naming only, no ADR 0006 conflict.

## Verdict

Not ready: 7 in-scope fixes above, none structural. Also `git add .beads/` — this review's comments dirtied issues.jsonl.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. Gate re-run this session: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{test,clippy,treefmt,deny,audit}` -> exit 0.

All seven round-1 fixes verified in the tree. The keys.rs split plus its three new tests is a better outcome than what I asked for — the malformed-seed path had no coverage at all. Keeping `unhex` as a message adapter is right; it now mirrors `number` beside it.

Two findings, both from round 1's own edits.

- crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs:283 — the rewrite dropped `{text:?}`, so a refusal no longer says what it got: `"{header} is not {N} bytes of hex: {error}"` against the old `{text:?}`. CLAUDE.md ## Code: 'a message naming what failed and what it got'. The length case also states the expectation twice ('is not 32 bytes of hex: decodes to 31 bytes, expected 32'), since HexError already carries it. Fix: `format!("{header} is not hex: {error} ({text:?})")`.
- metsuke-4zo.39 carries `to-issues:build`, but its title is 'Decide whether…' and its body recommends wont-do. That label puts it on the implement frontier, where the next agent builds the thing the ticket argues against. Fix: relabel `needs-decision`.

On the cli.rs deferral: accepted, no overrule. Two grammars and two ArgsError shapes reduce the shared part to one stdlib call, and a wire module around it deletes no logic.

Verdict: one code fix (s3.rs message) and one label change. Nothing structural.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Extracted crates/metsuke-wire (envelope, sqlite, hex, journal); metsuke-server no longer depends on metsuke. Server reads the agent version via build.rs + CLIENT_VERSION per ADR 0006, cross-checked by tests/version.rs. Shared hex replaced four copies and tightened decode (from_str_radix accepted a sign pair). cli.rs value() dedup declined and closed as metsuke-4zo.39.

title: Slow request body stalls all ingest
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs: serve() reads bodies on the accepting thread and tiny_http 0.12 exposes no socket timeout (ServerConfig is addr+ssl only; Request hands out no stream), so one client trickling a body blocks every pool until it gives up. read_body bounds size, not time.

Fix: front the server with a proxy that fully buffers request bodies, and bind loopback. Belongs with metsuke-4zo.12, which owns the NixOS modules and the hardened unit. If the endpoint is ever exposed directly, tiny_http has to go.
close_reason: hyper replaces tiny_http; both failure modes bounded in the server's own code (metsuke-jfb.6)

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Same root cause, second cost: memory, not just time.

Any path that answers without reading the body (413 by Content-Length, 404, 405, header-decode 400) leaves the remainder unread, and tiny_http's EqualReader::drop drains it with a single `vec![0; remaining]` sized by the *declared* Content-Length (util/equal_reader.rs:66-85; the >1024 branch at request.rs:215). Request::drop runs it on the serving thread, and no public Request method lets you skip it (upgrade/into_writer/respond all drop self).

Measured, debug build, one header-only POST declaring Content-Length: 4000000000, answered 400: VmSize 347544 kB -> 4253796 kB, freed when the client closed. RSS stays ~4 MB (calloc zero pages) until the attacker actually sends bytes.

Consequence: under the hardened unit's MemoryMax/LimitAS (metsuke-4zo.12) this aborts the process. Fix is the same proxy body cap this ticket already names; the cap has to be enforced *before* the request reaches tiny_http.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Fixed by metsuke-jfb.6: hyper replaces tiny_http. A declared Content-Length over max_body_bytes is refused before a byte is read and the Incoming is dropped unread, so nothing allocates what a client named; read_timeout_secs bounds the whole body, which is what a trickle renews past; every connection is its own task behind a connection cap. The two failure modes are tests/binary.rs a_declared_body_far_over_the_cap_neither_allocates_nor_stalls and a_body_that_trickles_is_cut_off_at_the_read_timeout.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Correction to the comment above: the trickle test is tests/binary.rs a_body_that_keeps_trickling_is_cut_off_at_the_read_timeout — it has to keep sending, because a body that merely stops is refused by a per-read deadline too. The allocation half is a_declared_body_far_over_the_cap_neither_allocates_nor_stalls, which reads VmPeak: an allocation made and freed while answering is gone from VmSize before the answer lands.

title: Agent panics on an https upload URL: ureq has no TLS provider
description:
crates/metsuke/Cargo.toml pins ureq with default-features = false, so no TLS feature is on: cargo tree -p metsuke -e features shows no rustls. ureq 3.4.0 panics on an https URI when the provider feature is off (ureq-3.4.0/src/unversioned/transport/mod.rs:485, "uri scheme is https ... feature is not enabled"). TLS is a hard requirement (docs/research/endpoint-protection.md, Transport).

Masked in the workspace: metsuke-server now takes ureq with defaults, and feature unification hands the agent rustls whenever both crates build together. An agent-only static build (metsuke-4zo.12) would not get it.

Fix: enable rustls on the agent ureq too, or bound the upload URL to https at config load and fail loudly there.
close_reason: agent ureq carries rustls; test-agent gate guards it

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing metsuke-b4r. Three files, all staged, no untracked files.

## The ticket's own premise is wrong, and the diff's comment is right

metsuke-b4r says ureq 3.4.0 *panics* on an https URI with no provider feature. It does not, in this configuration. `WarnOnMissingTlsProvider` is chained only under `#[cfg(feature = "_tls")]` (ureq-3.4.0/src/unversioned/transport/mod.rs:381-395), and `_tls` arrives only via `rustls-no-provider` or `native-tls-no-default`, neither of which `default-features = false` turns on. `TcpConnector` opens a plain socket, then run.rs:404-407 returns `Error::TlsRequired`, which uploader.rs:45 maps to `Retryable`. Observed directly: run at HEAD, the new test sees a TCP connection carrying zero bytes and no panic.

So the Cargo.toml comment is accurate as written and needs no change. What needs correcting is the ticket body, in the resolution comment.

The fix itself is verified: `cargo tree -p metsuke -e features` now shows rustls + ring + webpki-roots.

## In-scope fixes

title: A public verification key can spend an allowlisted pool's upload window
description:
intake::submit charged the limiter before it checked the signature, so what a submission claimed decided whose budget it spent. A pool's cold verification key is public: it travels in the headers of every submission that pool sends, and it sits in the witness set of the pool registration transaction that put the pool on chain. Anyone can therefore present an allowlisted pool's key over garbage bodies and empty that pool's window without holding anything secret.

At the shipped rate_limit_uploads of 100 an hour that takes about a second, and the pool's own agent then reads 429 for the rest of the window. Enough keys does the same to rate_limit_uploads_total and refuses the whole allowlist at once, which reaches every pool as Rejection::ServerBusy over traffic that was not theirs. metsuke-n8t is what the agent then did with those 429s.

Fix: verify before charging. The order becomes container, allowlist, signature, limiter, archive. A forged body still costs one Ed25519 verify, which is what the allowlist check in front of it bounds to keys that are on the list, and it costs the pool named by that key nothing.
close_reason: the signature is checked before the limiter is charged, so only bodies the pool signed spend its window

title: Two test suites carry their own copy of the attesting archive stub
description:
metsuke-fetch's tests/support carries an Attesting archive that answers the two metadata headers beside an object, and metsuke-server's tests/http.rs carries an Attested one that does the same thing for the same reason: a filesystem archive discards the pair at ingest, so neither suite could otherwise exercise the path where a download is checkable. Both were written the same night (metsuke-d4h and metsuke-s9r) and neither knows about the other.

That is metsuke-jfb.33's case again, narrower and fresh: two stubs whose only contract is "answer what S3 would", drifting independently the next time the archive traits move.

Fix: one of them, reachable from both. A test-only feature on metsuke-server that exports the wrapper is the obvious shape, since metsuke-fetch already dev-depends on that crate. Whether that is worth a feature flag against just letting the two sit is the decision this needs.

title: Bump workspace to Rust edition 2024
description: Cargo.toml workspace.package pins edition 2021; toolchain is rustc 1.97 and committed style is already rustfmt style_edition 2024 (treefmt), so cargo fmt disagrees with the repo. Fix: edition = "2024" in Cargo.toml, re-run gates.
close_reason: edition 2024 in workspace Cargo.toml; envelope seal check rewritten as let-chain; gates green

title: A filesystem archive produces a corpus nobody can ever check, and nothing says so
description:
ArchiveConfig offers Filesystem alongside S3, and the nix module exposes it as archive.filesystem. FilesystemArchive::store writes submission.wire_bytes and drops submission.vkey and submission.signature on the floor, so the pair is gone at ingest rather than merely unserved. No later route can answer it, metsuke-server verify-archive refuses outright on that backend (Fatal::CannotVerifyFilesystem), and metsuke-fetch counts every object it serves as unverifiable.

So a deployment that picks the filesystem backend produces an archive nobody can ever check, and nothing says so: not the config, not the startup log, not the nix module. ADR 0005 says S3 is what production runs, which is the decision, but the code offers the other one without comment.

Fix: say it where an operator would see it. A line in the startup log naming what that backend gives up is the cheapest; a nix assertion or a warning on the module option is the firmer one. Deleting the backend is not it: the config test and local development both use it.
close_reason: the server warns at startup naming the archive and what it drops, and the nix module warns at eval; the backend stays, since the config test and single-host development both use it

title: Wire format rework and server simplification
description:
* * * Rebuild the wire format as a zstd skippable-frame container (self-describing, duckdb-readable) and
strip the server to a stateless pipe: allowlist, cold-key verify, PUT. Fixes multi-machine data loss
(replay refusal, key collisions), removes Calidus/db-sync/SQLite, swaps tiny_http for hyper. Spec
was ephemeral; the durable record is the code.

## Decisions so far

- The container is a skippable frame (0x184D2A50, u32le length, plaintext JSON header) then a zstd
  data frame of JSON Lines, one detached Ed25519 signature over both. Header reads with no key and
  no decompressor. Both crates switched at once — no compatibility story, the bucket does not exist
  yet (jfb.1).
- max_header_bytes is a required [ingest] field, not a defaulted one: config.rs takes no defaults
  (jfb.1).
- Trace-line selection parses the line and reads the object's top level, rather than scanning for
  "ns":" and "sev":". The substring readers needed a first-occurrence and a last-occurrence rule,
  which was an unenforced claim about the node's key order. Every line the parse refuses declares
  neither field and is not selected; the distinct failures are one bucket. ADR 0010 amended
  (jfb.2).
- agent_id is a Header field, so identity on the wire is pool plus machine. jfb.4 keys objects by
  both, and a per-agent sequence number only reads if the header says which agent counted (jfb.3).
- A spooled row this build cannot read back is deleted and reported, not propagated: the parse
  refuses it every tick, so failing the tick stalls the stream behind one row until the byte cap
  catches up. Same trade as the over-budget head row (jfb.3).
- Provenance is stamped on the way into the spool, so a stored row is the line it will be on the
  wire and nothing deserializes it back. Supersedes the bullet above: no row is read back, so there
  is no row this build cannot read. Per-line provenance narrows to pool plus agent — the counter is
  drawn per batch and an unacked row is re-sealed into a later one, so a push-time counter would be
  wrong, not merely unknown. It and the batch timestamp stay in the header frame (jfb.11).

- Objects are keyed `v1/<date>/<uuid7>-<pool>-<agent>-<metrics|logs>.jsonl.zst`. The date is the
  server's receipt day, read back out of the id so the folder and the object cannot name two days;
  the pool derives from the verifying key, never a request header; uniqueness is the UUIDv7 alone.
  Object metadata narrows to the vkey and the signature, the two facts not inside the signed bytes
  (ADR 0005 amended, ADR 0002 deleted). The kind segment is named from the schema version, which
  leaves one version gate on the accepted path (jfb.4).
- That version gate stays, and is not schema gating. The key scheme needs a `<metrics|logs>`
  segment and a version this build has no `Kind` for has none, so accepting it would mean
  inventing a segment for data nothing downstream can read. `Rejection::UnnameableKind` is
  renamed `KeylessSchema`, so the refusal names the key having no name rather than the schema
  (jfb.18).
- Trace lines reach the agent from the source `[log].source` names, journald or the node's own
  stdout, behind one `LineSource`. It is required with no default: an agent that guessed would
  collect nothing or tee nothing and say neither. The pipe holds no group at all, so only the
  journal costs what ADR 0010 prices, and the NixOS module renders journald alone because the
  unit it writes has no node upstream of it (metsuke-4zo.95).


- Trace selection reads `ns` and nothing else; the severity floor is deleted. A namespace's severity
  is assigned by the node's own TraceOptions, so a floor selects a set that depends on the
  operator's config. The severity ask is dropped, not answered another way: every distribution the
  program asked for is already a namespace in the shipped default, so the floor added no measurement
  line, and what it added was error/warning/notice lines from namespaces nobody named. The
  node-config step names every namespace the node must emit for the agent's rules to select
  anything, each with its own severity, so it holds under whatever root threshold an operator has.
  ADR 0010 amended (jfb.19).
- The published pre-production node config is recorded at nix/fixtures/ and the e2e node's tracing
  is that recording, not the demo's, so the instructions page's snippets are merged into what SPOs
  actually run. The page's step-4 mechanism claim stays out of the page: an operator needs the
  instruction, and nothing here verifies another project's backend resolution order (jfb.20, jfb.21).
- The e2e node forges, on the demo pool's keys with the guest clock set to the genesis era. That is
  what makes the two block-adoption namespaces observable, and it avoids a fourth copy of the
  genesis restamp metsuke-4zo.60 already counts three of (jfb.20).
- Authority is cold-key-only and the server is stateless. Calidus resolution, db-sync and the
  SQLite index are deleted, with ADRs 0003/0008/0009; ADR 0005 keeps only the raw-signed-bytes
  half. The listing route is one ListObjectsV2 passing the client's prefix and start-after
  through, clamped to S3's 1000-key page, so `truncated` is the endpoint's answer and not a row
  count. The object route drops its existence pre-check and passes the bucket's 404 through.
  Restarting loses only the in-memory rate-limit windows (jfb.5).
- An absent listing prefix becomes `v1/`, not the empty string: "everything" is every object this
  server filed, never every key in the bucket. The GLOB-metacharacter refusal goes with SQLite —
  a prefix is a literal at both archive kinds now (jfb.5).
- The transport is hyper on a single-threaded tokio runtime, with every archive touch on the
  blocking pool. Routing takes a decoded `http::Request` and returns an `http::Answer`; no HTTP
  type reaches it. A new `[http]` table holds the idle, read and write timeouts and the
  connection cap, required like every other field. A body is read for the submit route alone and
  only once its headers decode. The download hands the archive's reader through rather than
  buffering. An accept failure about one connection is logged and skipped; anything else exits to
  systemd (jfb.6).
- A download states a `Content-Length` or is refused. The archive hands back a length, not an
  optional one: a chunked answer would put the server's copy granularity on the wire as a frame
  size, and an endpoint that will not state a length cannot be served off at all. S3 states one
  on every GetObject, so this is a requirement on `endpoint`, named there and in the shipped
  example, and reported as its own `ArchiveError::EndpointUnusable` (jfb.6).
- The fetch tool is its own crate (`crates/metsuke-fetch`), and its whole delta-sync protocol is one
  start-after cursor in a local state file. The state file holds the prefix and the pool/agent/kind
  selection beside the key, and a read under any other filters is refused rather than reset: a run
  advances the cursor past every key it saw, downloaded or filtered out, so the same cursor read
  wider would skip objects it never fetched. Selection is read off the key client-side, so narrowing
  a listing costs no download. Objects land under their key verbatim, which is what keeps them
  signature-checkable and duckdb-readable with no unpacking step (jfb.8).

Decision amended (metsuke-jfb.19): trace selection reads `ns` and nothing else. The severity floor is deleted from logselect, config, the example config, the instructions page and the NixOS module.

Why: the node's TraceOptions assigns severity per namespace — the config SPOs run (book.world.dev.cardano.org/environments-pre/leios/config.json) sets a root of Notice plus ~20 overrides including 'Silence' — so a floor selects a config-dependent set. title: Wire container: skippable-frame header + zstd data frame, both crates switched
description:
## What to build

A submission becomes exactly one zstd skippable frame (magic 0x184D2A50, u32le length, JSON header) followed by one zstd data frame (compressed JSON Lines), with a single detached Ed25519 signature over the whole byte sequence, verified with verify_strict. Header fields: schema version, pool id, agent id, agent version, sequence number, timestamp. The header is readable by seeking 8 bytes in with no decompressor; every conforming zstd tool (incl. duckdb read_json_auto) ignores the skippable frame and reads the payload — verified duckdb v1.5.2 / zstd 1.5.7 during design.

Both the agent (seal) and server (open) switch in this one ticket, because there is no compatibility story — the bucket does not exist yet. Existing server gates (replay, skew, schema) keep operating off the new header fields so CI stays green; their removal is a later ticket.

Header length is bounded by a max_header_bytes configuration value, default 4 KiB. A body not beginning with the skippable-frame magic, or declaring a header longer than the bound, is refused with 400 before anything else happens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Seal produces a byte sequence whose first frame is a skippable frame with the expected magic and length
- [ ] Open recovers the header without decompressing (seek 8 bytes, no zstd)
- [ ] A mutated byte anywhere in the file fails verification
- [ ] A body without the magic is refused; a header exceeding the bound is refused
- [ ] max_header_bytes is configuration, surfaced as a NixOS module option
- [ ] Committed fixture produced by the real sealing path, plus a test shelling out to `zstd -d` asserting it emits exactly the payload (recording, not assertion; re-record to detect drift)
- [ ] Agent seals the new container; server opens it; e2e VM test stays green

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: Skippable-frame header plus zstd data frame, both crates switched

The e2e VM test was NOT run.

### Intent

- crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs:194 — `/// Cap on the compressed body.` on `max_body_bytes`, which now caps header frame plus data frame
- crates/metsuke-server/tests/intake.rs:295 — `// The compressed body is capped before anything touches it.`

Fix: say "the wire body" or "the body as sent" at all three, matching the ADR's wording.

title: Stamp provenance on the way into the spool, so nothing deserializes a stored row
description:
Rows go into SQLite already stamped, so the read path stops deserializing them.

`Spool::push` writes `serde_json::to_string(sample)`, `Spool::readable` parses it back to a
`Sample`, and `payload_lines` serializes that `Sample` straight out again — text in, identical
text out. The only thing the round trip contributes is a way to fail: a `Sample` field that stops
being `Option`, a changed serde format, or a `TraceLine` that starts holding the reserved key makes
every stored row refuse, and `readable` deletes every row it reads with no per-tick bound. ADR 0004
makes the spool the only durability layer, so a deserialization regression drains it at upload
cadence behind one stderr line per tick.

The stamp moves to the write side: a row is stored as the line it will be on the wire, and taking a
batch concatenates rows with newlines. No parse, so no regression can refuse a stored row.

Per-line provenance narrows to `{pool_id, agent_id}`, the two values known at push. The counter is
drawn per batch in `delivery::Delivery::seal` and a row whose PUT fails is re-sealed into a later
batch with a different one, so a push-time counter would be wrong rather than merely unknown. Both
it and the batch timestamp stay in the header frame, inside the signed bytes (ADR 0002).
`nix/e2e-test.nix` already asserts only these two fields per line.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Spool::outstanding`/`outstanding_lines` hand back stored text; `Spool::readable`,
      `UncarriableReport::unreadable` and `unreadable_reason` are gone
- [ ] `Provenance` is `{pool_id, agent_id}`; `open` checks a line against the header on those
- [ ] `RowBudget::per_row_bytes` and `envelope::provenance_bytes` are gone — the stored `bytes` is
      the row's wire cost, measured once (closes metsuke-jfb.9)
- [ ] `TraceLine`'s reserved-key refusal happens before the row is written, not on read
- [ ] Both `.hex` fixtures re-recorded; ADR 0002 and ADR 0010 state where provenance lives now
- [ ] A test asserts a `Sample` field change cannot make a stored row unreadable
close_reason: spool stores wire lines; read-path deserialization gone

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Scope decided with the user: not a per-tick bound. The read-path deserialization goes away instead, so the regression class is unrepresentable rather than bounded.

Forced consequence, verified in the tree: the counter cannot be stamped at push. delivery.rs:167 draws it inside seal, one per batch, and an unacked row is re-sealed into a later batch with a different one. Per-line provenance is {pool_id, agent_id}; counter and timestamp stay in the header frame. nix/e2e-test.nix:363-364 already asserts only those two per line.

Alternative offered and declined: a per-row counter drawn at push. Finer gap detection, but a third redefinition of the counter this epic and an ADR 0002 rewrite.

Not in scope: dropping sync_progress. Decided separately on metsuke-ixn.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Rows go into the spool as the wire line (`envelope::PayloadLine`), stamped with {pool_id, agent_id} at push. Read path deletes: `Spool::readable`, `UncarriableReport::unreadable`, `unreadable_reason`, `RowBudget::per_row_bytes`, `envelope::provenance_bytes`. `PayloadLine::wire_bytes` is now the single place a row's wire cost is computed, so the stored `bytes` and a batch's budget cannot disagree (closes metsuke-jfb.9). TraceLine's reserved-key refusal moved to push. Counter and timestamp stay in the header frame (ADR 0002) because seal draws the counter per batch. Both .hex fixtures re-recorded; ADR 0002 and 0010 state where provenance lives. Filed metsuke-jfb.16 (migration drops pre-stamp backlog silently) and metsuke-jfb.17 (stamp-less row stalls its stream).

title: logselect drops a node line that carries a metsuke key with no trace of it
description:
crates/metsuke/src/logselect.rs, `select`: `let Ok(line) = TraceLine::parse(line) else { return Selection::Skip }` discards the refusal.

`TraceLineError::ReservedKey` is not malformation — it is a well-formed node line whose top level happens to hold `metsuke`. jfb.2 put malformed lines in one bucket; this one is silent data loss with no counter and no log.

Fix: count `ReservedKey` refusals separately and surface them the way `UncarriableReport` is surfaced.
close_reason: implemented, nix flake check green

title: Envelope and Header should hold a Provenance field, not four loose ones
description:
crates/metsuke-wire/src/envelope.rs: `pool_id`, `agent_id`, `counter`, `timestamp` travel together through `Envelope`, `Header` and `Provenance`, and `Header::of` copies them field by field into a fourth place.

`Envelope::new` is six positional args; adding `agent_id` forced edits at ~15 call sites across both crates and every test support module.

Fix: `Envelope { provenance, agent_version, payload }`, so `Header::provenance` is a field read and the `agent_version` clone in `Header::of` goes.
close_reason: implemented, nix flake check green

title: CONTEXT.md has no Agent term, and the diff names the concept four ways
description:
CONTEXT.md defines no Agent or Agent ID entry, while `AgentId` is now a wire field stamped on every archived line.

New prose names the same thing "machine" (contrib/config.example.toml, delivery.rs), "agent" (identity.rs), "host" (identity.rs), "relay" (fixtures). CONTEXT.md Relationships still implies a Pool reports once.

Fix: add Agent and Agent ID under Reporting with an Avoid list picking one of machine/host, plus "a Pool may report from many Agents".
close_reason: CONTEXT.md already carries the Agent terms

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
metsuke-jfb.5 added Agent, Agent ID, Frame and Sequence Number to CONTEXT.md, plus the
'a Pool may report from many Agents' relationship and a two-relay dialogue. What is left here is
the prose sweep: contrib/config.example.toml, delivery.rs and identity.rs still say machine/host,
fixtures say relay.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Already done: CONTEXT.md carries Agent, Agent ID, the Avoid list (machine/host/relay/node) and 'a Pool may run several', added in 034ed18.

title: push_capped runs the eviction sweep on every single row push
description:
crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs, `push_capped` (pre-existing): the window-function `DELETE ... WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT ... SUM(bytes) OVER ...)` scans the whole table on every push, whether or not the table is anywhere near `max_bytes`, and both SQL strings are re-formatted and re-prepared each call.

This is the per-trace-line hot path.

Fix: `Connection::prepare_cached` for both statements, and gate the sweep on the table total exceeding `max_bytes`.
close_reason: implemented, nix flake check green

title: Migration discards the whole pre-stamp spool backlog with no count and no log line
description:
The v3 migration in `spool::MIGRATIONS` deletes every row lacking a `$.metsuke` stamp. `metsuke_wire::sqlite::migrate` returns `()`, so no count reaches the caller and `Spool::open` prints nothing: an operator upgrading a node with a backlog loses it silently.

The same file already has the pattern — `UncarriableReport` counts oversized drops and `main::upload_tick` prints them. metsuke-jfb.11 removed the other drop-reporting path (`unreadable_reason`) and added this one without a replacement.

Fix: have `migrate` return rows affected per migration (or count in `Spool::open` before the delete) and print one WARNING naming how many rows the upgrade discarded.
close_reason: implemented, nix flake check green

title: A stamp-less row in the spool stalls its stream until the byte cap evicts it, with no distinguishing log
description:
`Spool::taken` hands stored text to `PayloadLine::spooled` unvalidated (metsuke-jfb.11, by design). A row without a valid stamp — corruption, a foreign writer, a future bug — goes into every batch; the server refuses the whole batch on `LineStamp`/`LineProvenance`, and `main::upload_tick` logs the same 'rows stay spooled' line it logs for any transient rejection. Selection is oldest-first, so the stream stalls until the byte cap evicts that row.

Not forever, and the same trade as the over-budget head row. What is missing is the signal: nothing tells an operator the stall is a poison row rather than a flaky server.

Question: on a rejection that names a line index, should the agent evict that one row and log which, or is the byte-cap eviction plus the existing rejection log enough?
close_reason: moot: server never decompresses, so no per-line rejection exists

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Moot: envelope::open and inflate have no production caller in either crate (grep across crates/*/src). The server stores raw bytes and never decompresses, so it never reads a payload line and can never answer 'payload line {index} ...'. The stall this describes died with jfb.4/jfb.5's stateless strip.

title: Unknown schema_version is still a 400, but jfb.4 listed schema-version gating as removed
description:
`Intake::submit` calls `Kind::of(header.schema_version)` and refuses an unrecognised version with `Rejection::UnnameableKind` (400). metsuke-jfb.4 lists "schema-version gating" among the checks removed, so observationally the gate survives under a new name.

Defensible either way: the key scheme jfb.4 mandated needs a <metrics|logs> segment, and an unnameable schema has none.

Question: is version-to-kind naming a permitted gate, or should an unknown version be accepted under a fallback key segment? If permitted, say so in the map's Decisions so far so the next reader does not re-open it.
close_reason: implemented, nix flake check green

title: Selection matches namespace only; the severity rule is deleted
description:
Trace selection reads `ns` and nothing else. The severity floor is deleted from `logselect`,
`config::LogConfig`, the example config, ADR 0010, the instructions page and the NixOS module.

Why: a namespace's severity is assigned by the node's own TraceOptions, so a floor selects a set
that depends on the operator's config. The severity ask is dropped, not answered another way. What
that costs is bounded: every distribution the program asked for is already a namespace in the
shipped `namespaces` default, so the floor added no measurement line. What it added was error,
warning and notice lines from namespaces nobody named, and no stated use exists for those.
close_reason: selection reads ns only; severity floor deleted, snippets are keys to merge

## Round 1's blocking finding is resolved, verified independently

Mutation-tested in a copy of the tree, not taken on report: re-adding `"severity": "Notice"` to
`trace_config`'s root makes `no_node_config_snippet_sets_a_root_severity` FAIL at
tests/instructions.rs:146; emitting invalid JSON from `trace_config` FAILs at :143 via the
