`NAMED_NAMESPACES: [&str; 0] = []` makes `every_named_namespace_carries_its_own_severity` FAIL at
:165 rather than pass over an empty loop. The unescape order in `snippets()` is the exact reverse of
`escape()` and is correct. Baseline 12/12 pass.

## Second round on the same ADR sentence (blocking)

docs/adr/0010:42-45 "every trace carrying a measurement above is `Info` or `Notice` under a
namespace already named". Still false: `Consensus.LeiosKernel.BlockPointMissing` is `"sev":"Warning"`
in tests/fixtures/recordings/leios-node-traces.log, carries `data:{ebHash,ebSlot,kind}`, and sits
under `Consensus.LeiosKernel` — a named namespace. docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md:40
records it as Warning independently. Round 1 cited this exact line; widening Info to Info-or-Notice
did not reach it.

Fix: stop enumerating severities. The argument does not need them — every namespace the program
asked for is already in the default list, so the floor selected nothing the namespace rule did not,
whatever severity those lines carry. Enumerating invites this re-check on every node version.
The ticket body and the epic bullet carry the same sentence and need the same correction.

## ADR 0010

- :14-19 — the rewrite deleted the ask "every trace at error, warning or notice severity" from the
  Context, but :37-45 still rebuts it, and :43's "measurement above" points at a list that no longer
  contains it. Fix: keep the ask in the Context sentence, marked as the one jfb.19 drops.
- :39-40 "the config SPOs run is one that overrides much of the tree, and
  docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md holds the detail" — dead pointer plus an unowned

## A test can now pass vacuously

crates/metsuke/tests/logselect.rs:28 and :205. The diff deleted
`assert!(fields.severity.is_some())` from `every_recorded_record_declares_the_field_a_rule_reads`,
which was what guaranteed every recorded line declares `sev`. `severity_of` returns `Option`, and
`.as_deref() == Some("Debug")` reads a missing `sev` as not-Debug, so a recording without `sev`
makes `the_shipped_rules_select_without_reaching_debug` pass while checking nothing.
Fix: `fn severity_of(line: &TraceLine) -> String` with `.expect("a recorded trace record declares
sev")`. `TraceLine::get` is public (metsuke-wire/src/envelope.rs:305), so the same signature serves
both call sites and drops the parse-render-parse round trip at :205.

## Prose

- docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md:59-60 states the why and cites ADR 0010 as its owner in

- crates/metsuke-server/tests/instructions.rs:153-154 "each named namespace carries its own severity

crates/metsuke-server/tests/instructions.rs:158-165 picks the trace snippet with `find` on a
structural discriminator (`TraceOptions` object with more than one key). The count is already
asserted as 2, so position identifies it without a discriminator that a future second key in
`backend_config` would fool — the same wrong-snippet class as the bug just fixed. Fix:
`let snippets = trace_options(&page); assert_eq!(snippets.len(), 2); let traces = &snippets[1];`

comments.text:
Review round 3. 14 files, all staged, no untracked. Gates run here: cargo test --workspace 43/43
binaries ok no failures, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets silent, cargo fmt --check clean.

## The round-2 nit I recommended removed a guard (blocking)

crates/metsuke-server/tests/instructions.rs, `every_named_namespace_carries_its_own_severity`.
Verified by mutation in a copy of the tree: with `NAMED_NAMESPACES: [&str; 0] = []` the test prints
`ok`. The loop body never runs, so it asserts nothing.

Round 2's version guarded this by accident:
`.find(|value| ...len() > 1).expect("the page carries the trace snippet")` returned None on an empty
const, because `trace_config` then emits a one-key `TraceOptions` — that `.expect` was the non-empty
check. Replacing it with `&snippets[1]` kept the count assert but dropped the guard. Both properties
are available together.

Fix: keep `&snippets[1]`, add `assert!(!instructions::NAMED_NAMESPACES.is_empty())` before the loop.

The suite as a whole still catches that mutation — `the_node_config_step_covers_every_namespace_the_
agent_selects` FAILs — so this is a hole in one test, not in the coverage. Fix it anyway: it is the
third round on the same vacuity class.

## The step does not name every namespace the agent selects

docs/adr/0010:91-92 "The step names every namespace the agent selects, each with its own severity",
and the operator-facing copy at crates/metsuke-server/src/instructions.rs:149 "Every namespace the
agent selects is named".

False as written. The agent selects the prefix `Consensus.Leios` (config.rs `default_log_namespaces`).
`NAMED_NAMESPACES` holds `Consensus.LeiosKernel` and `Consensus.LeiosPeer` — two children of it, not
it. The const's own doc comment at instructions.rs:28-31 says exactly this: "These are the node's own
namespaces, not the agent's selection prefixes". `the_node_config_step_covers_every_namespace_the_
agent_selects` matches in either prefix direction because of the mismatch.

Fix: "The step names every namespace the node must emit for the agent's rules to select anything",
and the same correction in the HTML.

## The ADR says both "dropped" and "nothing lost"

docs/adr/0010:42-45: "Dropping it costs nothing: every distribution the program asked for is already
a namespace in the list, so whatever severity those lines carry, the floor selected nothing the
namespace rule did not. What it did select was unrelated lines."

Two problems. The last two sentences contradict each other — it selected nothing extra, then it did
select unrelated lines. And "costs nothing" answers about *distributions* while :17 has just named
the dropped ask as "every trace at error, warning or notice severity", which is not a distribution,
so the argument never reaches it. Restoring the ask to the Context was right; the Decision now has to
own the drop rather than deny it.

Fix, roughly: the severity ask is dropped. Every distribution the program asked for is already a
namespace in the shipped `namespaces` default, so the floor added no measurement line; what it added
was error, warning and notice lines from namespaces nobody named, and no stated use exists for those.

The ticket body and the epic bullet carry the same two sentences and need the same correction.

## Minor

- ADR 0010:42 "already a namespace in the list" — the Decision names no list. Say "in the shipped
  `namespaces` default" (crates/metsuke/src/config.rs, `default_log_namespaces`).
- ADR 0010:18-20 "under `Consensus.Leios` but for RB adoption, which is both X and Y" — "which" can
  attach to `Consensus.Leios`. Fix: "all under `Consensus.Leios` except RB adoption, which is two
  namespaces: X and Y."
- docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md:46 "`Info` suffices for everything the rewards program
  asked for" — no longer true now the ADR has restored the severity ask to the list. Narrow it to

- Wrapping nit: ADR 0010 is an 80-column file; :19 and :52 wrap mid-paragraph at under 60.

## Not a finding

"changes with a node version's spelling of the ladder" (ADR 0010:41-42) stands — metsuke-jfb.10 is
the recorded instance of exactly that concern.

comments.text:
Review round 5. 14 files, all staged, no untracked. Gates run here: cargo test --workspace no
failures, clippy --all-targets silent, fmt --check clean.

Round 4's eight items are fixed. This round reviews the merge-not-replace change, which no earlier
round saw.

## The merge instruction does not guarantee `Stdout MachineFormat` (blocking)

crates/metsuke-server/src/instructions.rs:129-133. Step 4's snippet lists two backends, but the
instruction is "add `PrometheusSimple` to the backends already listed". An operator whose root
backends are `Stdout HumanFormatColoured` — or any non-machine stdout backend — follows that
exactly, gets a working metrics endpoint, then applies step 5 and gets the named namespaces emitted
in a format the agent cannot parse. `logselect::select` Skips every line, and nothing reports it.

docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md:28 is where this is recorded: "`Stdout MachineFormat` emits
one JSON object per line to stdout (captured by journald)". The whole trace path depends on it. The
old carries-it-whole snippet guaranteed it; the merge rewrite dropped the guarantee, and the page
names `MachineFormat` nowhere outside the snippet itself.

Fix: say the list has to end up with both, and that a different `Stdout` backend has to be replaced
rather than kept — step 5's traces are read back as machine-format lines.

Note the e2e does not cover this. nix/e2e-test.nix:139 sets `.TraceOptions."".backends = ["Stdout
MachineFormat", $backend]` wholesale, so it exercises replace, not the merge path the page now
instructs.

## Fifth of the vacuity class (blocking)

crates/metsuke-server/tests/instructions.rs, `the_trace_step_cannot_disturb_the_root_entry`:
`assert_eq!(traces.len(), instructions::NAMED_NAMESPACES.len())` is 0 == 0 when the const is empty.
Mutation-verified here with `NAMED_NAMESPACES: [&str; 0] = []`: the test prints `ok`. Its own comment
claims otherwise — "And it is not empty, or 'touches no root' would be true of nothing." The comment
states the guarantee; the assert does not deliver it.

Fix: `assert!(!traces.is_empty())`, or compare against a literal count rather than the same const the
snippet was built from.

## The page states an unverified external config as fact

instructions.rs:155-162 tells SPOs what
`book.world.dev.cardano.org/environments-pre/leios/config.json` contains. docs/research/cardano-node-
11-tracing.md:73-74 says of that same config: "Nothing in this repo is verified against this config;

title: Trace lines parsed as JSON; filter reads parsed fields
description:
## What to build

Trace lines are parsed as JSON objects. This replaces the current substring matching on `"ns":"` and `"sev":"` and its hand-reasoned first-occurrence and last-occurrence rules — the namespace/severity filter reads parsed fields instead. A line that does not parse has no namespace and no severity, so no filter matches it and it is not selected. No special case, no counter, no reporting for unparseable lines (explicitly YAGNI).

Filtering happens after parsing. If trace volume on a real block producer makes that cost something, a cheap prefilter is a local change later — measure on the devnet before optimising.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing log-selection cases pass against parsed fields rather than substrings
- [ ] The nested-ns-inside-data case that motivated the first/last-occurrence rules is trivially correct and stays as a test
- [ ] An unparseable line matches no filter and is not selected

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: Trace lines parsed as JSON; the filter reads the object's top-level ns and sev

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review

Gates run this session: `cargo test --workspace` — 0 failures across all targets, incl. the six rewritten logselect cases. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — clean. `cargo fmt --all --check` — exit 0. `nix flake check` and the e2e VM build were NOT run.

Nothing untracked; the whole change is staged.

### Intent
All three acceptance criteria met. Substring readers gone (`Fields::of`), nested-ns-in-data kept as `a_namespace_nested_in_data_is_not_the_lines_namespace`, unparseable line covered by `a_truncated_line_declares_nothing_and_is_not_selected`. No unasked behaviour.

### Prose
- crates/metsuke/src/logselect.rs:121-123 — the `Fields` doc restates the body ("declares neither" is the `else => Fields::default()` arm; "a severity this build cannot spell is not declared" is `.parse().ok()`), and the one claim that is not restatement is narrower than the behaviour: a line that *is* a JSON object but spells `ns` as a non-string also deserializes to `Fields::default()`, losing a well-formed `sev` with it. Fix: cut to what the code cannot say — that the two fields are read off the object's own top level, and any deserialize failure is one bucket.

### Efficiency
- crates/metsuke/src/logselect.rs:116-118 — `Keys` holds `Option<String>`, so every parsed line heap-allocates twice, including the majority the rules drop. The substring readers allocated nothing. This is not the parse cost the ADR bullet defers; it is avoidable within the chosen approach. Fix: `#[serde(borrow)] ns: Option<Cow<'a, str>>` (`Cow`, not `&str` — a value carrying an escape cannot borrow), lifetime through `Fields`.

### Beads
Ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason; the map metsuke-jfb has no `## Decisions so far` section. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is in sync and staged, carrying only the in_progress flip.

Filed nothing.

Verdict: two fixes before /commit, then close the ticket with a resolution comment.

comments.text:

Both round-1 fixes verified. Probed the borrow claims in a scratch crate rather than taking them: `#[serde(borrow)]` on `Option<Cow<'a, str>>` compiles and yields `Cow::Owned` for a literal value, so the newtype earns its place; dropping `#[serde(borrow)]` off the `Keys` fields fails to compile (`requires that 'de must outlive 'a`), so those attributes are not redundant either. `Fields` is referenced nowhere in src outside logselect.rs, so the lifetime reaches no other caller.

### Prose
- crates/metsuke/tests/logselect.rs:169-172 — the *why the newtype* is written twice: the `Read` doc at logselect.rs:114-117 already owns it, and the test comment restates the same `#[serde(borrow)]`-does-not-reach-through fact. - docs/adr/0010-log-based-trace-collection.md:31-33 — "a line that is not an object declares neither field" is the wording corrected in the code doc this round but left standing here: a line that *is* an object with `ns` spelled as a non-string also declares neither. ### Tests
- crates/metsuke/tests/logselect.rs:196 — `not_json` no longer counts what it is named: the branch is `fields == Fields::default()`, which a JSON object declaring neither field also takes. This diff changed the check from a parse to a declaration; the name did not follow. Fix: `declaring_neither`.

Unchanged from round 1 and acknowledged as step 4: no resolution comment, no close reason, epic has no `## Decisions so far` section. `.beads/issues.jsonl` carries the round-1 comment unstaged — stage `.beads/` with the code.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Selection parses the line instead of scanning it. logselect::Fields { namespace, severity } is built
by Fields::of, which deserializes the top level into a private Keys; the NS/SEV constants, string_at,
and the free namespace()/severity() functions are gone, and with them the first-occurrence and
last-occurrence rules — those were an unenforced claim about the node's key order. Every line the
parse refuses lands in one bucket declaring neither field, so no rule matches it: not an object, ns
not a string, cut short. No counter, no reporting (ticket's YAGNI).

Fields borrows out of the line. The fields go through a transparent newtype Read<'a>(Cow<'a, str>)
because #[serde(borrow)] does not reach through an Option — on Option<Cow<'a, str>> the attribute
compiles and every value still arrives owned, verified in a scratch crate. A borrowed &'a str field
would have refused any escaped value outright, dropping the whole line.

Tests: the_string_rules_read_what_a_json_parse_reads is gone (it compared a parse against a parse)
and four replace it — a_namespace_nested_in_data_is_not_the_lines_namespace,
a_truncated_line_declares_nothing_and_is_not_selected (real recorded line cut at its last comma,
both fields still present), every_recorded_record_declares_the_fields_a_rule_reads, and
reading_a_field_copies_only_what_the_line_does_not_spell_literally, which pins Borrowed for the
recorded shape and Owned for a .-escaped one. Cow's PartialEq compares contents, so the variant
needs matches!, not assert_eq!.

ADR 0010 amended: the Decision said "as substrings rather than by decoding the line". New
Consequences bullet records that the parse costs every line the node writes, that nobody has
measured it on a real block producer, and that a prefilter ahead of it is a local change.

Gates: cargo test --workspace 0 failures, clippy clean, fmt clean, nix flake check all passed,
hydraJobs.units and devnet hydraJobs.e2e both exit 0.

Prose now says "each replaces one of its own kind rather than joining it"; the merge filters only `not backend.startswith("Stdout ")`. Against the recording's root (`PrometheusSimple suffix 127.0.0.1 12798`) the result carries two PrometheusSimple entries, and the `kinds()` helper compares sorted first words, so its own assertion cannot see the duplicate. Fix: filter by first word for both kinds, and assert exactly one PrometheusSimple in `resolved[""]["backends"]`. The comment "Step 4's prose: ... replace an Stdout backend that is not MachineFormat" is stale with it.
- nix/e2e-test.nix, the eval-time `assert lib.assertMsg (metricsPort == examplePort)` — its message says an SPO who follows the page "keeps the port they had, and the agent scrapes one nothing listens on". The prose this diff added says the opposite: "replace it, or keep yours and point step 7's `metrics_url` at that port instead". Divergence is now a documented operator choice, so the assert fails the whole e2e evaluation for a case the page handles. Drop it or restate what it guards.
- jfb.20 asks to "assert the shipped `namespaces` are emitted under it". One of three is emission-asserted (`Consensus.LeiosKernel.Msg` via `archivedLines`). `ChainDB.AddBlockEvent.AddedToCurrentChain` and `Forge.Loop.AdoptedBlock` get key-acceptance only, through the `Illegal namespace` check — the diff says why (no operational certificate, so nothing forges). Decision: give the node the devnet pool's cert and KES so it forges, or record key-acceptance as the accepted bound in the map's Decisions so far and close jfb.20 on it.

## Standards

- scripts/record-preprod-node-config.sh — inlines its own `command -v jq` check. scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh, record-calidus-fixtures.sh and record-trace-fixtures.sh all define the same `need()` helper. Use `need jq`.

Correct today only because `escape()` emits exactly those three entities; add `"` there and this silently mis-parses the JSON snippets. Use `html.unescape`.

## Prose

- docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md — "the per-namespace rate limits and silences it sets on namespaces nobody here named would go with it" is false against the recording it cites: every `maxFrequency` in nix/fixtures/leios-preprod-node-config.json is 0, and line 54 of this same doc says `maxFrequency: 0` means no limit. Only the five `Silence` entries are real. Drop the rate-limits half.
- "the node configuration the Leios pre-production environment publishes, which is what SPOs in the rewards program run" appears in scripts/record-preprod-node-config.sh, nix/e2e-test.nix and the research doc. The recorder owns it; the other two point at it.

- nix/e2e-test.nix, the `canonical()` comment — "a maxFrequency of 2.0 comes back as 2" is an invented example; no non-integer maxFrequency exists in the recording. The mechanism is real, the number is not.
- Restatement: the comment above `pkgs.curl`; the comment above `options.update(trace_step)`; the two comments narrating the asserts immediately below them ("keeps its severity, its detail and every backend...", "each namespace step 5 names carries exactly what it asked for").

`nix eval .#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux.drvPath` in devnet/ succeeds, so the port asserts pass. `leios-node-config` builds: 27 TraceOptions keys, identical to the recording, genesis paths rewritten absolute. `cargo test -p metsuke-server --test instructions` — 13 passed, 0 failed.

## Intent

The subtest asserts what the node *resolved* (the Reflection.TracerConfigInfo echo) and that operator Silence keys stay absent. Now it boots the recording's `PrometheusSimple suffix 127.0.0.1 12798`, all metrics subtests run against that, and the merge swaps in the page's form followed only by wait_for_open_port. - docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md:77 — "drops the wire-level chatter above" is false. Line 53 defines wire-level as LeiosNotify.Remote / LeiosFetch.Remote; both are separate top-level keys in the recording and the merge touches neither, so they stay Debug. Delete the clause. - nix/e2e-test.nix:80 — "about one slot in six". Praos is 1-(1-f)^sigma = 1-0.5^(1/3), about one in five; one in six is the linear f*sigma approximation. The one-in-sixty figure at :174 is right.
- crates/metsuke-server/tests/instructions.rs:52-55 contradicts crates/metsuke-server/src/instructions.rs:311-312, both written by this diff. The test comment says nix/e2e-test.nix "is where a node reads the merged config and answers it (metsuke-jfb.24)"; the doc comment says nothing in this repo verifies another project's resolution order, and apply_steps() never hands the node a duplicate kind. - nix/e2e-test.nix:76 — "the date/jq pair metsuke-4zo.60 already has two copies of" states a count 4zo.60 owns, and disagrees with the epic's own Decisions line. It also claims a test-owned clock "needs none of it" while the derivation copies devnet/flake.nix's epochLength gate verbatim. Commented on 4zo.60.

## Question

Emission is asserted under the recording *plus* both page snippets, never under the recording alone — while docs/research/cardano-node-11-tracing.md:74 claims the unmerged config already emits each one. title: Two instructions tests assert on English sentences and verify nothing
description:

The string is copied from the prose it checks, so the assertion is a self-comparison: it fails on any rewording that keeps the meaning, and passes on prose that keeps the words and is wrong. title: Agent identity: agent id, per-line provenance, pool-id startup check
description:
## What to build

Every machine identifies itself. A new agent-id configuration field defaults to the slugified hostname — slugify rather than reject, since a machine that will not start over an underscore in its hostname is data loss for no benefit. The resolved id is logged at startup.

Every payload line — metrics and trace alike — carries the header fields (pool, agent, sequence number, timestamp) nested under the single reserved key `metsuke`. A metrics line is the sample fields plus `metsuke`; a trace line is the node's parsed JSON object plus `metsuke`. Nesting rather than flat merge: cardano-node's top-level trace keys are node-version-defined, and one reserved key is a constraint statable in a sentence. Measured overhead: +3.4% compressed.

The sequence number stays persisted before sealing, unchanged mechanically; its meaning becomes per-agent gap detection, not replay control.

Startup check: if the configured pool id disagrees with the pool the signing key implies, refuse to start with a message naming both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Agent id config field defaults to slugified hostname and is logged at startup
- [ ] Sealed batches carry the agent id in the header; every line carries `metsuke` provenance
- [ ] Sequence number advances per agent
- [ ] Startup refusal names both the configured pool id and the key-implied one (config suite)
- [ ] Metrics and trace lines have the same line shape (one duckdb query reads both)

## Blocked by

Wire container ticket, trace-parsing ticket.
close_reason: Agent id, per-line metsuke provenance, pool-id startup refusal

title: A pulled object carries no signature, so nothing downstream can verify it
description:
The download route (crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs, `object`) hands back the bytes alone. The
vkey and signature are S3 object metadata (`s3::META_VKEY`, `META_SIGNATURE`), and no route serves
them, so metsuke-fetch writes verbatim bytes it cannot check — re-verification needs the pair
out of band.

Consequence: `metsuke_wire::envelope::open`, `inflate`, `Limits` and `OpenError` still have no
production caller (only tests). Serving the two headers is what would give them one; otherwise they
are dead code to delete.

Fix: answer the download with the two metadata headers where the archive holds them
(`Fetch`/`FilesystemArchive` cannot, and that split is `archive::Bytes` versus `archive::Fetch`),
and have the fetch tool verify each object as it lands.
close_reason: the download answers the vkey and signature the object was stored with; metsuke-s9r carries the fetch half forward

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
metsuke-jfb.8 built no header read, so `envelope::open`, `inflate`, `Limits` and `OpenError` stay test-only until this ticket lands.

Why the fetch tool does not read the header for its schema version: the key's `<metrics|logs>` segment
is named from that version by the server (`key::Kind::of`), so the version states nothing the key does
not, and `--kind` already selects on it. Reading it would add a required `--max-header-bytes` flag —
a limit is configuration here — for a second copy of a fact the key carries. What the header would add
is signature-checked provenance, and that needs the vkey and signature this ticket is about.

metsuke-fetch instead checks the download against the length the route declared, so a truncated object
is refused rather than filed.

title: Neither rename is fsynced at its directory, so a power loss can leave the cursor ahead of its objects
description:
`metsuke_fetch::sync::download` and `Cursor::write` both `sync_all` the staged file, then `fs::rename`, and neither fsyncs the containing directory. The two renames are in different directories (the download tree and the state file's), so nothing orders them across a power loss: the cursor rename can be durable while the object rename is not, and the resumed run then skips that object for good.

That is the exact failure the comment above `cursor.advance` in `sync::run` says the ordering prevents — signal interruption is safe, crash and power loss are not.

Fix: open the parent directory and `sync_all` it after each rename, mapped to `SyncError::Write` / `CursorError::Write`.
close_reason: staged::replacing fsyncs the parent directory after the rename, so both the object's and the cursor's renames are durable

title: The developer password file is read and trimmed in two crates, and a drift between them breaks auth silently
description:
`metsuke_fetch`'s `main::password` and `metsuke_server`'s `main::developer` do the same three steps: `read_to_string`, `trim_end_matches(['\r','\n'])`, refuse empty by path. The server hashes what it trimmed and the client sends what it trimmed, so the two trims must agree — a change to one is a 401 with nothing naming the cause.

Fix: one `pub fn` in `metsuke-wire` (which already owns the pull contract both sides read), called by both binaries.

title: metsuke-fetch's test support re-creates metsuke-server's, with no tie between the copies
description:
`crates/metsuke-fetch/tests/support/mod.rs` copies `test_key`, `test_now`, `nonzero_u64`, `nonzero_u32` and the ingest/http config builders from `crates/metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs` (`permissive_config`, `permissive_http`). The fetch crate already dev-depends on `metsuke-server`, so nothing is gained by the copy: a required config field added on the server side leaves the fetch copy compiling against a stale shape until someone notices.

Fix: expose them from `metsuke-server` behind a `testkit` feature and delete the copies.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Also within the crate: `Asked`, `filters()` and `everything()` are defined in both `crates/metsuke-fetch/tests/cursor.rs` and `crates/metsuke-fetch/tests/sync.rs` while `tests/support/mod.rs` already exists for shared scaffolding. Same fix shape as this ticket's — one home, both binaries `mod support;` it.

title: The query escaper and its decoder live in different crates, with a third partial copy in a server test
description:
`metsuke_fetch::pull::escaped` is the inverse of `metsuke_server::developer::percent_decoded`, and `metsuke_server`'s `tests/binary.rs` holds a third, partial copy (`urlencoded`, escaping `/` only). The query field names the pair agrees on (`PREFIX_FIELD`, `KEY_FIELD`) are already in `metsuke_wire::http`, so the escaper is the one half of the contract still outside it.

`escaped` is also `pub` with no caller outside its own module.

Fix: move `escaped` beside the field constants in `metsuke-wire/src/http.rs` and have the server test call it.

title: The wire API names a Scrape a Sample, which CONTEXT.md lists under Avoid
description:
CONTEXT.md **Scrape** puts `sample` under _Avoid_, but `metsuke_wire::envelope` exports `Sample`, `Payload::samples`, `PayloadLine::sample`, `Envelope::samples` and `Schema::Samples`, so every caller is forced into the avoided word — including the new `metsuke-fetch` tests.

`SCHEMA_VERSION_SAMPLES` is a `u32`, not a wire string, so the rename is source-only and changes no bytes on the wire.

Fix: rename to `Scrape`/`scrapes` across the wire API and its callers.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Appears already done: `rg '\bSample\b|\bsamples\b' crates/ --type rust` returns nothing, and envelope.rs exports SCHEMA_VERSION_SCRAPES / SCHEMA_VERSION_LINES. Verify and close. The remaining Avoid-word is `batch`, filed as metsuke-jfb.37.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Verified landed. Every symbol this names is gone: rg for Sample, SCHEMA_VERSION_SAMPLES, Payload::samples, PayloadLine::sample, Schema::Samples and Envelope::samples across crates/ returns nothing. The wire API is Scrape/scrapes throughout. Renamed by the metsuke-uxw epic, not by this ticket.

title: The fetch tool never reads the envelope header, so open/inflate/Limits/OpenError still have no production caller
description:
jfb.8 says "The header's schema version tells the tool what it pulled". Nothing in `crates/metsuke-fetch/src/` reads it: the tool names the kind off the key segment instead, and `grep -rn "envelope::open\|inflate\|OpenError\|Limits" crates/*/src` finds no caller outside `metsuke-wire/src/envelope.rs` itself.

That is the condition jfb.8's 2026-08-26 comment set: this crate was their intended consumer, and "if the fetch tool ends up not using them, they are dead code to delete rather than keep".

Decision needed: surface the header's schema version per object in the sync report (which gives the four a production caller), or delete `open`, `inflate`, `Limits` and `OpenError` from the wire crate.

metsuke-fetch verifies each object as it lands (metsuke-s9r), which gives verify_strict and PoolId::from_cold_key a production caller. envelope::open, inflate, Limits and OpenError still have none: the tool checks the signature and the pool without inflating the payload or reading the header, so the decision this bead states, use them or delete them, is unchanged.

title: Code, logs and ADR 0010 call a Submission a batch, which CONTEXT.md lists under Avoid
description:
CONTEXT.md **Submission** puts `batch` under _Avoid_. `metsuke::delivery::SealedBatch` is the type, the agent logs `batch acked` (asserted by nix/e2e-test.nix:483,511), and CLAUDE.md:4, contrib/server.example.toml:8 and docs/adr/0010 lines 89-91 all use the word in prose.

Sibling of metsuke-jfb.35, which covered `Sample`. Nothing on the wire carries the string, so the rename is source-only.

Fix: `SealedBatch` -> `SealedSubmission`, the log line to `submission acked`, and the prose in the four files above. ADR 0010 edits are permitted by docs/adr/README.md, "Terminology, yes".
close_reason: SealedSubmission, the journal lines, and the prose in the four files

title: Server ingest strip, new object keys, two-agent e2e
description:
## What to build

The complete accepted path becomes: allowlist lookup → derive pool from the verifying key → per-pool and global rate limits → Ed25519 verify over the body → PUT with metadata headers. The server never decompresses and never parses a payload. Removed as a consequence: decompression limits, payload parsing, schema-version gating, pool-id cross-checking (the pool-id request header is dropped — it carried nothing the key does not prove), timestamp-skew refusal, replay-counter refusal. max_body_bytes on the compressed bytes is the only size limit. Tests for removed checks are deleted with them; the intake suite shrinks to allowlist, key-belongs-to-pool, signature.

Objects are keyed `v1/<date>/<uuid7>-<pool>-<agent>-<metrics|logs>.jsonl.zst`. Time-major; UUIDv7 stamped at upload so a late spool flush still sorts after everything synced — one start-after cursor is the whole delta-sync protocol. Uniqueness comes from the UUIDv7 alone, never the clock, sequence number, or agent id. Pool segment derives from the verifying key, not the header. Date segment is the server's receipt date.

Per-pool rate limit default: 100 submissions/hour (~16× headroom over 6 agents at one upload/hour) — a runaway-agent backstop, not abuse control. All limits are configuration.

The replay-counter refusal is keyed per pool, so today a second agent for the same pool is rejected as a replay — the motivating bug. metsuke-jfb.3 already made the agent's own counter per-agent gap detection (`envelope::Envelope::counter`); this ticket is the server half, and ADR 0002 (replay counter) is deleted in the commit that removes the code it describes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Intake suite covers exactly: allowlist, key-belongs-to-pool, signature
- [ ] Object keys match the scheme; pool segment derives from the verifying key
- [ ] HTTP suite asserts status codes for each refusal that remains
- [ ] e2e VM test runs two agents for one pool with different agent ids and asserts both objects land (regression test for the motivating multi-machine bug)
- [ ] ADR 0002 deleted in the same change

## Blocked by

Agent identity ticket.
close_reason: server ingest stripped to allowlist/vkey-pool/signature, new object keys, two-agent e2e green

title: Stateless cold-key-only server: Calidus, db-sync, SQLite all deleted
description:
## What to build

Authority becomes cold-key-only: pool identity is derived from the cold verifying key, the only claim under the signature. Calidus resolution is removed entirely — the directory, the CIP-151 witness check, the db-sync client, and the postgres dependency. Participants polled in favour of cold-key signing.

Server state becomes none: the SQLite index, counter reservations, and rebuild path are deleted along with rusqlite. The listing route calls ListObjectsV2 with the client's prefix and start-after; list_max_rows clamps to 1000 (S3's cap) so one request is one upstream page and truncated comes straight from IsTruncated. The object route GETs and passes through; the existence pre-check is deleted and the upstream 404 passes through. The rate limiter stays in memory — losing it on restart is harmless. The bucket is the source of truth, as it already was.

Docs land in the deleting commits: ADRs 0003, 0008, 0009 deleted; ADR 0005 trimmed to the part still true (archive stores raw signed bytes, source of truth; the SQLite-index sentence goes). CONTEXT.md loses Calidus Key, Registration, Nonce, Witness, Revocation; gains Agent (one machine's reporter, several per pool), Sequence Number, Frame. No new ADRs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server links no postgres, no rusqlite, no csv
- [ ] Calidus, db-sync, index and rebuild suites deleted with the code they cover
- [ ] Listing route is a ListObjectsV2 passthrough; truncated mirrors IsTruncated
- [ ] Object route passes upstream 404 through
- [ ] Server restart loses nothing but in-memory rate-limit windows
- [ ] ADRs 0003/0008/0009 deleted, 0005 trimmed, CONTEXT.md updated, in the deleting commits

## Blocked by

Server ingest strip ticket.
close_reason: server is stateless and cold-key-only; Calidus, db-sync and the SQLite index deleted

title: HTTP layer: hyper replaces tiny_http
description:
## What to build

hyper + hyper-util replace tiny_http. Why nothing else will do: tiny_http 0.12 exposes no socket timeout and no way to skip its drain-on-drop, so neither of metsuke-a3a's failure modes (60-byte request declaring 4 GB Content-Length drives 4.2 GB VmSize and a MemoryMax kill; a trickling body stalls all ingest) is fixable in our own code. Sequenced after the routes have shrunk, which makes it a smaller change.

- Read, write and idle timeouts, all configuration (NixOS module options)
- Body cap via a limited-body wrapper, no drain-on-drop allocation
- Global concurrent-request cap, default 64, enforced at accept
- The object download route streams the upstream body through rather than buffering

Routing stays a match on four paths — no router crate. TLS and IP-keyed limits remain the reverse proxy's; the proxy is defence in depth, no longer what any correctness argument rests on.

Closes metsuke-a3a; also resolves metsuke-4zo.72 (download buffers whole object) and .73 (download stalls ingest).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A request declaring a large Content-Length without sending a body neither allocates nor stalls other requests — as a test, not an inspection (metsuke-a3a's acceptance criterion)
- [x] HTTP suite: status codes for remaining refusals, 401 challenge on developer routes, body-size cap
- [x] Downloads stream; a slow developer download does not stall ingest
- [x] Timeouts, body cap, concurrency cap all NixOS module options
- [x] metsuke-a3a closed by this ticket's landing commit

## Blocked by

Stateless cold-key-only server ticket.
close_reason: hyper replaces tiny_http: timeouts, caps and streaming downloads

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Keep the transport out of the routing signature.

tiny_http's version does this wrong: `route` takes `&mut tiny_http::Request` and returns a private `Answer`, so the only way to reach it is over a socket. tests/binary.rs spawns the binary for 36 tests and SIGKILLs it in Drop, so LLVM flushes no profile: http.rs, intake.rs, ratelimit.rs and developer.rs all measure 0% under `cargo llvm-cov --test binary` while every one of those tests passes. The workspace 79.37% is a floor, not a measurement.

For hyper: routing takes decoded parts (method, path, headers, body reader + declared length) and returns a public status/body value. No hyper type in the signature. Then the HTTP suite acceptance criterion above is unit tests over values, and the socket tests are only the ones that must be — timeouts, the drain/allocation behaviour, streaming.

## Review: hyper replaces tiny_http (working tree, 22 files)

No untracked files; every changed file is staged, so the repo gate reads the diff.
Run in session: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean; `cargo test --workspace`
435 passed, 0 failed. Not run: `nix flake check`, treefmt, `cargo llvm-cov`.

### Intent

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — metsuke-a3a is still OPEN, against "metsuke-a3a closed by
  this ticket's landing commit". `br update metsuke-a3a --close`, flush, stage in the
  landing commit.
- `crates/metsuke-server/src/serve.rs:287` — the lying-length half of the body cap has
  no test, against "HTTP suite: ... body-size cap". `submission_head` always writes a
  `Content-Length`, so both a3a tests take the declared branch; no test anywhere sends
  `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and `bounded`'s `collected.len() as u64 > max` refusal
  is reached by nothing. Add one `Raw` test posting chunked past `max_body_bytes`,
  asserting 413.

### Silent failures

- `crates/metsuke-server/src/serve.rs:120` — `listener.accept().await?` makes every
  accept error terminal. `tokio::net::TcpListener::accept` retries only `WouldBlock`
  (`async_io(Interest::READABLE, ..)`, tokio 1.53.1 `net/tcp/listener.rs:163`), so
  `ECONNABORTED` from a client that vanished mid-handshake, or `EMFILE`/`ENFILE` under
  fd pressure, now exits `run()` and drops every in-flight submission. The comment at
  :82 inherits its "terminal" claim from tiny_http, whose accept *thread* had died.
  Match `error.kind()`: log and continue on `ConnectionAborted`/`Interrupted`/fd
  exhaustion, propagate the rest.
- `crates/metsuke-server/src/serve.rs:142` — the write-failure log lost the pool it
  existed to name. `Answer.signer` was deleted along with its stated justification, and
  the old `respond` logged `named(answer.signer)` with the status. The reasoning survives
  verbatim at :134-138 ("the agent never saw its ack and will send the batch again"),
  but the line names only `peer`, which behind the mandated reverse proxy is the same
  address for every pool. Carry `signer: Option<PoolId>` back onto `Answer` and log
  `http::named(..)` — that also gives `http::named`'s new `pub` (`http.rs:376`) its
  only caller outside the module; today it has none.
- `crates/metsuke-server/src/serve.rs:198` with `http.rs:311` — `SubmissionHeaders::decode`
  runs twice per submission, and the first one's `.ok()` throws the value away. Two costs:
  the hex decode plus `VerifyingKey`/`Signature::from_bytes` (Ed25519 point decompression)
  repeat on the blocking pool for every accepted submission, and a request whose headers
  cannot decode has its body read to `max_body_bytes` before `submit` re-decodes and
  refuses — metsuke-a3a's own comment lists "header-decode 400" among the paths that
  answer without reading the body. Decode once in `handle`; on `Err` refuse 400 before
  `read_body`, on `Ok` thread the value to `submit`.

### Standards

- `crates/metsuke-server/src/serve.rs:41` — `const DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;`
  against CLAUDE.md `## Conventions`: "Limits (sizes, rates, intervals) are configuration,
  never constants." The doc comment argues it is granularity, not a limit; that reads as
  the exception the rule does not state. Decide: move it into `HttpConfig`, or amend the
  Conventions line so the next reviewer does not re-litigate it. Recommendation: amend the
  line — a copy granularity is not an operator-facing bound, and three separate reviews
  flagged the same constant.

### Prose

- One *why* in five places: "the archive blocks, so the answer runs off the accept loop" —
  `Cargo.toml:36-38`, `serve.rs:1-5`, `serve.rs:59-62`, `serve.rs:152-153`, `http.rs:180-181`.
  Owner: `serve.rs:59` (`bind`, where the runtime shape is chosen). Cargo.toml keeps only
  the feature-list reason; the rest point or say nothing.
- One *why* in three places: what `HttpConfig` bounds — `config.rs:26-28` ("Every field
  bounds one way a client can hold a connection open without finishing with it") vs
  `serve.rs:7-9` ("Everything a client can do to hold a connection without finishing with
  it is bounded here") vs `http.rs:12-16`. Owner: `config.rs`, on the struct.
- One *why* in four places: a declared-but-unsent body costs nothing — `serve.rs:8-10`,
  `serve.rs:188-190`, `serve.rs:231-236`, `http.rs:50-52` (`Request.body`). Owner:
  `serve.rs:188`, the branch it describes.
- `tests/binary.rs:88-89` — "60 bytes on the wire against 4.2 GB here (metsuke-a3a)".
  CLAUDE.md `## Prose`: "Digits live in exactly one file." The measurement is in
  metsuke-a3a's comment (VmSize before/after). Drop the digits, keep the pointer.

### Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is in sync (dirty 0) and staged with the code; its only change is
jfb.6's status going in_progress. Two gaps: metsuke-jfb's `## Decisions so far` gained no
jfb.6 line, and jfb.6 has no resolution comment — its two existing comments are the
routing-signature note and a review of the earlier coverage-tooling diff.

### Filed

Nothing. Every finding above is this diff's own; no pre-existing issue survived the gate.
Repo-wide "batch" for **Submission** was considered and dropped: CONTEXT.md:108-109 already
records that the code's naming is not yet aligned, so it is documented drift, not a finding.

### Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`. Blocking: close metsuke-a3a, add the chunked body-cap test,
bound the accept-error case, restore the pool in the write-failure log. Then the
decode-once change, the prose de-duplication, the `DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES` ruling, and the
map's decision line.

comments.text:
## Review round 2: hyper replaces tiny_http (working tree, 23 files)

No untracked files; every changed file is staged. Round 1's eight fixes all land — verified
independently: metsuke-a3a CLOSED naming both tests; the chunked test exists and asserts 413
with the cap; `nix/unit.nix` `restartSecs = 30` reaches `RestartSec` via
`nix/server-module.nix`, so the accept-error reasoning's backoff is real; `decode` now runs
exactly once. Four new findings, three of them in what round 1's fixes introduced.

### Silent failures

- `serve.rs:78-81` — **the doc is now false.** "Serve until accepting fails, which is the one
  error this can see and is terminal" against :121-124, which logs and continues on
  `ConnectionAborted`/`Interrupted`. Fix: "Serve until accepting fails in a way this process
  cannot recover from (`one_connection`)", and let the match arm own the exit-to-systemd why.
- `serve.rs:178-183` — **`one_connection` is too narrow, and one bad connection exits the
  process.** `accept(2)` documents `EPERM`, `EPROTO`, `ENOPROTOOPT`, `ENETDOWN`, `ENETUNREACH`,
  `EHOSTDOWN`, `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ENONET` as pending per-connection network errors that "should
  be treated as EAGAIN by reliable applications"; none is `ConnectionAborted` or `Interrupted`.
  Checked the mapping on this toolchain: `ENETDOWN`→`NetworkDown`, `ENETUNREACH`→
  `NetworkUnreachable`, `EHOSTUNREACH`→`HostUnreachable`, `EPERM`→`PermissionDenied`, while
  `EPROTO`/`ENOPROTOOPT`/`EHOSTDOWN`→`Uncategorized` and cannot be matched by kind at all.
  Fix: add the four nameable kinds; if the `Uncategorized` three matter, match
  `error.raw_os_error()` instead and say so at the site. Descriptor exhaustion staying terminal
  is fine and the reasoning at :125-128 holds.
- `serve.rs:163-171` — **the log names the last pool answered, not the failure's owner.**
  `answered_for` is written after *every* answer, so a keep-alive connection that acks pool A
  and then fails while parsing request two's head logs "the connection answering `<A>` ended"
  under a comment asserting A's agent will resend. An operator hunts duplicates for a pool that
  was answered cleanly. Fix: clear `answered_for` once that answer's write completed, or drop
  the resend clause and word it "last answered".

### Intent

- `tests/binary.rs:854` with `:948-953` — **the chunked cap test turns on hyper coalescing head
  and body into one segment.** `head()` does a single 256-byte `read`, and the test asserts the
  response *body* (`"64 byte limit"`) is inside it. It passes today, but any flush that splits
  head from body makes the acceptance criterion's only chunked test fail for the wrong reason.
  Fix: read until `\r\n\r\n`, then read the declared `Content-Length`. Not reading to close is
  right — that would wait out `idle_timeout`.
- Coverage note, not a criterion miss: of the four `[http]` fields, only `read_timeout_secs` is
  exercised by a test (`:914`). `idle_timeout_secs`, `write_timeout_secs` and
  `max_concurrent_requests` are asserted nowhere, so wiring the wrong field to the wrong knob
  fails nothing. The criteria demand module options, which they are — your call whether to buy
  the evidence with one `Raw` test per field.

### Standards

- `serve.rs:36` with `s3.rs:293` — **the CLAUDE.md carve-out this diff wrote does not quite cover
  its own case.** `ObjectStream.length` is `body.content_length()`, an `Option`; where S3 declares
  no length, `respond` sets no `Content-Length`, hyper frames the answer chunked, and
  `DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES` becomes the chunk size a client observes. Not worth a config field — add
  the clause to the constant's comment so the exception stays honest.
- `http.rs:163` with `serve.rs:243` — `Answer.signer` now carries a value `handle` already holds.
  Every `Some(signer)` originates in `submit` or in `serve`'s own `refuse`/`oversized` calls, and
  that is exactly what `takes_a_body` returned; `respond` discards the field (`signer: _`). Fix:
  keep `signer` as a parameter of `refuse_withholding`, delete the struct field, and write the
  cell in `handle` from `takes_a_body`. Pairs with the log finding above — decide both together.
- `http.rs:62` — `pub submission: Result<SubmissionHeaders, HeaderError>` makes a GET carry
  `Err(Missing { header: HEADER_VKEY })`, a state no reader may act on; it works only because
  `submit` is the sole reader. CLAUDE.md `## Code`: "Make bad values unrepresentable." Fix:
  `Option<Result<..>>`, `None` where neither header was sent.

### Prose

Round 1's four collapses: #1 and #4 done. Three residuals and one new duplication:

- `serve.rs:5-6` ("where every field of `config::HttpConfig` is applied") restates
  `config.rs:26-28` ("`serve` is where each is applied"). Owner `config.rs`. Delete the
  serve.rs sentence.
- `Cargo.toml:37-38` ("a multi-thread scheduler would buy nothing it does not already have")
  restates `serve.rs:58` ("a second scheduler thread would buy nothing"). Owner `serve.rs:54`.
  Cargo.toml keeps the feature-list reason only.
- Declared-body cost, #3, not collapsed: owner `serve.rs:227-230`, second copies at `:248` and
  `http.rs:58-61`.
- New: signer-named-before-judgement in four places — `http.rs:156-158` (owner),
  `http.rs:323-324`, `serve.rs:235-236`, `serve.rs:134-137`. Drop both "Named before …"
  comments; `serve.rs:134` keeps only what is its own.
- `metsuke-jfb`'s new jfb.6 bullet carries three why-clauses the code owns ("so a declared
  length costs nothing" → `serve.rs:227`; "what lets a stalled reader stall only itself" →
  `serve.rs:262-265`; "so the whole surface is a unit test …" → `http.rs:5-8`). State the
  decision, drop the justifications.

Dead references: none. `Answer.signer`, `takes_a_body`, `nix/unit.nix`, `RestartSec` all
resolve. The CLAUDE.md `## Conventions` amendment is sound as prose — it defines "limit" once
and `serve.rs:34-35` points at it.

### Considered and dropped

`max_concurrent_requests` naming (config.rs:44-46 documents why requests == connections under
HTTP/1.1); `path_and_query().unwrap_or("/")` (`instructions::PATH` is `"/"`, so an asterisk-form
GET gets the unauthenticated page — no consequence); `declared_length`'s `.ok()?` chain (hyper
rejects a malformed `Content-Length` before the service runs, `proto/h1/role.rs:291`); the
non-UTF-8 header reading as `Missing`; a repeatable panic wedging at 503 (needs a panic path
inside the limiter lock, which `intake.rs:125` documents as unreachable); `Raw::head` vs
`support::opening_bytes` (different sides of the socket, read both).

### Beads hygiene

`metsuke-jfb`'s `## Decisions so far` has the jfb.6 bullet; metsuke-a3a is closed with a reason
and a comment naming its two tests; `.beads/issues.jsonl` staged with the code. jfb.6 still has
no resolution comment, which is right while it is open.

### Filed

Filed metsuke-jfb.27 — the instructions page is deep-copied per GET `/`
(`page.as_bytes().to_vec()`), pre-existing, unauthenticated route.

### Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`. Blocking: the stale `serve` doc, `one_connection`'s missing error kinds,
the log naming the wrong pool, and the chunked test's single-read assertion. Then the
`DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES` clause, the `Answer.signer`/`submission` shape calls, and the prose
residuals.

comments.text:
## Review round 3: hyper replaces tiny_http (working tree, 23 files)

No untracked files; everything staged. Round 2's fixes mostly land, and **your hyper claim is
correct** — h1 gates head N+1 on `can_read_head()` → `Reading::Init`, reachable only via
`State::idle` from `try_keep_alive`, which needs `(Reading::KeepAlive, Writing::KeepAlive)`;
`writing` is `Writing::Body` for all of response N, and `service.call()` sits behind that gate
(hyper 1.11.0 `proto/h1/conn.rs:175-185, 1072-1076, 1115`; `dispatch.rs:621`). No mid-body
dispatch.

This round's findings are mostly in the **tests**, and one of them is load-bearing for
metsuke-a3a.

### Tests

- `tests/support/mod.rs:90-96` with `tests/binary.rs:970` — **a3a's acceptance-criterion test
  passes with the full 4 GB allocated.** `VmSize` is sampled after `lying.answer()` returns, so
  any transient allocation over 128 KB has gone back to the kernel by mmap unmap. Demonstrated
  in a scratch copy: injecting `Vec::with_capacity(declared)` + `resize(declared, 1)` (every
  page touched) into `read_body` before the 413 **still passes**; switching the helper to
  `VmPeak` fails it with `grew 3906252 kB` and still passes on the unmodified tree. Fix: read
  `VmPeak:`, rename the helper `peak_virtual_kb`. The 413 and the follow-up `post == 200` halves
  hold, and the real code does not allocate — so a3a's closure is substantively right, but the
  test guards nothing against a regression. Worth fixing before the landing commit that closes it.
- `tests/binary.rs:1104-1109` — **`delivered < size` has no margin, and the test is non-vacuous
  only by luck.** `stalled_download` calls `answer_head`, which discards everything
  `until_blank_line` read past the blank line, so any body byte arriving in the head's segment
  satisfies `delivered < size` with no cutoff at all. Measured with `write_timeout_secs` widened
  to 60: `delivered == 8388608` exactly, three runs — it passed only because hyper happened to
  flush the head alone. This is the same coalescing fragility round 2 had you fix in the chunked
  test. Fix: return the carried bytes from `stalled_download`, add them to `delivered`, assert
  `< size / 2`. The 3s sleep is justified and the permissive 10s idle/read do separate this
  bound from the others.
- `tests/binary.rs:978-999` — **the trickle test does not exercise the case its doc claims.** The
  comment says "a body that arrives a byte at a time renews any per-read deadline forever, so the
  bound is on the whole body", but the test sends one byte and goes silent; a naive per-read
  deadline fires on that too, so the test cannot tell the two implementations apart. The strong
  case does work — `b"x"` every 400 ms for 3.2 s against `read_timeout_secs = 1` still yields 408.
  Fix: loop the byte with `let _ = write_all(..)`; the server closes mid-trickle, so `Raw::send`'s
  `unwrap` would panic.
- `tests/binary.rs:886` — `.unwrap_or(0)` on `Content-Length` frames a chunked or header-less
  answer as head-only. It fails rather than passes today, but silently and for the wrong reason.
  Fix: `.expect("the answer states its length")`.
- `tests/binary.rs:848` — `let _ = self.0.read_to_string(..)` discards the read error, and
  `read_to_string` restores the buffer on failure, so an error yields `""` and the assertion
  reports an empty `got:`. Fix: `.expect("the server answered")`.

### Silent failures

- `serve.rs:134` with `:156-167` — **the pool cell is still stale on the path round 2 named, and
  "never stale" is now a false claim.** Moving the write before the answer closes the
  mid-dispatch variant (which your hyper argument shows never existed) but not this one: after
  pool A's ack, a reset or a malformed next head fails *before* `handle` runs, so nothing
  rewrites the cell, and the line still reads "the connection answering `<A>` ended" under a
  comment asserting A's agent will resend. Clearing the cell from `handle` is not possible — the
  answer is unwritten when `handle` returns. Fix: take round 2's other option — word it "last
  answered" and drop the resend sentence.

### Standards

- `tests/binary.rs:867` — `answer_head` throws away the exact bytes `until_blank_line`'s tuple
  exists to keep ("a stream socket cannot put them back"), which is what makes the write-timeout
  assertion hollow. Fix: give `Raw` a `buffer: Vec<u8>` field; `until_blank_line` fills it and
  returns only the head length; `answer_head`, `one_answer` and `drained` all read from it. The
  tuple and its Data Clump disappear.
- `http.rs:9` — "every status, body and header this server can produce is reachable from a test
  without a socket" overclaims: the 408 text and the panic 503 are worded in `serve.rs`, and
  `tests/http.rs`'s own header concedes it. Fix: "every route's answer is reachable".
- `tests/binary.rs:846, 906, 923` — `answer()`, `closed_within()` and `drained()` are one
  read-to-close loop with three return types (possible Duplicated Code). One
  `read_to_close(&mut self, budget) -> (Vec<u8>, bool)` covers all three.

### Prose

- `http.rs:58-61` — both halves of the sentence are wrong. "decoded once, by whoever built this
  (`serve::takes_a_body`)" points at the function that only *reads* the field; `serve::handle`
  calls `decode`. And "`Err` … which is exactly what it says: neither header was sent" is false —
  `decode(None, None)` returns `Missing { header: HEADER_VKEY }`, naming one header.
- `serve.rs:44-46` — "`:0` is how the tests and any readiness check learn the port" duplicates
  `main.rs:176-177`, which already owns it. Cut the second sentence.
- The download-streams *why* in four places: `archive.rs:321-323` (owner, the trait that chose
  it), `http.rs:282-283`, `http.rs:166-167`, `s3.rs:288-289`.
- `tests/binary.rs:978-980` restates `config.rs:36-39` (owner) on per-read renewal; with the test
  fixed per above, the doc should say what it asserts.
- `serve.rs:115-116` "One client's failure, not the listener's" restates `one_connection`'s doc.
  The arm keeps only the trade sentence.
- `serve.rs:174-182` — the doc accounts for five of the six kinds ("accept(2)'s pending network
  errors … plus the two that are plainly one client's"); `PermissionDenied` is in the match and
  unexplained. It is also the only kind in the set that can be a *syscall-level* denial rather
  than a per-connection pending error, and on that path `continue` spins. One clause, or a
  consecutive-failure bound if you'd rather close it.

### Decision, third time

`serve.rs:31-36` cites CLAUDE.md `## Conventions` for "not a bound anything can observe", then
states the case where a client observes it as the wire chunk size. I asked for that clause, and
it is what shows the carve-out does not cover its own exception. Two clean ways out: always set
`Content-Length` on a download (buffer or refuse a length-less object, and the exception deletes
itself), or make it an `[http]` field. Recommendation: the first — `S3Archive::reader` gets
`body.content_length()` and S3 sends it for every GetObject, so the length-less path is
theoretical and closing it costs nothing.

### Your pushback, accepted

`submission: Result<..>` stays. Your reasoning holds: `None` would be a third state whose only
handler must invent a wording `decode` already owns, and `authorization: Option<String>` has the
same shape on the submit route. Not reopening — only the doc sentence above is wrong, not the
type. The `raw_os_error` trade is accepted too; it is stated on the page, which is what I asked
for. On `max_concurrent_requests`: a shape that does not race is cap 1, one connection holding
its slot with a partial head, then assert a second connection gets no answer within a budget —
the same timing shape the trickle test already uses. Your call; not blocking.

### Checked and dropped

An accept-loop busy-spin on the widened kinds was raised and rejected: `nix/unit.nix` sets
`SystemCallFilter` but no `SystemCallErrorNumber`, so a seccomp denial kills with SIGSYS rather
than returning `EPERM`, and accept(2)'s pending network errors are dequeued with the connection
that carried them, so they cannot spin. Only an LSM-level `EPERM` leaves the connection queued —
hence the doc finding above rather than a correctness one.

### Beads hygiene

Map bullet present and now decisions-only; metsuke-a3a closed with a reason naming its two tests;
`.beads/` staged with the code. jfb.6 has no resolution comment, which is right while open.

### Filed

Nothing new. metsuke-jfb.27 (page copied per GET `/`) is still open from round 2.

### Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`. Blocking: `VmPeak` (a3a's criterion currently guards nothing), the
write-timeout test's margin, the trickle test's renewal case, and the stale-cell wording. Then
the two `expect`s, `answer_head`'s discarded bytes, the prose items, and the
`DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES` ruling.

comments.text:
## Review round 4: hyper replaces tiny_http (working tree, 23 files)

No untracked files; everything staged. **All five acceptance criteria are met**, verified with
file:line evidence, and three of round 3's four fixes are confirmed by mutation in a scratch
copy. The fourth is not fixed. One change made on my round-3 recommendation has a blast radius
I understated, and it needs a decision.

**Verified sound, with numbers.** The new concurrency test is not flaky: the permit is taken
before `accept()`, so connection 2 never leaves the kernel backlog while cap 1 is held — the
negative assertion is a consequence of the code, not a timing race. It fails in 0.01 s at cap 8,
so the 2 s window has ~200x margin; a slow machine makes it pass, not fail; `drop(holding)` →
EOF mid-head → hyper ends → `_slot` drops, and the follow-up read blocks up to `PATIENCE`, so
there is no window. `peak_virtual_kb` catches even an untouched `Vec::with_capacity` reservation
(`VmPeak grew 3906252 kB`). `delivered()` includes the retained bytes (pinning the write
deadline to 3600 s fails with `got 8388721 of 8388608`). No new test depends on hyper flushing
head separately from body.

### Blocking

- `tests/binary.rs:1030-1037` — **the trickle test is still vacuous, and it passes having sent
  zero body bytes.** Replacing the loop condition with `if false` so no `x` is ever sent →
  **passes, 3.22 s**. `read_body`'s outer `timeout` fires at 1 s on a body that never arrives, so
  a body that merely *stops* earns the same 408 as one that keeps trickling — the exact
  distinction the docstring says the test exists to draw. Round 3's rewrite changed the sending,
  not what is asserted. Fix: count what landed and assert it,
  `assert!(landed >= 4, "the trickle never reached the read timeout, {landed} bytes landed")`.
- `serve.rs:192` with the doc at `:169-183` — **the new `PermissionDenied` clause asserts
  something false.** The doc says every kind in the set "is dequeued with the connection that
  carried it, so none can spin this loop". In `do_accept()`, `security_socket_accept()` runs
  *before* `sock->ops->accept()`, so an SELinux/AppArmor denial returns `EPERM` with the
  connection still queued: the next iteration hits the same connection, and the loop spins at
  full CPU emitting one WARNING per pass. The seccomp half of the clause is correct (no
  `SystemCallErrorNumber` in `nix/unit.nix`, so the default is SIGSYS kill), and the firewall
  justification is weak for TCP anyway — netfilter drops the SYN, so nothing is ever pending.
  Fix: drop `PermissionDenied` from the set. An LSM refusing `accept(2)` is host policy, not one
  client, and it belongs on the exit path with descriptor exhaustion — which also makes the
  kernel-ordering question moot rather than something the comment has to be right about.
- `.beads` — metsuke-a3a's resolution comment names
  `a_body_that_trickles_is_cut_off_at_the_read_timeout`, renamed this round to
  `a_body_that_keeps_trickling_…`. A dead reference in the record that closes the criterion.
  Amend the comment.

### Decision — the length refusal, and my part in it

`archive.rs:327-337` with `s3.rs:289-293`. I recommended "always set `Content-Length`, buffer or
refuse a length-less object", and called the length-less path theoretical because S3 sends a
length for every GetObject. That premise was AWS-only, and `endpoint` is an arbitrary URL. What I
missed:

- ureq returns `None` for chunked, close-delimited and no-body responses (`body/mod.rs:195-206`).
  Decompression is correctly ruled out — `default-features = false, features = ["rustls"]`, and
  no `flate2`/`brotli-decompressor` in `Cargo.lock` — so there is no false positive there.
- **The repo's own S3 double chunks by default.** `tiny_http` picks chunked whenever
  `entity_length >= chunked_threshold`, default 32768 (`response.rs:177, 246`), and its docstring
  notes chunked is mutually exclusive with `Content-Length`. `tests/s3.rs:53` uses bare
  `Response::from_data`. So the S3 download tests pass only because their fixtures are under
  32 KiB, and the next person adding a realistic fixture gets a confusing 503 from
  `an_object_downloads_as_the_bytes_that_were_put`.
- No test asserts the new refusal; `"declared no length"` appears only at `s3.rs:293`.

Two ways out, and this is yours to pick. **(O1)** Keep the refusal, document the endpoint
requirement where an operator sets `endpoint`, and add the test the double makes easy:
`Response::from_data(body).with_chunked_threshold(0)`, asserting 503 with a body of exactly
"the archive cannot be read". **(O2)** Buffer to `AnswerBody::Bytes` under a new `[http]` limit
when the length is absent, which keeps non-AWS endpoints working. Recommendation: O1 — it is the
smaller change, the deployment target is AWS, and O2 adds a buffering path the ticket spent this
whole effort removing. Either way the refusal is behaviour the ticket never asked for
("streams the upstream body through rather than buffering" is satisfied by chunked too), so it
needs a bullet in `metsuke-jfb`'s `## Decisions so far`, the way jfb.4 and jfb.5 recorded theirs.

Related, and independent of which option you take: `s3.rs:293` reuses `ArchiveError::Fetch`,
meaning "this key could not be read", for an endpoint-conformance fault that is per-archive and
permanent. It reaches the client as a 503, which says "retry" about a condition every retry
reproduces. A distinct variant (`EndpointUnusable { endpoint, reason }`) gives the log an honest
name. The refusal itself is loud, correctly not `NoSuchObject`, and leaks neither endpoint nor
bucket — `refuse_withholding` keeps the detail in the log.

### Tests, non-blocking

- `tests/binary.rs:879-891` — `until_blank_line` returns `None` on `Ok(0) | Err(_)`, so a clean
  EOF and every socket error collapse into the value its own doc calls "`budget` passed with no
  head arriving". The concurrency test survives only because its follow-up `answer_head` panics
  on a closed connection; the contract is still wrong for the next caller. Fix: `None` only for
  `WouldBlock`/`TimedOut`, panic otherwise naming the error.
- `tests/binary.rs:965` — `delivered` discards `read_to_close`'s bool, and its doc claims exactly
  the distinction that bool carries ("a server still holding the connection open runs into the
  budget instead"). Return `(closed, len)` and assert `closed`.
- `tests/binary.rs:1039-1041` — "Answered while the trickle is still open" is false: the loop
  exits only on a failed write, which needs the server to have closed already. Measured 1.62 s,
  so the 408 landed at t≈1 s and the `post` runs against a dead connection. Drop the claim, or
  spawn the `post` from a thread started before the loop.
- `tests/binary.rs:1123` — `a_download_left_unread_stalls_no_upload` runs at cap 64, so it proves
  nothing about the object being streamed, which its docstring claims; `tests/http.rs` is where
  that is tested.
- `tests/binary.rs:98` — the `expect` still says "a live process reports VmSize" under a helper
  that parses `VmPeak`.

### Standards

- `tests/binary.rs:956-958` — `closed_within` is a rename-only wrapper around `read_to_close`,
  same signature, one call site, with a doc restating it. Delete it, or rename `read_to_close`.
  Otherwise `Raw` is coherent: primitives, projections of the retained buffer, and I/O, with each
  projection answering a distinct caller need.
- `http.rs:176-181` — `AnswerBody::as_bytes` has no production caller; `tests/http.rs:113` is the
  only user, and `:331` already matches `AnswerBody::Stream` directly. Match `Bytes` in the test
  helper and delete the method.
- `ObjectStream.length: u64` as a type choice is right and I am not reopening it: `Option<u64>`
  keeps a chunked branch alive in `respond`, and a chunked answer puts `DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES` on
  the wire as an observable frame size. The two representations are not equally simple.

### Prose

- `CLAUDE.md:9` — round 3 removed the only exception the amended clause existed to carve out, and
  `DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES` is now its sole client and states the distinction itself. Revert to the
  one-line rule.
- Three *why*s still in more than one place: per-read renewal — `config.rs:36-38` (owner),
  `tests/binary.rs:1014-1017`, `:1030`; the chunked-body bounded read — `serve.rs:322-324`
  (owner), `serve.rs:285-286`, `tests/binary.rs:1046-1047`; every-download-declares-a-length —
  `archive.rs:327-330` (owner), `serve.rs:31-33`, `serve.rs:366-368`.
- `serve.rs:169-183` — thirteen lines defending one `matches!`, grown across rounds. Dropping
  `PermissionDenied` removes most of the argument; keep the pending-network sentence and the
  SIGSYS one, and name `ECONNABORTED`/`EINTR` rather than counting them.
- `serve.rs:257-258` — `takes_a_body`'s doc says what its two-line match says and repeats
  `handle`'s comment above it.
- `serve.rs:122` — `RestartSec` called "where a backoff already lives"; `nix/unit.nix:7` is a
  fixed `restartSecs = 30`, which is a delay, not a backoff.
- `tests/http.rs:312` — restates the test's own `AnswerBody::Stream` match; keep the
  metsuke-4zo.72 cite.

Round 3's prose fixes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 applied and left one owner. 6 not applied (per-read
renewal, above). No dead references beyond the two named.

### Beads hygiene

Map bullet present and decisions-only; a3a closed with a reason; `.beads/` staged. Two gaps: the
a3a comment's dead test name, and no bullet for the length refusal.

### Filed

Nothing new. metsuke-jfb.27 (instructions page copied per GET `/`) still open from round 2.

### Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`. Blocking: the trickle test's vacuity, `PermissionDenied`, and a3a's dead
test name. Then answer the length-refusal decision and record it on the map; the rest is cleanup.

## Review round 5: hyper replaces tiny_http (working tree, 22 files)

No untracked files; everything staged. **The production code is sound and all five acceptance
criteria hold** — `cargo test --workspace` 344 passed, clippy clean, verified independently. The
`EndpointUnusable` disclosure audit comes back clean: `error.to_string()` reaches
`unavailable`'s second argument, which `refuse_withholding` appends to the log only, so the
endpoint never enters a client-visible body (`http.rs:289-291, 344-365`). `one_connection` is now
the five kinds that are dequeued with their connection, `EPERM` takes the exit path, and the
permit is released on `continue`.

What does not converge is the **test suite**. A mutation pass — breaking the production code in a
scratch copy and checking the tests notice — found four defects that four rounds of reading
missed. Two of them are on claims the ticket is accountable for.

### Blocking

- `tests/binary.rs:1056-1060` — **the trickle test passes under the exact regression it names.**
  Mutation: replace the whole-body `timeout(read_timeout, bounded(..))` with a per-frame timeout
  inside the loop — the shape `config.rs:37-39` exists to rule out. **The test still passes**
  (`landed=8`, connection never cut, 408 fires once the trickle stops); the whole workspace stays
  green. Baseline is `landed=4, renewals=2`, and that margin is TCP RST-detection lag — a send at
  t≈1.2 s succeeds after the 1.0 s deadline — not renewal. `renewals` is also anti-derived: at
  `bound=4` it would exceed the loop's 8 attempts and the test could never pass. This is the
  fourth round on this test; the assertion still does not encode "the cut happened *during* the
  trickle". Fix: add `assert!(landed < attempts)` beside `landed > renewals`, and rename
  `renewals` to match the whole-body deadline it is actually about.
- `tests/binary.rs:1145` — **`a_download_left_unread_stalls_no_upload` proves nothing about
  per-connection tasks**, which is metsuke-4zo.73's whole claim. Mutation: replace
  `tokio::task::spawn(async move {…})` with an inline `.await`, so the server serves one
  connection at a time. **The test passes**, taking 10.04 s against a 0.03 s baseline — the upload
  simply waits out `write_timeout` and gets its 200. The full 36-test binary suite stays green.
  Fix: bound the latency — run `post` on a thread, `recv_timeout(2s)` on a channel, and fail if
  the upload did not answer well inside `write_timeout`. `tests/binary.rs:1040` has the same
  defect in the trickle test's `thread::scope` (`ingest.join()` has no deadline), so fix both.
- `tests/support/mod.rs:432` with `tests/s3.rs` — **the no-leak rule is unguarded.** Mutation:
  replace `unavailable("the archive cannot be read", &error.to_string())` with
  `refuse(None, 503, error.to_string())`, which puts the endpoint in the client's body. **No test
  breaks.** `impl Bytes for FailingArchive` is never exercised — nothing pulls `OBJECT_PATH`
  against `unreachable_archive()`, and the new S3 test asserts the error *value*, not an HTTP
  body. Given the rule at `http.rs:295-297` is the reason the variant carries the endpoint at all,
  it should have a test. Fix: mirror `a_listing_over_an_archive_that_will_not_answer_is_unavailable`
  for the download route, asserting 503 and that the body does not contain the endpoint.
- `tests/s3.rs:53` — **the chunking trap I flagged last round is still latent.** `Seen::as_object`
  sets no `with_chunked_threshold`, so tiny_http's 32 KiB default still governs. Mutation to
  `with_chunked_threshold(4)`, simulating an over-threshold fixture, fails
  `an_object_downloads_as_the_bytes_that_were_put` with `EndpointUnusable`. You added a test for
  the refusal, which is what I asked for, but the double is still one fixture-size change away
  from a confusing failure. Fix: `.with_chunked_threshold(usize::MAX)` at line 53 — one line, and
  the trap is gone rather than named.

### Non-blocking

- `tests/binary.rs:964` — `read_to_close`'s `Err(_) => return false` folds every read error into
  "still open", including `ConnectionReset`, which is a close. Round 4 added `assert!(closed)` at
  both call sites, which makes the collapse consequential: when `WriteDeadline` fires, hyper drops
  the `TcpStream` with unsent data queued, and Linux sends RST. I ran
  `a_download_nobody_reads_is_cut_off_at_the_write_timeout` 8 times and it passed 8 times, so this
  is latent here rather than an observed flake. The argument is the inconsistency:
  `until_blank_line` got the explicit match this round and this helper did not. Fix: `WouldBlock |
  TimedOut => false`, `ConnectionReset | BrokenPipe => true`, `_ => panic!` naming the error.
- `archive.rs:245` — `EndpointUnusable { endpoint, reason }`: `reason` has exactly one inhabitant
  across its single construction site, so the `String` carries what the variant already means.
  Fix: `#[error("{endpoint} answered a GET with no Content-Length")] EndpointUnusable { endpoint:
  String }`; `tests/s3.rs:665` still passes.
- `tests/binary.rs:853-867` — `send` reduces a write failure to a bool via `try_send`, so its
  panic names no cause. The swallow is justified for the trickle, where a close mid-write is the
  outcome under test, but not for `send`. Return `io::Result<()>` and let the trickle call
  `.is_ok()` at its own site.

### Prose

- The length-refusal *why* is now in four artifacts: `archive.rs:333-336` (owner — chunked would
  put copy granularity on the wire), retold at `s3.rs:289-292`, `config.rs:114-118`, and
  `contrib/server.example.toml:22-23`. Keep the mechanism in `archive.rs`; `s3.rs` points;
  `config.rs` and the example keep only the operator requirement.
- `archive.rs:239-243` — five lines on one variant, and "The client is told 503 either way"
  restates `http.rs`'s status mapping. Shortest honest version: "Not `Fetch`: no key can be read
  off this endpoint and no retry changes that. Both answer 503, so this exists for the operator's
  log line." `tests/s3.rs:651-652` restates the same distinction — cut it, the `matches!` is the
  claim.
- `tests/support/mod.rs:196` — "The timeouts are the suite's patience" is false: `PATIENCE` is
  30 s and these are 10 s. Fix: "Bounded rather than unlimited, so a regression fails a test
  rather than hanging it."
- Neither `config.rs:114-118` nor the example TOML says **chunked**, the word a MinIO/Ceph/Garage
  operator would search for; it appears only in `s3.rs`'s comment. One clause on the example line.

Round 4's prose items 1-7 all landed. Every path and symbol resolves; no residual mention of
`closed_within` or `AnswerBody::as_bytes`; no tiny_http digit written into prose.

### Beads

The map's new length-refusal bullet is glued to the previous one — the text reads
`…exits to systemd (jfb.6).- A download states…`. Insert a newline. a3a's superseded comment
naming `a_body_that_trickles_…` is fine: comments are append-only and the correction names the
live tests. jfb.27 open and genuinely unfixed (`http.rs:190` still `page.as_bytes().to_vec()`).

### Verified sound, by mutation

Named so you know what is actually guarded: `try_send`→false fails the trickle; `bound=30` fails
it; `Semaphore::new(1024)` fails the concurrency test; `header_read_timeout(3600s)` fails the idle
test; `WriteDeadline(3600s)` fails the write-timeout test; `content_length().unwrap_or(0)` fails
the new S3 test; preallocating the declared length fails the 4 GB test with `VmPeak grew 3906252
kB`. `until_blank_line` panics on `Ok(0)` and on other errors, so the concurrency test's negative
assertion cannot be met by a dead server. Both `delivered` call sites assert `closed`. Deleting
`AnswerBody::as_bytes` and `closed_within` lost no assertion.

### Filed

Nothing new.

### Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`, and the reason is narrower than last round: the code is right, four tests
do not guard what they claim. Blocking: the trickle test's per-read mutation, the
stalls-no-upload latency bound, a download test for the no-leak rule, and pinning the S3 double's
chunk threshold. Everything else here is cleanup.
